chapters.title: Chapter 2051: You did very well indeed.
paragraphs: "Chaos...?"
Sharnoth blinked in surprise.
"Yes, but not as the world defines it.
Chaos is not destruction, madness, or sin.
Chaos is the raw breath of all things.
The spark before creation.
The will to defy all written fate.
You were born with the Fate that tried to tame you.
But you are not who you were supposed to be anymore.
You now walk on your own Path,
A Path of Freedom."
Zylarith’s hand hovered above the Seed.
"Eat this and everything will be unmade.
Your Energy, your Soul, your very Foundation will be torn apart.
You will begin again—not as a creature of Darkness, but as a Daughter of Chaos."
Sharnoth’s heart shuddered at those words, her fingers trembled.

She thought of her mother’s face, the chains that bound her, the cage of Radiance, the nights she bled, the mornings she was unable to scream. She thought of the Herald of Justice who smirked at her, the laughing guards and—
She thought of the promise she made—not with her lips, but with her very being.
Her Revenge.
The Princess clenched her fists, the trembling stopped.
She took a breath.
Then, slowly... she reached out.

Her fingers closed around the Seed of Uncreation—and the moment she touched it, her skin blistered, not from heat or cold, but from the sheer absence it carried. It wasn’t poison. It wasn’t power. It was the undoing of meaning itself.
Her body shook, blood leaked from her eyes, it was painful, but the little girl was so used to pain by now that it didn’t matter.
She just tightened her hold around the seed and,
She ate it.
The Seed slid down her throat and the moment it reached her core—
BOOOM
The very reality shook.
A scream—her scream—split through the world, but no sound came out, or maybe the world just couldn’t comprehend that scream and put a voice to it.
Sharnoth’s Energy circuits collapsed, her soul and her body, everything was restructured. The little girl continued to scream silently.
Even the strongest Beasts in the World trembled without knowing or understanding why. The entire process lasted six months,
And finally,
The Princess was reborn, purple-black energy surrounding her body, her crimson eyes shining brightly.
Zylarith, who saw this scene, smiled.
"You are finally free, child."
After this, Sharnoth’s training began.
Zylarith became her teacher.
He didn’t teach her any Spells, Sword Skills, or any other Powers.
He only taught her one thing,
Chaos.
The very meaning behind Chaos.
"Chaos is not a weapon. It is a truth.
Spells rot. Techniques fade.
But Truth... truth remains."
"What is Chaos?"
He asked her each day.
And every time she answered, he shook his head.
"Freedom?"
"No. That is a consequence."
"Destruction?"
"No. That is a byproduct."
"Creation?"
"Only if you see what was never meant to be."
"Then... what?"
"That is for you to find out."
This continued for centuries. Sharnoth didn’t have to cultivate like others. No, her body was scarily adaptable with the Power of Chaos, so much that the Chaos inside her grew on its own.
It was almost as if she was born to carry the Energy of Chaos in her.
Even Zylarith, who had expected her to be talented, was taken by surprise at how quickly her body was adapting to it.
If the girl was born in Chaosveil, the entirety of Chaosveil would be beneath her steps, she would have been below one and above the rest.
She was... perfect.
Zylarith’s eyes shined as he continued to focus on the training.
"All things in creation are told what they are allowed to be.
A flame must burn.
A river must flow.
A child must obey.
That is Order.
But you, Shar, must become something that even the universe cannot define."
As the Princess continued to grow stronger, her training became much and much different.

She was made to walk into storms that should have shredded her into pieces, she was made to live in a dream-realm where time flowed backwards, she was even made to die—again and again—not physically, but in meaning.
She was made to experience what made no sense.
All for a single purpose,
To comprehend the incomprehensible.
To comprehend... Chaos.
"The world worships Balance. Light and Dark. Good and Evil. Cause and Effect.
But Balance is just Control with a prettier face.
The true path of Chaos is not about tipping the scales, it is about breaking them, tearing down the courtroom, and laughing as the judge begs for mercy.
That is Chaos.
When you no longer need to belong, when others are unable to justify your existence,
That is the sign that you are ready."
As those words echoed through the world Sharnoth and Zylarith were in, something finally happened.
BOOOOM
Sharnoth’s Aura exploded as she broke through and became a Sovereign,
A Sovereign with a Law.
Law of Absolute Chaos.
And...
It wasn’t just Sharnoth that formed this Law.
Nux, who was watching all these memories carefully, was the same.
Yes, understanding Sharnoth’s Comprehension and mixing it with his own, allowed him to form the same Law.
He now finally had complete access to the Energy of Chaos he so desperately wanted,
But suddenly—
Nux noticed something strange in his Law.
He narrowed his eyes, examining what was wrong and soon, his expression turned solemn. Soon however—
’So you finally showed your true face, huh.
I was wondering when it would happen.’
He just laughed, staring at Zylarith, who was still looking at Sharnoth with a light, elderly smile on his face.
A smile that made Nux sick.
For now, however, he focused back on the memories he was seeing.
After all, what he saw was enough for him to understand that this wasn’t over.
He just wanted to see when Sharnoth will realize it,
Or...
If she ever will.
"Master."
Sharnoth knelt and bowed her head, her face was expressionless, but both Nux and Zylarith knew what she wanted.
Her Master’s appreciation.
"You did well."
Zylarith nodded.
"You did very well indeed."
His smile widened.

chapters.title: Chapter 2052: He wasn’t overpowered, he was outsmarted.
paragraphs: Once Sharnoth broke through and became a Sovereign, Zylarith no longer had to play an active role as her Master.
His aim was to change Sharnoth’s Core and help her be reborn as a being of Chaos. With Sharnoth forming the Law of Absolute Chaos, that goal was achieved.
Clearly, Sharnoth now understood Chaos—enough to form an Absolute Law at that. Even in Chaosveil at its prime, her Law would be counted as one of the strongest. But from here on out,
Sharnoth didn’t need to understand Chaos—she needed to understand her Law.
And that was the path she had to walk on her own.
The second part of her growth began; it was time for the sheltered bird that Zylarith protected all these years to fly on her own.

Zylarith took away all the Relics he had given to her. The little girl was now alone in the dead world, full of dangerous beasts. The cloak that she had been using all this while to hide from them was no longer with her.
She had to live on her own. She had to set up her own camp, she had to keep watch on her own, she had to scour for her own food, and... she had to fight her own battles.
Since this was the first time the little girl was actually going to face real threats, Zylarith stayed with her for the first few times. Soon, however, the old soul realized something.
Sharnoth wasn’t normal.
It wasn’t just her body being suitable to cultivate Chaos energy—she herself was a monster far beyond anything he could imagine.

Within a few battles, she got the hang of it. Because her understanding of Chaos was so high, and Chaos itself was such a strong energy, she quickly realized how to use this dangerous energy to deal with her opponents.
In just a few years, she had already started creating techniques that surprised even Zylarith—techniques that would have caused a commotion if they were ever released in the Chaosveil market.

It didn’t take long for her to start fighting multiple opponents at the same time. Even the beasts at the Primordial Level—while Sharnoth couldn’t defeat them, she could still get away from them by messing with their senses.

As the battles she fought became harder and harder, her understanding of her Law became deeper and deeper. Adding to that the fact that Chaos flowed in her body like it was its home, this allowed her to advance at a rate that was almost as quick as Zylarith’s himself.
Zylarith even decided to leave the girl alone in this world. Without his presence, if something unexpected happened, Sharnoth would die. But the girl did not show fear.
Rather, she looked forward to the challenge.
So for the first time in her life, the girl was alone in a world full of mindless enemies.
And in this world, despite not being the strongest, she was the devil incarnate. She hunted day and night, fighting numerous beasts that no being at her level should be fighting.
There were times she won, there were times when she was defeated, but never once did she give up.
Even when she was gravely injured, she never backed down from a fight and unleashed hell on the poor beasts that encountered her.
By the time Zylarith returned, she had turned into a monster in her own right. Within just five thousand years, she had reached the level of Transcendent—Peak Transcendent.
With the strongest beasts in this world being at the Transcendent Level as well, it wasn’t even a fair battle any longer.
Sharnoth had become an Apex Predator—a being who made these mindless beasts tremble in fear just at the sight of her.

She no longer needed to hunt for food; the mindless beasts brought food to her themselves. Not just that, they guarded her from possible enemies; they used their abilities to set up a camp for her. Yes, Sharnoth had started to rule them as their Queen.
And when Zylarith saw this, although surprised, he nodded to himself,
“It is time.”
He muttered.
“What?”
Sharnoth questioned. Now that she had grown up, she looked like an exact copy of her mother. Zylarith stared at her face and,
“To leave this place.”
“Huh?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“You were not planning on staying here for the rest of your life, were you? Or have you perhaps gotten too comfortable here and already forgot why you accepted my help in the first place?”
Zylarith questioned. His words, however, instantly got a reaction out of Sharnoth,
“I am still not strong enough.”

She remembered how strong the Herald of Justice was. She was strong, yes, and even though she had come up with a few techniques that might work against that being, in the end, there was a difference of an entire Phase between them.

An Absolute Difference that she wouldn’t be able to overcome no matter what. The only option was to break through and become an Eternal herself—only then would facing that heinous bastard be possible.
“Obviously, you aren’t strong enough to face him yet.”
Zylarith, however, snorted at her words.
“You think I am telling you to go to him right now?”
Sharnoth stared at her master with a frown.
“You think defeating him would be possible even if you became stronger than him?”
“Is that not...”
Sharnoth couldn’t understand.
Wasn’t that how the Universe worked?
She would obviously be able to defeat him when she was stronger than him, no?
“Don’t be a fool.
The Universe isn’t a jungle with just mindless beasts roaming around. While strength is important, it isn’t the sole factor that decides the outcome of a War.
If that was the case, you think your Father would have lost?”
“My Father didn’t lose; he was ambushed and outnum—”
The Princess was quick to defend her Father’s honor, but,
“His World fell, he is dead, his wife is dead, and his daughter is on the run.
He lost.”
Zylarith declared coldly.
“And he didn’t lose because he wasn’t strong enough—no, he was plenty strong. He lost because he lost the Battle of Interest.”
“Battle of Interest?”
“Gathering subordinates, creating a Faction, finding allies, and using those allies to your benefit—
This was the battle he lost. This was the reason he was ambushed and outnumbered.
He wasn’t overpowered.
He was outsmarted.
And now, it is time to make sure the same doesn’t happen to you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 2053: The Queen of those who Lost.
paragraphs: "Your father wasn’t overpowered, he was outsmarted.
And now, it is time to make sure the same doesn’t happen to you."
Zylarith declared, and Sharnoth stared at him with a determined look on her face and,
"How... do we do that?"
She questioned, prepared to go through any form of training no matter how harsh.
"We will be continuing as we have done till now, practical experience."
Zylarith answered, making the Princess frown. Seeing her expression, a light smile appeared on Zylarith’s face,
"It is now time to create your own Kingdom."
"My... Kingdom?"
"Mhm, we will now roam around the Universe and find people worthy of being your subordinates. You will gather them, train them under you, and raise them as your men.
You will give them food, shelter, protection, and power.
This will be your first step into the Battle of Interests.
You will create a force that no one in this Universe will be able to look down upon."
Sharnoth’s eyes flickered with intense emotions as she heard those words. Soon, however, those emotions dimmed down and she lowered her head,
"Everyone who might have followed me no longer exists in the Universe."
She spoke in a low voice. Zylarith, however, didn’t care.
"And?"
He questioned, making Sharnoth frown.
"Are you going to give up because the people you once knew are dead?"
The Princess turned silent.
She couldn’t give up, there was no way she would.

"You will find new people, and not just anyone. You need people with strong potential. These will be the people who will follow you; their very presence will represent you. Mediocrity isn’t allowed. You will only accept the best of the best."
Zylarith spoke as he clenched his fists, his eyes looked like they were prepared to capture the world.
"...Why would such people follow me when they don’t even know me?"
Sharnoth questioned again.
"That is up to you, isn’t it?"
Zylarith just shrugged. He then looked into his disciple’s eyes and,

"If they do not know you, just make them know you. Show them that following you is what’s best for them. Make them rely on you. Make it so they become so reliant on you that instead of you recruiting them,
They submit to you on their own, willingly."
"Can I do that...?"
"Do you think you have any other option?"
Zylarith questioned back and once again, Sharnoth’s eyes changed. Her Master was correct, it wasn’t a question of whether she could do it or not—she had no other choice but to do it.
"Where do I find these people?"
The Princess questioned, her crimson eyes shining with a different light than before.
"That, you can leave to me."
Zylarith grinned.
And with that, Sharnoth Nocthys left the world she had hidden in and took her first step back into the Universe.
She had access to Zylarith’s storage and all the magical items he had. For her, travelling through the Universe at an absurdly high speed wasn’t difficult.
Zylarith too, took her to various places to gather more followers. As Zylarith said, these people would in future represent Sharnoth—their potential had to be strong.
So Zylarith came with a condition.
These people could only belong to a High Level World.
"Why not the people from Supreme Worlds, wouldn’t they be stronger?"

Sharnoth questioned with a frown, and at that question, Zylarith momentarily paused. He soon realized that he was essentially dealing with just an eleven-year-old. Yes, she was older, but her knowledge about the Universe was comparable to that of an eleven-year-old.
She knew almost nothing about the Universe, and this made him sigh. To think he would need to teach her the basics as well.

The Old Soul sighed again, and in the end, Sharnoth’s lecture began. He told her about the Supreme Worlds, their Factions, and other Lower Level Worlds. He explained the Universal System, the Rules they had to follow, and many more things.
It took months before Sharnoth’s understanding of things came to an acceptable level and after that...
"What about you, Master?"
Sharnoth questioned.
Her master’s very existence confused her. His Cultivation was unfathomable, he had helped her escape from a High Level World—a task that should have been impossible for any normal being—and yet...
Her Master did it without any difficulty.
There was no way he was a normal being. Even Eternals weren’t as resourceful as he was.

Zylarith became silent at that question. Soon, however, he decided to reveal the truth. He talked about the Fifth and the strongest Supreme World, the Power of Chaos that they used, and how they fell. He revealed his background, his history, and his current situation—everything.
Nux, who was hearing everything, couldn’t help but notice how scarily similar the story was word for word, almost as if this man had practiced it.
Even his end goal was similar; he wanted Sharnoth to take over the Will of the Universe. The only thing he did not tell her about was the Law of Absolute Growth that Nux had.
Sharnoth didn’t question him either. Hearing her master’s background, she nodded with a solemn look on her face and swore that she would revive him the moment she takes over the Universe.
For now, however, she had to focus on what’s in front of her. With the basics fed into her mind, Sharnoth once again focused on gathering followers.
Since the condition was to only gather beings from High Level Worlds, Sharnoth believed it would take a long while to find such people.
After all, no one from a strong, well-known High Level World would willingly follow her—there was no reason to.
She could only target...
"The Fallen High Level Worlds."
Zylarith smiled.
"The Fallen High Level Worlds...?"
Sharnoth tilted her head in confusion, and Zylarith nodded.
"Nocthys isn’t the only High Level World that lost a war. There are hundreds of such worlds, and obviously, survivors of those worlds exist to this day."
Zylarith then glanced at Sharnoth and,
"You will recruit those survivors and take them under your banner.
You will become the Queen of those who Lost."

Zylarith answered, making the Princess frown.
Seeing her expression, a light smile appeared on Zylarith’s face,
"It is now time to create your own Kingdom."
Kingdom?"
"Mhm, we will now roam around the Universe and find people worthy of being your subordinates.
You will gather them, train them under you, and raise them as your men.
You will give them food, shelter, protection, and power.
This will be your first step into the Battle of Interests.
You will create a force that no one in this Universe will be able to look down upon."
Sharnoth’s eyes flickered with intense emotions as she heard those words.
Soon, however, those emotions dimmed down and she lowered her head,
"Everyone who might have followed me no longer exists in the Universe."
She spoke in a low voice.
Zylarith, however, didn’t care.
"And?"
He questioned, making Sharnoth frown.
"Are you going to give up because the people you once knew are dead?"
The Princess turned silent.
She couldn’t give up, there was no way she would.
"You will find new people, and not just anyone.
You need people with strong potential.
These will be the people who will follow you; their very presence will represent you.
Mediocrity isn’t allowed.
You will only accept the best of the best."
Zylarith spoke as he clenched his fists, his eyes looked like they were prepared to capture the world.
"...Why would such people follow me when they don’t even know me?"
Sharnoth questioned again.
"That is up to you, isn’t it?"
Zylarith just shrugged.
He then looked into his disciple’s eyes and,
"If they do not know you, just make them know you.
Show them that following you is what’s best for them.
Make them rely on you.
Make it so they become so reliant on you that instead of you recruiting them,
They submit to you on their own, willingly."
"Can I do that...?"
"Do you think you have any other option?"
Zylarith questioned back and once again, Sharnoth’s eyes changed.
Her Master was correct, it wasn’t a question of whether she could do it or not—she had no other choice but to do it.
"Where do I find these people?"
The Princess questioned, her crimson eyes shining with a different light than before.
"That, you can leave to me."
Zylarith grinned.
And with that, Sharnoth Nocthys left the world she had hidden in and took her first step back into the Universe.
She had access to Zylarith’s storage and all the magical items he had.
For her, travelling through the Universe at an absurdly high speed wasn’t difficult.
Zylarith too, took her to various places to gather more followers.
As Zylarith said, these people would in future represent Sharnoth—their potential had to be strong.
So Zylarith came with a condition.
These people could only belong to a High Level World.
"Why not the people from Supreme Worlds, wouldn’t they be stronger?"
Sharnoth questioned with a frown, and at that question, Zylarith momentarily paused.
He soon realized that he was essentially dealing with just an eleven-year-old.
Yes, she was older, but her knowledge about the Universe was comparable to that of an eleven-year-old.
She knew almost nothing about the Universe, and this made him sigh.
To think he would need to teach her the basics as well.
The Old Soul sighed again, and in the end, Sharnoth’s lecture began.
He told her about the Supreme Worlds, their Factions, and other Lower Level Worlds.
He explained the Universal System, the Rules they had to follow, and many more things.
It took months before Sharnoth’s understanding of things came to an acceptable level and after that...
"What about you, Master?"
Sharnoth questioned.
Her master’s very existence confused her.
His Cultivation was unfathomable, he had helped her escape from a High Level World—a task that should have been impossible for any normal being—and yet...
Her Master did it without any difficulty.
There was no way he was a normal being.
Even Eternals weren’t as resourceful as he was.
Zylarith became silent at that question.
Soon, however, he decided to reveal the truth.
He talked about the Fifth and the strongest Supreme World, the Power of Chaos that they used, and how they fell.
He revealed his background, his history, and his current situation—everything.
Nux, who was hearing everything, couldn’t help but notice how scarily similar the story was word for word, almost as if this man had practiced it.
Even his end goal was similar; he wanted Sharnoth to take over the Will of the Universe.
The only thing he did not tell her about was the Law of Absolute Growth that Nux had.
Sharnoth didn’t question him either.
Hearing her master’s background, she nodded with a solemn look on her face and swore that she would revive him the moment she takes over the Universe.
For now, however, she had to focus on what’s in front of her.
With the basics fed into her mind, Sharnoth once again focused on gathering followers.
Since the condition was to only gather beings from High Level Worlds, Sharnoth believed it would take a long while to find such people.
After all, no one from a strong, well-known High Level World would willingly follow her—there was no reason to.
She could only target...
"The Fallen High Level Worlds."
Zylarith smiled.
"The Fallen High Level Worlds...?"
Sharnoth tilted her head in confusion, and Zylarith nodded.
"Nocthys isn’t the only High Level World that lost a war.
There are hundreds of such worlds, and obviously, survivors of those worlds exist to this day."
Zylarith then glanced at Sharnoth and,
"You will recruit those survivors and take them under your banner.
You will become the Queen of those who Lost."

chapters.title: Chapter 2054: You will Fall again.
paragraphs: "You will recruit those survivors and take them under your banner.
You will become the Queen of those who Lost."
With those words, Sharnoth’s new journey started.
She thought it would be difficult to find such people. After all, survivors of a destroyed world must be some runaways trying to hide from the Universe. How was she supposed to find them?
This problem, however, was solved by Zylarith and her combined efforts. With numerous artifacts and relics in Zylarith’s possession, finding them wasn’t difficult, the problem was the recruitment.
These people were highly paranoid and had no reason to join a completely unknown being. Sharnoth had to prove herself time and time again, and in the process, she made quite a lot of mistakes.

After all, till now, she only had the experience in leading the mindless beasts—beasts she could dominate and subdue with her strength. The same, however, couldn’t be said for intelligent beings. While strength still mattered a lot, it wasn’t the only thing needed to rule them.
Of course, with Zylarith as her guide and constant failures that further strengthened his words, Sharnoth learned quickly.
"You are powerful, much more powerful than other Transcendents around you. You are powerful enough for people to want to follow you. Now, you just need to show it to them."
Zylarith lectured.
"Show it to them?"
Sharnoth tilted her head in confusion.
"Indeed.
These are called Visible Pillars of being a Leader.
Competence, Unshakable Conviction, Decisiveness, Charisma, and Vision.

Show them your power, show them how competent you are. This is what will attract their attention. Of course, this is only the first step. Attracting attention and making them follow you are two different matters.
Once you have shown them your competence, it is now time to show them your conviction—a cause that you believe in.
In your case, you are to become the Queen of those who Lost. You will become the guide who will lead them back to their glory days. Under your banner, they will raise their heads with pride again.
Have a relentless will, the kind that outlasts exhaustion, defeat, and betrayal. Make it so they follow because you are still standing.
Learn to be a storyteller—the ability to reframe suffering as ’sacrifice’ and failure as ’a lesson.’ People endure pain if it has meaning.
Have an aura of inevitability around you. Make the people believe that your victory is fated, inevitable.
Make them have blind faith in you. Make them rely on you. Make it so they can never imagine a future without you, so much so that they are even willing to give their lives for you.
That is how you make people follow you."
Zylarith explained.

Of course, the process was slow. This wasn’t something one could learn through theory alone—real experience was needed. Sharnoth needed to understand people in general, then have an instinctive understanding of those around her in particular. There were several other factors that just couldn’t be put into words.
She started small.

It began with taking over a High-Level Mercenary Party with fourteen mercenaries. She led them with strength and resourcefulness, making them believe her. There were times she faltered—times she abandoned her people and had to start from nothing once more.
Centuries passed just like that, and Sharnoth began getting the hang of things. As people under her command grew, she learned more.

Zylarith too started finding more and more people that met the criteria of becoming Sharnoth’s followers. The numbers continued to increase. Nux, who was watching everything, also recognized a few people Sharnoth had gathered—few that were still with her when she became the Queen.
Sharnoth’s influence began to grow. Nux, however, wasn’t particularly interested in these developments. He was more focused on the time Sharnoth spent in strengthening her Law.
However, one interaction in particular attracted his attention.

It was the time when Sharnoth had already broken through and become an Eternal. Her command over the hundred thousand beings who followed her was absolute. And mind you, all hundred thousand of these beings were once a part of High-Level Worlds—their bloodline and potential were strong.
Her army could easily be compared to other High-Level Worlds. No, actually, they had an edge because of how diverse her people were.
At this point, Sharnoth’s fame had grown to a considerable degree. Even her story had become popular.
People had begun calling her the Princess who rose from Chains, and the title attracted a lot of attention.
More and more people came to her, wanting to be recruited.
Yes, she no longer needed to go around recruiting people, everything happened on its own now.
However,
This time, she faced an issue with a race called Verani.
The Verani were an ancient, enigmatic race with silver-white eyes and translucent, glass-like skin that faintly glows under stress.

They weren’t particularly strong. In fact, these people were weak compared to other beings from High-Level Worlds. Even amongst Sharnoth’s followers, there were quite a few who could defeat the strongest Verani.
This was also the reason the Veranis fell—they were simply too weak and became an easy target in this world.
But even then, Sharnoth wanted them because of how useful they were.

The Veranis possessed an instinctive sense of what "shouldn’t" be happening. They could not see the future or read minds, but they could feel when something was wrong—even if it defied logic or was undetectable by normal senses.

This was called True Intuition, and while their intuition wasn’t correct every time and had no real authenticity, it could still be relied upon. At the very least, the Veranis could be used as advisors.
But when Sharnoth went to them, the current Verani leader, Vehrian Rahkul, he refused to follow her.
"Why?"
Sharnoth questioned.

"You should know that your people are weak. If things continue like this, you will be targeted again and might even face annihilation. I will give you protection in exchange for your services. Your people will have a safe place to live and thrive. Is that not what you desire?"
"It is indeed what I desire."
Vehrian nodded.
He then stared at Sharnoth and,
"But when I look at you, I only see inevitable destruction."
"Destruction...?"
"The forces that you are aligned with are not your true allies."
At those words, Sharnoth frowned. For the first time in centuries, she felt something foreign stir in her—doubt.
And as if to put the final nail,
"Princess who rose from Chains,
You will Fall again."

chapters.title: Chapter 2055: Champions.
paragraphs: "Princess who rose from Chains,
You will fall again."
Vehrian spoke in a calm, almost unsettling voice.
’Oh?’
Nux, who saw what happened, raised his eyebrow, his interest finally piqued.
’Verani, huh...’
He muttered to himself.
When he first heard about the race, he didn’t particularly care. It was a fallen race and honestly, there were thousands of races just like them.
After coming this far, Nux had become indifferent to such things. Now, however, his thoughts were different.
’I need to get one of them for myself.’
He decided, his eyes shining with a flicker as he planned to find them. Of course, for now, he focused on the ongoing conversation. He was interested to see how Sharnoth would react to this.
’Would she finally notice?’
He wondered in his head.

At Vehrian’s words, Sharnoth’s face turned grim. She wasn’t angry. By now, she had strong control over her emotions. She could sense that Vehrian wasn’t trying to threaten or warn her; he simply stated what he felt.
"Why do you say that...?"
Sharnoth questioned. Vehrian, however, shook his head.
"I apologize, Lady Sharnoth. I have no reasoning behind my words. It was just my intuit—"
"Intuition is not an omniscient magic... it stems from something."
Before Vehrian could complete his words, Sharnoth interrupted.
"Intuition is the result of accumulated experience and subconscious pattern recognition. It emerges from familiarity—whether conscious or not.
If the mind has no prior exposure to a pattern, situation, or principle, it cannot intuitively respond to it.
If your intuition says that I am bound to fall, there must be a sort of conscious or unconscious reasoning to it. Explain that reasoning to me."
She ordered, making Vehrian smile wryly.
"Lady Sharnoth, please forgive me. Even if you are correct, it will be difficult for me to put this into wo—"
"Do this one thing for me and I will spare your life for daring to reject me."
Sharnoth ordered arrogantly.
Yes, it was ruthless, unreasonable even, but she had no other choice. The doubt that she was sensing—she wanted to ease it.
Anything that came between her and her goal, she had to destroy it, no matter what it took.
Vehrian stared at the woman in front of him in silence. Once again, his intuition told him that giving in was the only choice he had, and he believed it.
He closed his eyes for a moment, trying to collect his thoughts. Sharnoth waited patiently, giving him the time he needed.
Yes, she had now learned to make good use of people around her—follower or not.
"...You are what I would like to call a Champion."
Vehrian began.
"Champion?"
Sharnoth tilted her head with a slight frown, and Vehrian nodded.
"Your story about how you rose from chains against all odds, your absurd strength incomparable to others around you, and all the different artifacts and relics that you possess—
It is almost as if you are favored by a greater being, a being that people like me cannot fathom."
Sharnoth stayed silent. She didn’t show any reaction to those words. Inwardly, however, she was indeed a little surprised. Vehrian, however, was just beginning.
"This isn’t the first time I have heard a story about a Champion."
"What...?"
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes.
"Throughout the history of our Universe, there have been many Champions. There was one in our race, and even the people who follow you—many of them had Champions leading their people as well.
Of course, not all Champions had the same story or benefits, but the Champions did exist and..."
Vehrian paused, not sure how to say it.
Sharnoth pressured, and after a while, Vehrian just said what was in his mind,
"...and while these Champions lived a heroic life, many of them met the same fate."
Sharnoth stared at Vehrian, waiting for him to continue.
"Death."
The Queen of those who Lost narrowed her eyes, and Vehrian explained further,
"Most of the Champions fell. There could be several reasons for their fall—too many enemies, or perhaps they fell to fate itself.
But the fact that the Champions fell remained.
And after the Champions’ fall, the people who followed them and were overly reliant on them—they fell as well.
I have already experienced this fall when our Champion fell. I have no intention of going through the same experience again."
The Verani explained his thoughts the best way he could.
Sharnoth stayed silent, thinking about Vehrian’s words. Her thoughts even went to the direction Nux was waiting for them to go into. Soon, however, she suppressed those thoughts and,
"Alright."
She nodded.
"I will be true to my words and forgive you.
This will also be the last time you will see me—unless, of course, you are willing to join me. My doors will always remain open for you and for your people."
Sharnoth nodded.
"I hope you become the Champion who never falls, Lady Sharnoth."
Vehrian bowed his head respectfully, and Sharnoth just nodded before disappearing.
"...What are you thinking?"
While Sharnoth was returning after her conversation with Vehrian, Zylarith questioned.
"The previous Champions were weak."
"If they fell even when they were ’favored by a greater being’, it means they were weak."

Sharnoth explained herself, looking into Zylarith’s eyes with a meaningful look on her face. She didn’t say anything else, she didn’t ask any questions, she simply said what needed to be said, and Zylarith nodded at those words.
"This is exactly how a Queen should think."
He praised.

Sharnoth nodded with a light smile on her face. Clearly, despite having complete control over her emotions, to her master, she was still a little girl who couldn’t help but smile when she was praised.
Or at least...
That was the image Sharnoth was creating. But Nux, who was seeing everything from Sharnoth’s perspective and knew her true thoughts—
He could see it.
Sharnoth had lied.
And her lie placed a big smile on Nux’s face.
This was getting much more interesting than he was initially expecting it to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 2056: Beginning of the Queen’s rise.
paragraphs: Time passed, Sharnoth’s army grew at an absurd rate, her name spread far and wide.
Word that the Queen of those who Lost is recruiting talented individuals spread, and more and more people flocked towards her.
It had reached the point where Sharnoth was no longer capable of screening everyone who wished to join them; the job was left to her subordinates.

Even the people from Lower Level Worlds tried to join her, and while most were rejected, some talented ones were accepted—and that spread the word even faster, increasing the number of people trying their luck.
Of course, it was good for Sharnoth. The more men she had, the better it was for her. Soon, however, one problem became apparent.
Sharnoth...
She did not have a stable world or a place she called her base.
Nocthys was still under Aurendor’s control, its resources were being used by those light bastards to gain more allies.

As for the world she had trained in before, it was merely a Middle Level World. It wasn’t strong enough to support her and her men—not to mention it was a Dead World. Its Law Structure was not suitable for intelligent beings anyways.
Sharnoth needed a new home—and not just any home, she needed a home strong enough to support her and her goals.
And as if the very Universe was waiting for her to realize it, a solution appeared right in front of her eyes.
A High Level World named Khaemorr.

Khaemorr’s situation was a bit special. The most recent Next Heir to Khaemorr’s Throne was about six hundred thousand years old, and the current Ruler had already stopped counting his age after reaching two million.
Of course, such cases weren’t rare. The Leaders of High Level Worlds were Eternal Level Beings; a few million years old were actually considered quite young.
Then why such a big difference between the Heir’s and Ruler’s age?
That was quite common as well.
After all, the current Heir wasn’t the only Heir to Khaemorr. Just like how it was with many other worlds, there were hundreds if not thousands of Heirs before him.
Just that none of them could reach Eternal Stage to achieve immortality, and their lifespan ended. The current Heir, however, was an exception.
He had formed an Absolute Law.
He had attained Immortality long ago, and other than his Father, no one could defeat him. He was truly an exceptional heir.
But...
That was all he was.
An Heir.
No matter how skillful he was, unless he became an Eternal, he could not become the Ruler, and...
Khaemorr wasn’t strong enough to support two Eternals.
Meaning that as long as his Father, the current Ruler, existed, the Heir could never obtain what was his by right.
Of course, all worlds face the same problem—with Immortal Rulers, barely anyone abdicates the Supreme Throne. Plus, letting a Transcendent rule a High-Level World was shameful.

However, usually, these problems are solved during Wars between Worlds. When the Rulers die, the Heirs replace them almost instantly. This was also the reason most worlds do not fall just because the Ruler is dead. The World’s Will automatically picks the Heir, and if the Heir is strong enough, he would break through and replace his father.
This did not happen in Nocthys because Nocthys had no Heir. Sharnoth was supposed to be one, but it all happened before she could grow.

Anyways, in Khaemorr, this problem and the tensions that came with it were much stronger. The Ruler refused to be a part of any War. He allied himself with as many as he could and avoided Wars even at the cost of his World.
He cherished his life too much, and Khaemorr was in decline because of his actions.
And the Heir did not like this.
There was no chance for him to replace his father, and this made him impatient, especially after seeing how his father was going out of his way to protect himself.
In the end, the Heir arranged a coup.
And of course, since he couldn’t take on an Eternal himself, he invited...
Yes, he invited Sharnoth and her army into his world.
And just like that, the War of the New Sun began—with the Heir ’leading’ one side and the Ruler the other.
Of course, as the war continued, due to some ’unknown, unfortunate accident’, the Heir fell.
Many believed this would put an end to the war, since Sharnoth and her men no longer had a reason to stay,
But...
Sharnoth did not need a reason.

She never cared about such trivialities. The war continued, now much more strongly than ever. Sharnoth’s army should have been at a disadvantage, considering they were up against an army that was fighting in their home with the support of their world,
But the Heir’s coup had weakened Khaemorr’s army.
Yes, the world was all prepared for the taking. Sharnoth just had to make sure to take it before others noticed and took advantage of the situation.
With that in mind, the Queen charged in at full might.
The true battle had begun.
The skies above were painted in smoke and blood.
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
Khaemorr’s cries had become a common sight, so much that it no longer bothered the two armies facing each other.

These beings clashed with each other like tidal waves, their weapons tearing through their enemies’ flesh, and their abilities shaking the earth beneath them. The stench of burning corpses mixed with the cries of dying soldiers.
War had descended in its truest, most merciless form.
Sharnoth stood at the center of the chaos, her long black cloak fluttering behind her. Her crimson eyes glowed with power, and her voice rang across the battlefield like thunder.
"Push forward! Don’t give them time to regroup! This is the day we take what we deserved!
This is the day,
We get a Home!"
She announced, her voice thundering through her army, filling them with an unknown power—enough to give them the courage to run to their deaths.
These people—who had once lost their worlds, their families, and their pride—resonated with her words and answered her call.
"For The Queen!"
"For our Home!"
A wave of energy burst through her army.
They were no longer just warriors, they were survivors chasing salvation.
Fallen bloodlines.
Forgotten heirs.
They were all there, under the Queen’s command.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
As her army charged forward, Sharnoth raised her hand toward the sky.
A black sun formed above her—almost as if declaring the end.
This was not just war, it was reclamation.
And the beginning of the Queen’s rise.

chapters.title: Chapter 2057: Trap
paragraphs: "For The Queen!"
"For our Home!"
With one shout and endless energy, Sharnoth’s soldiers charged forward.
At the same time—
BOOOOOOOOOOM
A big explosion engulfed tens of thousands of soldiers, not even their ashes were left as the Black Sun Sharnoth had created unleashed its wrath.
What’s even scarier was the fact that the aftereffects of that attack remained. It wasn’t a normal attack, it had the Power of Chaos infested in it.

It instantly turned the field it affected into the Field of Chaos, a field where only Transcendents with Domains could use their abilities. Primordials and lower-level beings, on the other hand, had to rely on their physical strength.
Of course, the conditions were the same for Sharnoth’s men as well, but the difference between them and the defenders was that Sharnoth’s men were prepared for it.

Their formation and troop distribution were made with physical battle in mind. The advantage one single ability gave to them was so absurdly big that even with Khaemorr’s Will supporting the defenders, they were helpless.
What’s worse?

Because it was the Power-infested Chaos, the size of the Field continued to increase. Everything was so perfectly well planned that Sharnoth’s vanguard, people most loyal to her and the army she had invested most of the resources in, moved at the same pace as the field expanded.
It allowed them to remain in the field and lead the charge on their terms.
"CHARGE!!
KILL!!!"
They shouted, their morale burning brighter than ever.

Their blades cut through enemies like they were made of paper. Black and purple energy danced around the field. No one recognized this energy, neither could anyone understand why their abilities stopped working all of a sudden.
"What is happ—"
"I cannot use m—"
"No! No—"
"Something’s wro—"
Yes, before the defenders could even understand what was happening, they were slashed into pieces.

Bodies fell at a rate much faster than anything the defenders had seen before. This wasn’t the first time they were facing Sharnoth’s army—after all, they were the reason the Heir could arrange a coup in the first place.
Countless battles had taken place before this but...
Now, it felt like they were facing completely different opponents. It was almost as if the invaders weren’t even serious before the Heir was dead.
It didn’t take long for the defenders to realize it.
It was a trap, these people had planned it all.
They had been playing right into their hands all this while. Victory was impossible—heck, even survival seemed difficult.
As these thoughts became stronger amongst the soldiers, panic spread.
"I-I DO NOT WISH TO BE A PART OF THIS ANY LONGER!!"
Nobody knew who shouted and it didn’t matter. The shout started a wave.
"A-AGGGHHH!!!"
"GET OUT OF THE WAY!!"
"I DO NOT WISH TO DIE HERE!!"
"WE CANNOT WIN!!"
"RUN!!"
Just like that, the defenders began to break their already weak formations. The Transcendent Commanders did try to control the situation, but it was already too late.
The panic had already spread, the defenders were losing their will to fight.
The defensive formation shattered, siege towers fell, war beasts screamed and collapsed, and barriers that protected the defenders were being undone.
All this happened because of Sharnoth’s one move.
And...

She hadn’t even used much of her strength. After all, the enemy Eternal still hadn’t appeared. In a war like this, it was foolish to use one’s energy on lower-level beings since even the slightest mistakes could change the outcome.
Sharnoth was being careful of that, and within minutes, the situation had turned into something where the Ruler had no choice but to appear.
And he did.
The air grew heavy, the sky above dimmed. The Chaos field Sharnoth had created disappeared in an instant, surprising her charging troops.

A figure stepped down from the sky like a god. A tall, wiry humanoid figure with rough, pale skin like cracked stone, textured with sharp edges and scars. His eyes were pitch-black slits, glowing faintly red, capable of seeing through illusions and movement.
He was Kethrian Khaemorr, the Skarnethi Leader.
*Picture*
Skarnethi were the race that ruled over Khaemorr. They were also called the World’s Trapper, known for their terrifying expertise in traps, ambushes, and battlefield manipulation.
Skarnethi were not physically powerful, nor did they possess grand magic—but they were fearsome, especially Kethrian.
The moment Kethrian appeared, a sudden silence fell over the place. The pressure he released instantly attracted Sharnoth’s attention.
The two Leaders stared at each other.

Sharnoth’s face turned solemn as well. Kethrian was indeed not an opponent she could look down upon. After all, she had only broken through to the Eternal Stage recently, while he was an old monster who had managed to stay alive in this ruthless world for millions of years.
One doesn’t pull it off through luck alone.
What was even more annoying was that Kethrian also had an Absolute Law, so Sharnoth couldn’t simply overpower him with her domain either.
It would be a one-on-one battle.
A battle that would decide the fate of their people.
And in such an important battle,
Sharnoth moved first, teleporting in front of him and striking with her Chaos-infused blade. Yes, she wasn’t afraid of using Chaos right now—after all, she had no plans on keeping him alive.
Kethrian blocked her blade with two fingers.
BOOOOOOOM
The shockwave sent bodies flying and cracked the earth.
Without a word, Kethrian struck back. Sharnoth dodged, but the blow grazed her arm. She realized that she had to be careful—after all, her opponent was a tricky one.
BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM
Their fight lasted only seconds, but each clash led to an explosion. Countless died. Sharnoth tried to keep the death toll on her side to a minimum.
And Kethrian didn’t fail to notice that.
A light smile appeared on his face. Soon, however, the exchange continued.
Within a minute, both sides knew the result in their hearts. Sharnoth was stronger. If this continued like this, Kethrian would lose.
But...
Kethrian also understood another thing—
Sharnoth lacked experience.
He exchanged a few more blows, then suddenly, Khaemorr’s Will teleported him somewhere else.
Sharnoth frowned. She tried to find him and the moment her senses caught him, her eyes widened in horror.
He stood in front of her vanguard—her most loyal followers.
"Don’t yo—"
Sharnoth tried to move, but suddenly,
"It is a trap."
Zylarith warned.
"What?"
Sharnoth frowned.
"It is a trap. Let them die, let them die, there is nothing you can do."
Zylarith declared coldly.
After all, pawns existed to be sacrificed.
But—
"I am not letting them die."
Sharnoth decided as she rushed forward, ready to step into the trap on her own. Kethrian grinned at that sight.
"I told you it is a trap!"
Zylarith raised his voice.
"I will be fine.
I invested too much in them."
Sharnoth spoke as she stepped forward, and the instant she did—
Kethrian activated the trap,
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM

chapters.title: Chapter 2058: FOR THE QUEEN!!!
paragraphs: It was a momentary lapse in judgment.
One step, one wrong step towards her endangered subordinates and the very reality answered.
It began with a flicker.
There was no light, no sound, just... absence.
A sudden folding of existence, as if the world exhaled and forgot to inhale.
Then came the flash.
Just a pulse of blinding white—so bright that it blinded every being present in Khaemorr, even the one standing at the very opposite end.
Yes, the entirety of Khaemorr was lit up,
And then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOM
Collapse.

The space around the impact point folded in on itself, jagged threads of black lightning cracking inward, dragging stone and light into a singular, snapping point. An implosion, as if the very universe had bitten a chunk of Khaemorr out of the map.

A ring of shattered terrain peeled outward in a perfect circle, glass-like debris hanging in the air as if time had forgotten gravity. The air vibrated, then stopped. For a moment, the world simply... paused.
Where there had been a ground—there was nothing.
No scorch marks.
No smoke.
No blood.
Just a smooth, perfect hole in reality.
It was the Absolute Law of Doomed Path.
A Law that allowed Kethrian to set up a Death Region, a region that would kill any being who is not an Infinity the moment they stepped in it.

It was an absurdity, a ridiculous law. This was also the reason why most of Kethrian’s enemies refused to face him. He wasn’t strong himself, but he had the uncanny ability to lure his enemies into his Death Region and end them.

Just like how he did with Sharnoth, it didn’t take long for him to understand that the woman cared for all her subordinates, and the ones she cared the most about were the vanguard. Not just that, the woman was arrogant, she was strong and she knew it.
She was underestimating him.
And that was all Kethrian needed.
He allowed Khaemorr to change his location and teleported in front of her vanguard, tempting her to rush towards him and step right into the Death Region.
Yes, it was that simple.
There were no grand schemes or strong mind play, this is what happens when the enemy underestimates Kethrian. He knew how to take advantage of people’s habits and nature.
And with that,
The battle was over.

Sharnoth was evaporated out of existence, her men were now no longer a threat. Kethrian was planning to recruit the useful ones and massacre the rest, he was even planning to use some of them as slav—
Kethrian suddenly froze.
His connection with Khaemorr showed him where every being, especially an outsider, was.
This connection should no longer show him Sharnoth’s position, then why... why did it still show—
Very slowly, he turned towards the place where Sharnoth stood and there... he saw it.

The woman stood, her face distorted in fear, as if she had witnessed a horror that shook her very core. Yes, she was shaken, yes, her body was trembling, and it looked like she was no longer in the condition to fight.
But...
She was alive.
And she was unhurt.
’B-But how...!?’
Kethrian couldn’t understand.

Because of his and Sharnoth’s clash, every being had evacuated the area, there was no living being around them. This was the entire reason he had been facing her head-on anyway—to create space for his Death Region.
He made sure no one else but Sharnoth stepped into his Death Region, then how...
How was she alive!?
Kethrian’s world was falling apart.
But suddenly,
BOOOOOM
Sharnoth appeared in front of him again, her crimson eyes shining much more intensely than before.
Kethrian, who barely blocked her sword, was taken aback. Didn’t she look like she could no longer continue the battle?
Why does she look as good as new now?
No, not just new, she looks... stronger...?
Kethrian had too many questions in his head. Right now, however, he didn’t have the time to think about them.
He had to fight back.
He tried it many times, somehow dragging Sharnoth into the Death Region, but it simply didn’t work. Sharnoth was too fast and precise, almost as if she had turned into a different person.
The two continued to exchange blows and very quickly, it had become apparent,
Sharnoth had a heavy upper hand.
The only reason Kethrian was even able to hold on till now was because Khaemorr’s Will was doing everything in its power to keep him alive.

His Death Region wasn’t working at all. Every time he activated it, Sharnoth dragged someone in it to defuse it that instant. He was tired, he was running out of energy, and his body had thousands of bruises and injuries.

Sharnoth’s abilities were far beyond his capability. Even now, he had no clue what her Law actually was—heck, he wasn’t even able to comprehend the sort of energy she used. He just knew that whatever it was, it was creating a mess inside his body.
Yes, Sharnoth’s energy had infiltrated his body.
It was over.
And with a final slash, Sharnoth beheaded Kethrian, marking the end of the war.

With the death of the ruler and his head hovering in the air for all to see, it was only a matter of time before the rest of the soldiers gave in. Some tried fighting to the bitter end, but it didn’t matter.
The battle was over. In three hours, the defenders were either captured or killed. Sharnoth took over Khaemorr’s Will and made the world hers.
Yes, Khaemorr was now home to Sharnoth and her people.
"W-We did it!!!"
The soldiers shouted.
"Our Queen did it!!"
"FOR THE QUEEN!!!"
"FOR OUR HOME!!"
The soldiers roared in joy. Sharnoth, hovering in the air, stared at her people with a proud smile on her face.
She addressed her people, it was time for a victory speech, but Nux couldn’t care less about it.
He was more interested to see what was going to happen next.
After all, Zylarith momentarily took over Sharnoth’s body. He wanted to see what the man had to say about it.

sentences.text: It was a momentary lapse in judgment.
One step, one wrong step towards her endangered subordinates and the very reality answered.
It began with a flicker.
There was no light, no sound, just... absence.
A sudden folding of existence, as if the world exhaled and forgot to inhale.
Then came the flash.
Just a pulse of blinding white—so bright that it blinded every being present in Khaemorr, even the one standing at the very opposite end.
Yes, the entirety of Khaemorr was lit up,
And then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOM
Collapse.
The space around the impact point folded in on itself, jagged threads of black lightning cracking inward, dragging stone and light into a singular, snapping point.
An implosion, as if the very universe had bitten a chunk of Khaemorr out of the map.
A ring of shattered terrain peeled outward in a perfect circle, glass-like debris hanging in the air as if time had forgotten gravity.
The air vibrated, then stopped.
For a moment, the world simply... paused.
Where there had been a ground—there was nothing.
No scorch marks.
No smoke.
No blood.
Just a smooth, perfect hole in reality.
It was the Absolute Law of Doomed Path.
A Law that allowed Kethrian to set up a Death Region, a region that would kill any being who is not an Infinity the moment they stepped in it.
It was an absurdity, a ridiculous law.
This was also the reason why most of Kethrian’s enemies refused to face him.
He wasn’t strong himself, but he had the uncanny ability to lure his enemies into his Death Region and end them.
Just like how he did with Sharnoth, it didn’t take long for him to understand that the woman cared for all her subordinates, and the ones she cared the most about were the vanguard.
Not just that, the woman was arrogant, she was strong and she knew it.
She was underestimating him.
And that was all Kethrian needed.
He allowed Khaemorr to change his location and teleported in front of her vanguard, tempting her to rush towards him and step right into the Death Region.
Yes, it was that simple.
There were no grand schemes or strong mind play, this is what happens when the enemy underestimates Kethrian.
He knew how to take advantage of people’s habits and nature.
And with that,
The battle was over.
Sharnoth was evaporated out of existence, her men were now no longer a threat.
Kethrian was planning to recruit the useful ones and massacre the rest, he was even planning to use some of them as slav—
Kethrian suddenly froze.
His connection with Khaemorr showed him where every being, especially an outsider, was.
This connection should no longer show him Sharnoth’s position, then why... why did it still show—
Very slowly, he turned towards the place where Sharnoth stood and there... he saw it.
The woman stood, her face distorted in fear, as if she had witnessed a horror that shook her very core.
Yes, she was shaken, yes, her body was trembling, and it looked like she was no longer in the condition to fight.
But...
She was alive.
And she was unhurt.
’B-But how...!?’
Kethrian couldn’t understand.
Because of his and Sharnoth’s clash, every being had evacuated the area, there was no living being around them.
This was the entire reason he had been facing her head-on anyway—to create space for his Death Region.
He made sure no one else but Sharnoth stepped into his Death Region, then how...
How was she alive!?
Kethrian’s world was falling apart.
But suddenly,
BOOOOOM
Sharnoth appeared in front of him again, her crimson eyes shining much more intensely than before.
Kethrian, who barely blocked her sword, was taken aback.
Didn’t she look like she could no longer continue the battle?
Why does she look as good as new now?
No, not just new, she looks... stronger...?
Kethrian had too many questions in his head.
Right now, however, he didn’t have the time to think about them.
He had to fight back.
He tried it many times, somehow dragging Sharnoth into the Death Region, but it simply didn’t work.
Sharnoth was too fast and precise, almost as if she had turned into a different person.
The two continued to exchange blows and very quickly, it had become apparent,
Sharnoth had a heavy upper hand.
The only reason Kethrian was even able to hold on till now was because Khaemorr’s Will was doing everything in its power to keep him alive.
His Death Region wasn’t working at all.
Every time he activated it, Sharnoth dragged someone in it to defuse it that instant.
He was tired, he was running out of energy, and his body had thousands of bruises and injuries.
Sharnoth’s abilities were far beyond his capability.
Even now, he had no clue what her Law actually was—heck, he wasn’t even able to comprehend the sort of energy she used.
He just knew that whatever it was, it was creating a mess inside his body.
Yes, Sharnoth’s energy had infiltrated his body.

chapters.title: Chapter 2059: Sharnoth’s Determination
paragraphs: "I told you it is a trap!"
Zylarith raised his voice.
"I will be fine."
Sharnoth replied confidently as she glanced at Kethrian with a dangerous look on her face.
"I invested too much in them."
She declared. She had no plans on losing the subordinates she had gathered and cultivated with so much effort.
But—
"I can say the same too."
Suddenly, Sharnoth heard a voice and before she could react—
She lost control over her body.
She frowned. Everything around her slowed down as her senses became stronger. Then, as if to shock her even further, she saw her arms move without her... wanting to move them.
They... they were moving on their own.
No, more accurately, someone else was moving them.
She stuttered.
She saw how ’she’ accessed her storage ring and took out an artifact. It was a summoning artifact that allowed her to summon one of her most loyal subordinates in front of her.
’She’ activated the artifact, summoning a subordinate who was currently fighting another enemy. His sudden summoning confused him,
"Lady Shar—"
He tried asking a question, but before he could say or do anything, Sharnoth’s hand moved. ’She’ grabbed his head and threw him into the Death Region Kethrian had created and just as she did—
BOOOOOOOOOOM
She witnessed the explosion right in front of her, the explosion that was more than enough to kill her a few times over.
Less than a second.
From her losing control over her body, to summoning a subordinate, using his body to activate the trap, all the way to the explosion she was seeing—it all happened in less than a second.
And the moment that second was over—
Sharnoth regained control over her body.
"W-What...?"

The woman stuttered, unable to believe what just happened. Her worldview crumbled. Letting someone else control her body as if it was their own was a strange, disgusting feeling that she didn’t like one bit.
But...
For now, it was time for her to deal with the enemy.

Once she realized what he was capable of, Sharnoth became serious. The battle continued without any mistakes from her side and soon, she overpowered him and took over Khaemorr within the next few hours.
The matter ended just like that—
Or at least, that was what Sharnoth was hoping.
But...
"Sharnoth Nocthys, talk to me."
Zylarith ordered with a solemn look on his face.
He had been staying silent all this while, waiting for Sharnoth to bring it up. But realizing that the girl had no plans on saying anything, he stepped forward on his own.
Sharnoth paused and Zylarith continued,
"I took over your body, I am sure you must have a lot of questions, ask—"
"You did what you had to do in order to keep me alive."
Sharnoth spoke up.
She had more than a few hours to think about it. She had already come up with a conclusion in her head.
Zylarith frowned.
"You only did what was necessary, I am thankful—"
"I took over your body and all you have to say is a thank you? We both know you are a smarter girl than that, Sharnoth.
You have questions in your heart, ask."
Zylarith ordered again, but once again,
"I do not."
Sharnoth shook her head.
Her answer surprised Zylarith. He obviously didn’t believe it, but Nux knew it was the truth. Sharnoth truly did not have any questions in her mind.
How did Zylarith take over her body?
What did he do to her?
To Sharnoth, none of it mattered.
Sharnoth was no fool, Nux knew it better than anyone. She had suspected Zylarith ever since Vehrian, the Verani, mentioned the story of Champions.
She knew Zylarith had a goal, a goal that was not aligned with hers. She knew that just like other champions, she would fall as well but—
"I do not care what you have done to me, Master. I only know that you gave me power and made me who I am.
I have but one goal—destruction of Aurendor and blood of Vexarion Aurendor in my hands. As long as I achieve that,
I do not care what happens to me."
Sharnoth declared in a bone-chilling cold tone, a tone that surprised even Zylarith.
"Do what you wish, Master. I will not question you.
And in return, I just want one thing."
Sharnoth stated.
Yes, she knew that her Master was a demon and she...
She was prepared to sell her soul to the demon for the sake of her revenge.
"You will get what you want, I promise you."
Zylarith declared boldly and at those words, Sharnoth kowtowed on the floor, showing her true submission.

Nux wasn’t surprised by this scene, he already knew the woman’s thoughts. She knew how desperately she wanted her revenge. She knew she would go to any lengths to achieve it, even if that turned her into nothing but an empty soul with no control over her own body for eternity.
Yes, she was willing to risk it all.
She was that determined.
And with that determination, her life continued. Khaemorr became hers, she made a name for herself, joined the Faction of Darkness and soon, she declared war on Aurendor.

The war continued for years, but she never once got to face Vexarion. The Herald of Justice avoided her because he knew what sort of monstrosity she was. Sharnoth had no choice but to force him to face her through political pressure. The woman created her faction, her faction was slowly overpowering Vexarion’s, but then—
Nux appeared and everything turned to shit.

Her subordinates died, the worlds under her faction declared neutrality, her enemy became stronger, her Council Members started leaving—everything she had prepared all her life, she saw it all crumble in front of her own eyes one by one.
And she... she couldn’t do anything about it.
She was desperate and full of hatred,
But then—
"Get stronger."
Her master suddenly spoke up as he presented a black-purple football-sized crystal to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 2060: Why not ally with the same monster?
paragraphs: "Get stronger."
In Sharnoth’s desperation, her master suddenly spoke up as he presented a black-purple football-sized crystal to her.
"Absorb this, get stronger, and destroy the enemy you have hated all your life."
He instructed.
"What is it?"
Sharnoth questioned, slightly confused.
"Crystallization of all the Chaos I have gathered ever since I raised you. I intended to give it to you once I was sure it would help you break through to Infinity Stage.
But since things have come this far,
I have no other choice.
If not Infinity, then be Pseudo-Infinity instead.
We will figure out the rest later."
Zylarith answered as the football-sized crystal moved towards Sharnoth.
Sharnoth stared at it in silence.
"What are you doing?"
Zylarith questioned with a frown. After all, Sharnoth wasn’t in the position to waste any more time. Now that she had the solution, she should act in haste.
Or at least that’s what was supposed to happen.
But suddenly—
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM
Sharnoth, who stayed silent for more than a minute, suddenly extended her domain.
{Capture}
She ordered.
Just like any other Eternal, in her Domain, she had turned into an Absolute Being whose words had become a Law.
Even if Zylarith was a being she couldn’t truly interact with in his Soul Form, inside her domain, this was possible.
With her words, Zylarith’s surroundings moved, purple-black chains came out of nowhere and tried to capture him, but...
The moment the chains touched his body, his body dispersed into thin air and the Chaos Chains wrapped themselves around a disc-like relic.
"I did not think you would move against me, you are brave."
Zylarith spoke before his body disappeared like dust in the air. The only thing left of him was the relic that came out of his body.
Zylarith...
He escaped.
No, more accurately, he was never here to begin with. It was merely his projection cast by the relic that was now in Sharnoth’s hand.
Sharnoth grabbed the relic her chains had ’captured’ without saying anything. From the expressionless look on her face, it was clear that she wasn’t surprised by what just happened.
Zylarith was no fool; she knew it better than others.
He would never risk his life, so the fact that she couldn’t capture him did not surprise her. As for what he was saying before...
Sharnoth slowly glanced at the crystal in front of her with the same expressionless look on her face.
A crystal that would raise her strength and turn her into a Pseudo-Infinity.
’What a joke.’
The Queen snorted in her head.

If something like this truly existed, Zylarith would have given it to her a long time ago. Sure, he acted like he wanted to give it to her when she was ready to become an Infinity and what he did was a desperate action,
But Zylarith would never act ’desperately’.
Sharnoth knew it a long time ago—Zylarith was no ally. He, for some reason, wanted to take over her body; he was just waiting for the right time.
And honestly, Sharnoth didn’t care.

She knew she needed to be stronger before Zylarith took action. At the very least, it would happen after she destroyed her enemy. In her mind, Sharnoth thought of it as a price for Zylarith’s help and convinced herself.
No matter what Zylarith wanted, as long as she got her revenge, it didn’t matter.
But...
With Nux coming into the equation and making things difficult for her, Zylarith’s plan changed as well.

This crystal—it must be full of Chaos Energy, just like Zylarith said. But its goal wasn’t to strengthen Sharnoth, it was to fill her body with more Chaos Energy. Energy that belonged to Zylarith. Energy that would allow him to get complete control over her body instead of the partial one he already had.
Yes, Zylarith wanted to take the price before fulfilling his part of the deal.
Of course, all of this was just Sharnoth’s theory. She could still be wrong about him. But if that was the case...
’He would be here instead of this...’
She muttered in her head as she stared at the disc in her hand.
Yes, that disc was more than enough reason for her to believe what Zylarith was actually planning. He wouldn’t have prepared all this if he was being honest.
The disc in her hand was all the proof she needed.
But the thing was...
Even if she figured it out, even if she didn’t fall for Zylarith’s schemes, things still weren’t any better.
Her problem still remained the same, the empire she built was still crumbling, and she couldn’t think of any way to protect it.
Honestly, in her mind, Sharnoth was cursing the day she first interacted with Nux. To think she attracted that monster’s attention because of that master of he—
The instant that thought appeared in her mind, Sharnoth’s expression changed as suddenly, a new idea popped up.
Nux...
His enemy was Zylarith, wasn’t he?
The two of them had only interacted one time. There was no reason for them to be enemies anymore, especially when Zylarith had also turned his back on her.
The more she thought about it, the better the idea sounded in her head.
All this happened because she offended an incomprehensible monster, did it not?
A monster whose ability she or anyone around her did not understand.
Then...
Why not ally with the same monster?
He first approached her because he wanted to be her ally anyways, did he not?
Why doesn’t she approach him now?
The moment she thought about it, she recalled something.
’He says he is leaving it here in case you changed your mind.’
She remembered her subordinate passing her the Call Artifact that Nux had left for her in case she wanted to talk to him.
{No being other than me should exist inside}
With a determined look on her face, Sharnoth made sure Zylarith wasn’t around her, took out the Call Artifact, and activated it.
Then, she heard a voice—an extremely annoying voice.
"It has been a while, Lady Sharnoth.
I must admit, I didn’t think you would call this soon."

chapters.title: Chapter 2061: A Promise...
paragraphs: From there, Nux saw Sharnoth’s memories all the way to the point where she wore the Artifact he gave her, and the memories finally ended.
Nux stayed silent for a minute. To him, it felt like a total of a hundred thousand years had passed, but in reality, barely a few minutes had passed.
He needed some time to get used to the time disparity.
Yes, it wasn’t the first time he had done this, not to mention he had devoured actual worlds with millions if not billions of years of memories, so it shouldn’t be a big deal for him.
But he still needed a few seconds to adjust.

Not to mention he just formed a new Law—an incomplete Law, yes. Sharnoth may be a genius, but she wasn’t born in Chaosveil, and Zylarith only gave her the artifacts that dealt with just a single part of Chaos, ensuring that her knowledge would always be incomplete.
Of course, it wasn’t a big deal. Almost every being in the Universe has Incomplete Laws. Even the Umbrasol Progenitors were no exception; they only understood a part of Death, not complete Death.
However...
If Nux’s theory was correct,
Then Zylarith was an exception to this rule.
He... he must have the Complete Law of Absolute Chaos.
A stronger version of the Law Sharnoth had formed. This was also how he was able to momentarily take over Sharnoth’s body back in Khaemorr.
Of course, to Nux, this did not matter.
Complete or Incomplete, it was still a Chaos-related Law nonetheless. With a light smile on his face, Nux raised his head and suddenly, a black-purple energy hovered above his palm.
He then closed his eyes to sense the energies inside his universe, and there it was.
The Energy of Chaos flowing inside his Universe together with other Primordial Energies.
’Three more left.’
Shadow muttered with a big smile on her face, knowing exactly what Nux was thinking.
’Indeed.’
Nux nodded.
’Found anything interesting?’
Aisha questioned with a playful smile on her face.
’I did.’
Nux nodded.
’Very interesting things.’
His smile widened.
’You should call her then.’
Aisha suggested. Nux, however, shook his head.
’Not now.
I need to prepare something.’
’Hmm?’
The Succubus frowned, and Nux’s smile widened even further.
’She is going to be an ally; shouldn’t I prepare a meeting gift?’
A few hours later, Nux activated the Call Artifact, and Sharnoth picked it up in one ring—almost as if she was waiting for him.
"You look desperate."
Nux laughed.
"It isn’t good if you act too desperately in a negotiation. People on the other side of the negotiation could take advantage of that situation."
"I already showed you my memories. You know everything about me. These political games would only waste more time."
Sharnoth answered with an emotionless look on her face.
"That’s true."
Nux nodded.
"So? What is it that you want?"
"You already know that."
Sharnoth answered with the same look, and Nux just stared at her with a deadpan look on his face.
"You are no fun, you know that?"
"I sometimes get that."
"Stop lying. No one ever said that to you because they were too scared. I know because I read your memories."
Nux waved his hand dismissively.
Sharnoth stayed silent.
After a moment, Nux sighed, and the playful look on his face disappeared. He then looked into Sharnoth’s eyes and—
"You want revenge, do you not?"
"Yes."
"It won’t be easy."
Nux shook his head.
"You do not have to—"
"I will stop acting against you. I have no reason to, not anymore.
But you know this won’t solve the problem."
Sharnoth’s face turned solemn.

Just as Nux said, even if he did give up now, the damage was already done. Her reputation had plummeted, her Faction was weakened considerably, and the enemy had used this chance to strengthen itself.
Not just that—even if Sharnoth ignored all that, rebuilt her strength, and surpassed Aurendor and its Faction to reach a point where she could defeat them—
Now that she has used Chaos so openly, it was nearly impossible to contain this matter. Vexarion and his people could always use that as an excuse to seek asylum in the Supreme Worlds.
It wouldn’t be surprising if the Supreme Worlds decided to act against them as well.
Not to mention, there was also Zylarith, who wouldn’t just let Sharnoth go—not after she ruined whatever plan he had.
There were simply too many variables stacked against her.
"What do you want?"
Sharnoth questioned directly. She knew that if Nux was bringing it up, he must have had a solution.
Whatever the price, she was prepared—even if she had to sacrifice her life.
"Time."
Nux answered.
"What...?"
"I can help you in your battle against Aurendor, but I am not strong enough to deal with the Supreme Worlds if they decide to involve themselves with this situation, which I know they will.
I would have directly teleported you next to Vexarion, but you will then be suppressed by Aurendor, and defeating him in that state wouldn’t be easy either.
If you wish to win, you need to capture Vexarion off guard, which is highly unlikely considering the current situation.
The only other, much surer way would be... to go against the Supreme Worlds, which, admittedly, I am not strong enough for yet."
Nux answered honestly. Then, he looked into Sharnoth’s eyes with a determined look on his face and—
"So give me time, Sharnoth Nocthys.
I promise you that there will come a day when Aurendor and Vexarion Aurendor will be under your feet, groveling and begging for mercy."
Sharnoth turned silent at those words.
A promise...
Honestly, she did not have the heart to believe such a thing after being betrayed once. But in the position she was, she had no other cho—
"And to prove my determination, I offer you this."
Just as Sharnoth was thinking all this, Nux suddenly waved his hand, and suddenly, a face Sharnoth could never forget appeared beside him.
"Remember him?"
Nux questioned and—Sharnoth’s crimson eyes burned with rage.
The Aurendor soldier who once raped her mother till she started crying...
This bastard...
He was alive!!
"As unlikely as it sounds, the dude became a Transcendent.
He doesn’t have much time left though,
So I was hoping to gift him to you—you know, to give him some ’good time’ like he always wanted."
Nux offered as his smile became demonic.
