chapters.title: Chapter 2062: New Obsession
paragraphs: "As unlikely as it sounds, the dude became a Transcendent.
He doesn’t have much time left though,
So I was hoping to gift him to you, you know, to give him some ’good time’ like he always wanted."
Nux offered as his smile became demonic.
And Sharnoth...

She stared at the unconscious man she was seeing with her crimson eyes wide open. The world around her slowed down, her breathing became louder, and the memories of this bastard walking towards her mother, tearing her clothes and...
Sharnoth clenched her fists. Her mind recalled everything as if it happened a few moments ago. All those emotions she felt—her rage, her hatred—it all returned, twisting her face.
Nux stared at her for a moment, then, with a wave of his hand, the being in front of him disappeared and appeared next to Sharnoth.
"If you need any torture method, I have quite a few. Well, I do know you have some interesting ideas too, so I guess I am not needed anymore."
He shrugged.
Sharnoth couldn’t say anything. She was too busy staring at her enemy.
Nux chuckled at that reaction, then he decided to end the call.
He knew Sharnoth was currently in no condition to talk. Her mind should currently be overwhelmed with memories of the past.
To be honest, he was pitying the man he sent to her. His end...
It wouldn’t be good.
After the call ended, all his wives appeared next to him and,
"You just promised you will help her without gaining anything. Was that wise?"
Felberta questioned.
"You should have negotiated."
Aeliana nodded as well.
It felt like a waste.
"Nux, you..."
Amaya narrowed her eyes.
"Hmm?"
Nux turned towards her and smiled, and this smile was all it took to rile up Amaya.
"Nux, is she an enemy?"
She questioned directly.
"Oh, come on, don’t be naïve, Amaya.
I told you before, didn’t I?
She had potential."
Allura chuckled, her purple eyes shining playfully.
Amaya narrowed her eyes even further. The fact that Nux wasn’t denying these claims made her even warier.
Another bitch!
"What are you planning, Nux?"
Vyriana questioned directly.
She didn’t care if another one joined them, it was inevitable. If not Sharnoth, then it would have been someone else.
She just cared about what was going to happen going forward.

Whether Sharnoth was a potential sister wasn’t yet known, but what they did know was that she wasn’t a helpless little girl. She was an Eternal. Simply giving her favors was foolish—they should get something in return.
An alliance, a useful relic, important information—anything.
But then—
’Stop worrying. If it continues like this, we won’t just get "something" out of it, we will get that woman’s absolute loyalty.’
Everyone heard a voice.
It was Melia. Currently, the woman was in one of the dead worlds that the Leander Family was using as their base.
’Looks like you are done.’
Nux smiled at her words.
’It wasn’t difficult.’
Melia shrugged, and when the rest of the women heard her, only one thing came to their mind.
Monster.
The women all stared at each other. Nux, on the other hand, chuckled and teleported everyone in front of Melia.
"Tsk, quit showing off, will you?"
Aisha snorted as she looked at her surroundings. The world she had known was no longer recognizable.
A thick mist of crimson rolled across the land like a living tide.

The sky was not blue. It was red—deep and heavy, like it had been soaked in blood for centuries. The earth beneath it pulsed softly, as if it had a heartbeat. Mountains, trees, even the distant castle walls—everything was formed of glistening blood, hardened yet somehow still fluid, shifting with each breath the world took.
At the center of this bleeding realm stood a towering 25-meter-tall, sharp, grand throne, and on it sat Melia.
She wore a dress stitched from threads of blood that shimmered like silk. Her long black hair rested lazily over one shoulder, framing her perfect, flawless, pale face.
Her head was adorned with a delicate crown of blood thorns, hovering just above her as if the very world itself bent to her will.
She looked like a queen born of a nightmare—and she was calm, completely still, the kind of stillness that made your breath catch, your instincts scream.
The moment her eyes fell on Nux, she stood up and walked down from her throne in a slow, regal manner.
Nux stared at his Vampire with a big smile on his face. He stepped forward as well; the blood beneath him formed ripples as he walked.
Slowly, Melia walked close to him and entered his embrace, her head now resting on his chest.
"You look beautiful."
Nux praised. His hands had already started kneading her butt, an act that made Melia’s body tremble.
"She is just showing off!"
Aisha complained.
At those words, Melia raised her head and glanced at the succubus.
"I am not doing this on purpose. This is just how my domain looked like when I broke through."
She answered calmly.
Yes, the Vampire had broken through as well. She was now a Transcendent.
And not just that—as if her powers were waiting for her to break through the Transcendent Stage—her powers instantly surged, surpassing most of the Transcendents.
Her domain was simply too strong.
The Law of Absolute Blood Sovereignty.

A Law that allowed her to have absolute control over blood. In a domain created out of blood, it meant that Melia had absolute control over this place. The people in her domain were already at a great disadvantage—after all, the blood beneath their very feet could be the one to end them.
The blood couldn’t just bind them; it could poison, weaken, or even pierce through them, and there is nothing most beings could do about it.
What’s worse was that since Melia had an Absolute Law, overpowering her domain was next to impossible. Very few people could defeat her if she focused on staying in her realm and defending herself.
The woman had already reached a level where she took down multiple Aurendor Transcendents, even though she had only broken through a few weeks ago.
"What did you mean Nux will get her absolute loyalty?"
Aeliana questioned as she glanced at her disciple.
"I read their memories."
Melia answered.
"I saw her through their eyes. I saw what they did to her. I saw her eyes.

That woman is filled with rage and hatred. You can say she is obsessed with these emotions. If we allow her to let those strong emotions out and empty herself, her mind would automatically start looking for a new obsession."
"New obsession..."
Amaya’s expression changed, and Melia nodded as she glanced at Nux.
"This is what you were planning, weren’t you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2063: When I am done with you, you will fall in love with me.
paragraphs: "This is what you were planning, weren’t you?"
Melia questioned as she glanced at Nux.
"I can’t just not help a woman in need, now can I?
I am not that heartless,
My heart is simply too pure for that."
Nux grinned and the women around him rolled their eyes.
"So that was the plan..."
Vyriana muttered.
"You want her to be indebted to you, and not just with one gift. You are planning something much bigger."
The Dragon spoke as she turned her head and glanced at the 3-meter-tall blood seeds that were hovering in the air, bound by both the blood sky and ground.

Yes, these ’blood seeds’ weren’t just some props to make this domain look prettier; they were Aurendor Transcendents Melia had defeated, and every single one of them had interacted with Sharnoth or her mother in one way or another.
"We are quite lucky."
Nux commented with a smile.
Melia nodded as well.
"The Aurendorians are quite interesting. To think their people could outlive most people in this Universe."
She commented, a little impressed.
Of course, she knew different races had different lifespans.
Even back in Yrniel, Vampires and Dragons usually had longer lifespans compared to others. Demons, Elves, and Dwarves too had different lifespans, while Humans and Beastmen had the lowest lifespan.

However, the total difference between the long-living races and the race with the shortest lifespan wasn’t bigger than 500 years. Sure, this difference got bigger when races from other Universes were considered,

But all this was only considerable when mortals were compared. As beings started to cultivate and became stronger, their lifespan extended as well. At this point, a few thousand years didn’t make much difference.
Aurendorians, however, were different.
Their lifespan was much higher than normal. What’s more, was that their lifespan increases more than other races in the Universe as they break through.
While a normal Transcendent can only live for 100,000 years, an Aurendorian Transcendent can live for 125,000 years.
This was the reason Nux was able to catch these Transcendents, who were once soldiers who had defiled Sharnoth’s mother.
Of course, Nux knew there were such races in the Universe with longer lifespans—some Transcendents could live for 500,000 years or more—but to think Aurendorians would be one such people.
This indeed worked out well for him,
Now, he could gather more sacrifices to permanently have Sharnoth on his side. After all, unlike her, he didn’t need to go for an all-out war to abduct people he wanted to.
Yes, he still couldn’t gather most of the culprits since all of them had died, but the higher the number, the better it is for him.
"Did you find anything?"
He questioned as he glanced at Melia.
"Three more."
Melia answered.
"Just three?"
"Rest are dead."
The Vampire answered and Nux just shrugged.
"Where are they?"
He questioned.
Melia then gave him the coordinates of the worlds the three targets were in and Nux—
"I will be back."
He disappeared.
"He is working hard."
Allura chuckled.
"When has he not worked hard at a time like this?"
Astaria rolled her eyes.
The rest of the women chuckled as well.
Aisha, on the other hand, had another problem.
"Oi, how long do you plan on keeping this domain?"

"This is called training. One does this to push themselves beyond the limits and get stronger. It is a concept foreign to many, so don’t feel foolish or alone. You can come to me if you have any questions."
The Vampire answered sarcastically. What made it even worse was the fact that she said those words with a straight, deadpan tone.
"You have gotten much more annoying after breaking through, you know?"
Aisha snorted.
"I apologize for working hard. I will see to it that I slack around like you do."
Melia once again answered in her deadpan tone, and the Succubus almost lost her mind. It was quite entertaining to watch.
"You sure are having fun."
On the other side, Edda walked towards Allura, who was watching everything with an amused look on her face.
"Are you not?"
Allura questioned back, staring at her two sisters who were about to throw hands, and Skyla and Evane, who had gone there to stop them.
"I am."
Edda nodded,
"I am more curious about you though.
You are oddly silent these days, almost as if you are trying to hide something."
"You are thinking too much."
Allura just smiled.
"You don’t think you can hide it from me, do you? I thought we had a special relationship."
Edda muttered, recalling the time the two of them were together inside the Skyfall Royal Palace.
Allura laughed gently. She then glanced at Edda for a moment and—
"I am preparing something, and it needs time."
"Hmm?"

"You will know when it is time."
Allura simply placed a finger on her lip, signaling Edda to stop.
Edda was momentarily taken aback. Soon, however, she just shrugged and stopped talking about it.
On the other side, Nux, who, together with his subordinates, abducted the three Transcendents, read their memories, trying to find more, but his luck seemed to have run out.
The rest of the culprits were all dead.
’Well, I guess fifteen should be enough.’
He shrugged inwardly and suddenly,
Bzzz
The Call Artifact inside his storage ring buzzed, instantly placing a smile on his face as he realized who it was.
"Lady Sharnoth, I thought you would take your time enjoying the gift I sent you."
He answered with a big smile.
"I lost myself for a moment there. I apologize for my action."
Sharnoth slightly bowed her head.
"What do you mean? I wanted you to lose yourself. You have a lot of pent-up emotions in your heart—let them out."
"No, I would like to take my time. I do not know when I will get this chance again. Acting rashly would be foolish."
"Right."
Nux nodded at those words.
"Indeed, it wouldn’t be fair for our guest if you acted without being considerate. You should take your time and come up with something perfect for him.
But...
You don’t have to worry, he isn’t the only gift I prepared, you know?"
"What...?"
Sharnoth’s expression changed, and Nux’s smile widened even further.
"This is just the beginning, Sharnoth Nocthys,
When I am done with you, you will fall in love with me."

Nux grinned and the women around him rolled their eyes.
"So that was the plan..."
Vyriana muttered.
"You want her to be indebted to you, and not just with one gift.
You are planning something much bigger."

"We are quite lucky."
Nux commented with a smile.
Melia nodded as well.
"The Aurendorians are quite interesting.
To think their people could outlive most people in this Universe."
She commented, a little impressed.
Of course, she knew different races had different lifespans.
Even back in Yrniel, Vampires and Dragons usually had longer lifespans compared to others.
Demons, Elves, and Dwarves too had different lifespans, while Humans and Beastmen had the lowest lifespan.
However, the total difference between the long-living races and the race with the shortest lifespan wasn’t bigger than 500 years.
Sure, this difference got bigger when races from other Universes were considered,
But all this was only considerable when mortals were compared.
As beings started to cultivate and became stronger, their lifespan extended as well.
At this point, a few thousand years didn’t make much difference.
Aurendorians, however, were different.
Their lifespan was much higher than normal.
What’s more, was that their lifespan increases more than other races in the Universe as they break through.
While a normal Transcendent can only live for 100,000 years, an Aurendorian Transcendent can live for 125,000 years.
This was the reason Nux was able to catch these Transcendents, who were once soldiers who had defiled Sharnoth’s mother.
Of course, Nux knew there were such races in the Universe with longer lifespans—some Transcendents could live for 500,000 years or more—but to think Aurendorians would be one such people.

"Just three?"
"Rest are dead."
The Vampire answered and Nux just shrugged.

He disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 2064: We can... kill Vexarion?
paragraphs: “This is just the beginning, Sharnoth Nocthys,
When I am done with you, you will fall in love with me.”
Sharnoth blinked in confusion. At her reaction, Nux just laughed out loud.
“I am just messing around, don’t take my words seriously.”
Sharnoth had no clue how to react to those words. Nux knew that, so he started the conversation instead,
“So? Why did you call me? What do you need?”
“This is what I am supposed to ask.”
Sharnoth replied, forgetting what Nux said before.

“You said you need time in order to be strong enough to deal with the Supreme Worlds. What I do not understand is why go so far for me? To think you would declare your intention to face the Supreme Worlds for my sake, why? What do you need from me?”
The Queen questioned.
She did not believe in kindness without reason. Every person acts based on their want, and it scared her since she did not know what Nux wanted.
“I am not going against the Supreme Worlds for your sake, I am doing it for my own.”
“Huh?”
Sharnoth frowned, and Nux started explaining.
“It is only a matter of time before the Supreme Worlds come after me.”
“Why would they?”
“You already know that, do you not?”
Nux questioned back with a light smile on his face, and Sharnoth’s expression changed.
“...you are the anomaly the Universe is after.”
She muttered with a wary look on her face.
“That is correct.”
Nux nodded, admitting it without any intentions to hide anything.
From Sharnoth’s memories, he knew the woman already had her suspicions, yet she still came to him because she had no other choice.
After all, it wasn’t like she herself could go to them. The Supreme Worlds might not be taking any action right now, but it is only a matter of time before they act against Sharnoth.
“Supreme Worlds will be after both of us eventually. They are our common enemy, we have no choice but to ally with each other.”
Nux answered.
“So you need my help.”
Sharnoth commented.
“You can say that, yes. Your strength will be a valuable addition.”
Nux nodded again.
“You already know what I want.”
Sharnoth muttered.
“I already made a promise.”

The two stayed silent for a moment, staring at each other, as if trying to read the other. Well, it was mostly Sharnoth trying to read Nux. Nux just stayed silent and gave her all the time she wanted.
“...I will do what you want me to.”
Sharnoth spoke up.
“Hmm?”
Nux frowned at those words.
“That was not what I was expecting.”
“Huh?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“Shouldn’t you be doubting me? After all, I am my father’s son. Who is to say I wouldn’t just use you and discard you when I am done?
Or at least... that is what you should be thinking now.”
The Queen turned silent at those words, not saying anything.
“Ah, you must be clinging to whatever hope you are left with. I did not consider your desperation in my prediction. That was my bad.”
Nux nodded to himself. Sharnoth clenched her fists at those words. Her situation truly was... laughable. It was pitiful.
“It truly is a pity.”
Suddenly, Nux commented. Sharnoth turned towards him with a frown, and he continued,
“I came prepared. I had thought of so many things to make you trust me and get you on my side, but to think you would come to me in desperation, of all scenarios. Truly a pity.
What wasted efforts.”
Nux sighed as he shook his head, and Sharnoth...
“...what are you talking about?”
She questioned directly. She was more confused than ever.
Why does every conversation with this man sound so... vague? Just how is this even possible?
Does he do it purposefully?
Why?
Does he like being annoying or something?
Or does he take pleasure in confusing others around him?
What sort of rotten personality was it?
Oblivious to the woman’s thoughts, Nux just shrugged,
“I had come here with a plan, a plan that would benefit you.”
“What plan?”
“Declare War on Aurendor.”
Nux spoke, and in an instant, the air around him changed. His jolly, laid-back face was nowhere to be seen.
“What...?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“I have long since declared War on them.”
She answered.
“War with that half-baked Faction of yours? You do realize what your situation is right now, correct?”
Nux countered.
Then suddenly, he waved his hand, and suddenly, another being Sharnoth recognized appeared next to him.
The Queen called out, her eyes glaring at the woman standing next to Nux.
“Lady Sharnoth, it has been a while.”
Maeve bowed her head, changing the way she addressed Sharnoth to ‘Lady Sharnoth’ instead of ‘Your Majesty’.
Sharnoth, however, continued to glare at her, something Maeve completely ignored.
“Maeve, tell us about the current situation and what’s the most logical step we can take in this situation.”
Nux ordered, and Maeve nodded.

“The Faction’s power is scattering. Lady Sharnoth is losing control over her people. Her people are scared. Her enemies are using this chance to strengthen themselves. The Council members can see how the situation is deteriorating and are panicking.
Lady Sharnoth’s decision to destroy Ravenhelm, Sevenruin, and Zarenal wasn’t correct either. It left too many openings and showed her desperation.
People are nervous, and we need to ease their nervousness. We need to regain control and stabilize our situation before any further damage.”
The Nocthari did what Nux ordered him to.
“And how do we do that?”
Nux questioned.
“Doing what Master suggested is one option. Declaring War on Aurendor would send out a public message that the situation is under control and we are prepared for war.
It would reassure not just our people but also confuse our enemies.
If we are fortunate, Vexarion Aurendor might see this as Lady Sharnoth’s desperate, weak action and use this opportunity to actually come forward and face her.
Lady Sharnoth uses the Power of Chaos. If he presents her to the Supreme Worlds, he will win their favor. We can use that greed to our advantage and kill him.”
Maeve declared, and in an instant, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
“We can... kill Vexarion?”

chapters.title: Chapter 2065: What are you doing here?
paragraphs: "Lady Sharnoth uses the Power of Chaos. If he presents her to the Supreme Worlds, he will win their favor. We can use that greed to our advantage and kill him."
Maeve declared, and in an instant, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
"We can... kill Vexarion?"
She spoke, her disbelief couldn’t be clearer. She looked pitiful, and how could she not—she was finally hearing words she wanted to hear for the past hundred thousand years.
"As I said, this is merely a possibility."
Maeve didn’t react to Sharnoth’s emotional reaction; she just stated in her deadpan tone.
"It would be better not to get our hop—"
However, before she could speak more,
"Alright, that is enough."
Nux ordered.
"Yes, Master."
Maeve bowed her head as she stepped back.
Nux then looked into Sharnoth’s eyes and,
"This was my plan to convince you."
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes.
"Before I get your help, I planned to help you. I plan on declaring war on Aurendor, this time, much more aggressively than before.
If Vexarion comes forward, we will get rid of him, but if he hides behind the Supreme Worlds, then we would have no choice but to wa—"
"You have my complete support, Nux Leander."
Sharnoth declared.
"I half-heartedly trusted your father before, but this time, I will put my complete faith in you.
The results do not matter, whether Vexarion faces me or runs to the Supreme Worlds. Once this is over,
I will be yours.
You can use me however you wish to."
"...you really shouldn’t say it like that, you know? You are making things difficult for me."
Nux complained.
"What do you mean?"
Sharnoth frowned, and Nux just shook his head.

"Anyways, I will be sending Maeve to you. There is no need to reveal that she tried to escape before. Use her to calm your Council, also reveal that you have finally negotiated with the Leander Family.
It is time for Khaemorr to strike back."
He declared, and Sharnoth nodded with a determined look on her face.
She didn’t even ask how Nux got his hands on Maeve.
Was she always on his side?
Honestly, Sharnoth did not care. She had no reason to, after all, even she was on his side now.
Nux waved his hand, and Maeve appeared in front of Sharnoth.
"Lady Sharnoth."
She bowed again.
Sharnoth nodded. Soon, however, her expression changed as she noticed something. Khaemorr’s Will couldn’t sense Maeve anymore. To Khaemorr, Maeve wasn’t even here.
It was just like how it reacted to Nux or his people.
’Is this why he is an Anomaly?’
Sharnoth wondered in her head, but before she could think anymore,
"Ah, right.
Have this too, almost forgot about them."
Nux spoke as he waved his hand again, and fourteen more unconscious beings appeared in front of Sharnoth—beings she recognized in an instant.

"These are who are left aside from Vexarion. Others are hidden or do not exist anymore. I have read their memories, but I can’t find others. It will be difficult to continue from there, especially because so many years have passed.
Have fun with them for a while. We will find more once we destroy Aurendor."
Nux spoke, reassuring the woman that this was just the beginning, and Sharnoth...
She stared into Nux’s eyes and,
"...thank you, Nux."
She bowed her head.
"Don’t thank me. I still haven’t done much.
The main culprit is still alive and well, isn’t he?"
Nux smiled, and at his words, Sharnoth’s expression turned serious, and she nodded.
"Well then, take care of the situation from your side. Once you are done, contact me and we will discuss our future action."
Nux muttered as he ended the call.
Once he was done, Aeliana, who had appeared next to him, smiled lightly,
"You are very cruel, husband."
"What do you mean?"
Nux spoke as he pulled the Vampire in his arms.
"You are laying such a vicious trap."
Aeliana complained, her fingers tracing through his back as she continued,
"She showed you her memories because she wanted you to trust her, but you are using those memories to press all the right buttons. You use your words to make yourself the only person she could trust.

You plan to make her rely on you to the point she would come to you before she takes even the smallest of decisions. The poor girl will grow so dependent that she wouldn’t even be able to imagine her life without you.
You will be the only thing she will see.
How so vicious.
How so... familiar."

Aeliana muttered as she looked into her husband’s eyes and pressed her breasts on his chest. Nux’s grin widened at that sight. Obviously, he did not ignore such heartless allegations—his hands had already moved inside Aeliana’s gown to punish her.
He pulled the Vampire even closer to him, so much that not even air could pass through them.
"Anh~"
The Vampire moaned, and just as she did, Nux grabbed her lips with his teeth and started sucking on them.
His canines then elongated and—
Pierce
He bit her lips.
As the husband and wife lost themselves in the Outer Space in the middle of nowhere, on the other side,
Everything in Khaemorr was changing.
The Council Meeting was called. By now, the Council Members had gotten used to urgent summons like this, it wasn’t even surprising anymore.
After all, the situation was just that dire.
But the moment the Council Members appeared in the Council Room, their expression changed.
"What are you doing here?"
Siara, the Elar’zhun, questioned as she glared at Maeve, who was sitting on her chair.
"Please be silent. The very fact I came here means I am not an enemy. Think log—"
"Of course you are not an enemy. You are not strong enough to call yourself our ’enemy’.
You are a traitor.
Nothing more, nothing less."
Siara declared, and the rest of the Council Members agreed. At her words, Maeve just sighed and closed her eyes. Her indifferent action annoyed the rest of the Council Members, but then,
"Sit down."
A command was heard.
The Queen was here, and this time, the air around her was much different than before.
The desperate little girl could no longer be seen. Sharnoth Nocthys had once again become the Queen she was born to be.

Once you are done, contact me and we will discuss our future action."
Nux muttered as he ended the call.
Once he was done, Aeliana, who had appeared next to him, smiled lightly,
"You are very cruel, husband."
"What do you mean?"
Nux spoke as he pulled the Vampire in his arms.
"You are laying such a vicious trap."
Aeliana complained, her fingers tracing through his back as she continued,
"She showed you her memories because she wanted you to trust her, but you are using those memories to press all the right buttons.
You use your words to make yourself the only person she could trust.
You plan to make her rely on you to the point she would come to you before she takes even the smallest of decisions.
The poor girl will grow so dependent that she wouldn’t even be able to imagine her life without you.
You will be the only thing she will see.
How so vicious.
How so... familiar."
Aeliana muttered as she looked into her husband’s eyes and pressed her breasts on his chest.
Nux’s grin widened at that sight.
Obviously, he did not ignore such heartless allegations—his hands had already moved inside Aeliana’s gown to punish her.
He pulled the Vampire even closer to him, so much that not even air could pass through them.
"Anh~"
The Vampire moaned, and just as she did, Nux grabbed her lips with his teeth and started sucking on them.
His canines then elongated and—
Pierce
He bit her lips.
As the husband and wife lost themselves in the Outer Space in the middle of nowhere, on the other side,
Everything in Khaemorr was changing.
The Council Meeting was called.
By now, the Council Members had gotten used to urgent summons like this, it wasn’t even surprising anymore.
After all, the situation was just that dire.
But the moment the Council Members appeared in the Council Room, their expression changed.
"What are you doing here?"
Siara, the Elar’zhun, questioned as she glared at Maeve, who was sitting on her chair.
"Please be silent.
The very fact I came here means I am not an enemy.
Think log—"
"Of course you are not an enemy.
You are not strong enough to call yourself our ’enemy’.
You are a traitor.
Nothing more, nothing less."
Siara declared, and the rest of the Council Members agreed.
At her words, Maeve just sighed and closed her eyes.
Her indifferent action annoyed the rest of the Council Members, but then,
"Sit down."
A command was heard.
The Queen was here, and this time, the air around her was much different than before.
The desperate little girl could no longer be seen.
Sharnoth Nocthys had once again become the Queen she was born to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 2066: Counterattack.
paragraphs: "Sit down."
Sharnoth ordered in an authoritative tone.
Everyone turned towards the Queen and their expressions changed. Their Queen looked... much calmer than before.
It looked like they were once again watching the Queen they had decided to follow.
"Lady Sharnoth."
Varys greeted. The rest of the Council Members followed and bowed their heads as well. Everyone settled down like they were told to; Siara was no exception.
By now, Sharnoth had arrived at the table and settled down as well.
She looked over at the Council Members—three of them were missing.

After Maeve left, two more had left just like her, and the rest didn’t stay out of loyalty either. Sharnoth killed the third Council Member who attempted to leave; the rest stayed out of fear. Most of them were waiting for the chance to get away.
If Sharnoth ordered them to use the Portal now, she was sure that every single one of them would take this chance to escape.
After all, they weren’t born to join her cause. They weren’t of her race, they weren’t her people—they joined her because she was strong, and it was convenient for them to be under her banner.
Yes, there was a trace of loyalty in them, there was a time where they might have given their life for their Queen.
But ultimately, all these beings belonged to the Faction of Darkness. They were inherently evil, their thoughts changed, their loyalties changed.
In face of certain defeat, they weren’t foolish enough to wait and give their lives.

Of course, Sharnoth was no exception either. She only recruited these people because they were capable. Loyalty was the least of her worries. After all, loyalty only came when she showed strength—when she stood tall as a reliable pillar.
And she was confident that she would be that pillar till she reached her goal.
Well, at least that was what she believed till that monster appeared.
Anyways, because all the Council Members wanted to leave, the Council’s efficiency dropped considerably. After all, Council Members had subordinates, who in turn had more subordinates.
The panic had started spreading. Being able to leave Khaemorr had become a way out of prison, and no one who got the opportunity to leave returned.
Because of this, Sharnoth had to restrict movements, and information could only be travelled through Call Artifacts.
"Lady Sharnoth."
Varys spoke as he noticed Sharnoth’s gaze. He was prepared with the day’s report. Yes, even though everything had become chaotic, he still kept everything in order from his end.
Sharnoth, however, raised her head.
She had no interest in knowing what worlds had declared neutrality and which ones had betrayed them and turned to Aurendor.
She would get all those reports later. For now, it was time for counterattack.
"Maeve."
She called out.
Maeve nodded, signaling that she was listening.
"Speak your mind."
Sharnoth ordered.

The order confused other Council Members. They all thought Sharnoth would explain why Maeve was actually here; some even believed that she brought her here to punish her and induce fear into the rest,
But...
To think she would allow her to ’speak her mind.’
Maeve wasn’t shocked either. The Nocthari knew she was one of the few people Sharnoth could trust. After all, her Master had ordered her to aid her as much as she could.
Right now, Sharnoth’s orders and well-being were above her own self.

"Aurendor dared to poach the worlds under our Faction. It is an offense that has turned our Faction into a joke. Other Factions have also started poaching worlds under our rule without fear, and if this continues, it will only be a matter of time before our Faction is destroyed.
This needs to stop now."
Maeve declared.
"And how do we do that, genius?"
Siara questioned in an annoyed tone.
She always hated how Maeve simply pointed at the problem without giving any solution, but this time—
"We will attack Aurendor’s five strongest subordinate worlds."
Maeve answered.
"What...?"
Siara’s expression changed.
"Do you even realize what you are saying...?"
She questioned with a shocked look on her face. This went against Supreme Worlds’ rules. They would be destroyed if they didn’t have a proper reason to explain their actio—
Wait...
Siara’s expression changed as she realized something.
She stared at Maeve with a shocked look on her face, and Maeve nodded.
"I know."
The Nocthari began.

"We will declare that Aurendor hired the Leander Family to destroy the worlds under our Faction so it could spread panic, and then sent their men to recruit other worlds under us in order to weaken us. This will give us enough reason to act."
"It is not a strong enough reason."
Varys shook his head.
"Hiring mercenaries for war doesn’t go against the rules."
"Then that’s even better, isn’t it?"
Maeve smiled.
"After all, we are going to hire mercenaries to do what we want as well."
"You want to hire mercenaries capable of destroying Middle Level Worlds?"
Varys narrowed his eyes.
Let’s not even talk about us being able to pay them—do mercenaries strong enough to do it without our direct support even exist?"
"Varys, were you not listening to what I just said? Aurendor hired mercenaries strong enough to do what we want them to do. How could they hire those who do not exist?"
Varys frowned at those words.
Siara, on the other hand, realized it.
"You... are you talking about the Leander Family?"
She questioned.
"That is correct. We will hire the Leander Family to destroy Aurendor’s five strongest subordinate Worlds."
Maeve nodded, and the rest of the Council Members just stared at the woman with deadpan looks on their faces.
"...have you lost your mind?"
One of the Council Members questioned.
Hire the Leander Family?
Wasn’t the entire problem they had been facing all this while because they couldn’t get their hands on the Leander Family?
If they could just ’hire’ them, why would they even go through so many troubles to begin with?
The Council Members turned towards Sharnoth. They wanted her to bash Maeve’s skull and destroy her existence, but suddenly,
"Does anyone wish to speak against this plan?"
The Queen questioned, and the Council Members...
They just...

chapters.title: Chapter 2067: The Leander Family will not dare to attack u—
paragraphs: "Report."
A tall being sitting on a throne with a leisurely, almost bored look on his face ordered.

He had golden-veined obsidian skin, glowing faintly as if there was molten stone beneath it. His eyes were hollow, like glass orbs refracting faint light. A thin, unbroken obsidian halo was floating behind his head like a divine mark. He wore silver armor, smooth and polished to a mirror-finish, layered with robes of ivory and gold.
The air around him radiated purity and justice,
Or at least... that should have been the case.
But...
Something about him was different from his people.
He was Vexarion Aurendor, the Sovereign of Aurendor and the being who called himself the Herald of Justice.
*Picture*
In front of him knelt another being with similar features as him; clearly, they belonged to the same race. His subordinate, however, did not have the halo hovering over his head.
The halo seemed like the mark of leadership,
The sign of absoluteness.
At Vexarion’s orders, his subordinate finally raised his head and began,

"The worlds under Khaemorr have started removing the Chaos Energy, making it difficult for our people to sneak in. Some of our subordinates were therefore caught. We have tried initiating negotiations to bring our people back, but we have not received any answers yet."
"What...?"
The instant he heard those words, Vexarion’s expression changed.
Other than a few minor inconveniences, everything had been going in his favor. This was also the reason he was so laid back till now,
But in just a few hours, this was the second bad news he had received.
"They removed the Chaos Energy...?"
He couldn’t believe it.
Why would they do it?
"Did they deal with the Leander Family?"
"There are no such reports yet. If they had, they would have announced it, considering how much damage they have taken."
Vexarion nodded.
He agreed with those words.
The Universe sees Khaemorr and its Faction as a joke. They have become easy targets everyone could pick on. With such operations, it was only a matter of time before their Faction was dissolved.
If Sharnoth had dealt with the Leander Family, she would have announced it that very instant in order to cut off her losses.
Then...
Does this mean whatever they were planning failed?

Honestly, when they came up with such a desperate countermeasure, he thought that they might have a plan against the Leander Family. After all, even he, Sharnoth’s long-standing enemy, did not know that the woman had the Power over Chaos.

Just this fact alone was more than enough for him to seek the Supreme Worlds’ aid against her. The only reason he hadn’t reported anything till now was because he wanted to capture Sharnoth on his own and deliver her to the Supreme Worlds himself.
After all, he would gain much more that way.
Who knows?
He might even become Light’s direct subordinate.
It was truly a one-in-a-billion-year opportunity, an opportunity he couldn’t give up on no matter what, even if it meant losing a few of his subordinates.

After all, their lives held no value in front of what he would gain if his plan came through. All he needed to do was express his grief for his fallen ’comrades’ and that would be enough. Even being present at their funeral would be an honor they usually would have never received.

But it was indeed surprising—to think even after showing her trump card and turning herself into nothing more than a shining target for the rest of the Universe, she still wasn’t able to get rid of the Leander Family. It was almost funny.
Vexarion felt embarrassed that he had been at a standstill against them for tens of thousands of years. It would have been much better if he had destroyed them before.
After all, a Faction that couldn’t even deal with a mere mercenary party—how could they possibly stand against him?
He was being overly cautious.
It was a mistake.
"What about the Leander Family? Did we receive any reply?"
He questioned.
"...we did not."
His subordinate shook his head with a hesitant look on his face. He knew this had become a triggering point for his Master. The Leander Family has been ignoring their summons as if they do not exist.
They weren’t putting them in their eyes at all, and it had become annoying, especially for someone like Vexarion, who had never been treated in this manner before.
"Heh."
At those words, Vexarion clenched his fists in anger. Soon, however, he controlled his expression and smiled gently and ’gracefully.’
"They are quite an odd bunch, aren’t they?"
He laughed politely.
The subordinate knew it was better to stay silent. He had no intention of losing his head.
"What about the Transcendents who disappeared a few hours ago? Did you find anything regarding the matter?"
"...no, we did not."
Once again, the subordinate shook his head, and Vexarion...
His ’gentle’ smile widened,
"You have become lethargic these days, haven’t you, Ythric? You should work on that, don’t you think? After all, sloth is a sin. If it spreads too far... I will have no choice but to purge you."
Ythric trembled.
Honestly, he wanted to mention a theory he had in his mind, but since he had no way to prove it, he didn’t dare to say it out loud.
After all, his Master wasn’t in his best mood right now.
Vexarion, who sensed his hesitation—
"Speak."
He ordered.
Ythric stared at him dubiously. Now that he was given permission, he somehow regained his confidence and,
"Before the Leander Family targeted Khaemorr and the worlds in its Faction, some of Khaemorr’s Transcendents had disappeared as well."
"Are you saying...?"

"It could just be a coincidence. This was also the reason I did not mention it—not till I had something more concrete. I tried contacting our spies in Khaemorr to learn more about the disappearance of their Transcendents, but the situation there is quite chaotic. Sharnoth is keeping an eye on everyone because of recent betrayals; they aren’t in a position to answer my questions."
Ythric answered.
"Cease the needless worry, the Leander Family will not dare to attack u—"
"Lord Vexarion!"
Before Vexarion could even complete his sentence, another subordinate barged in with a horrified look on his face and—
"I-It is the Leander Family!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2068: Knock Knock
paragraphs: "Cease the needless worry, the Leander Family will not dare to attack u—"
"Lord Vexarion!"
Before Vexarion could even complete his sentence, another subordinate barged in with a horrified look on his face and—
"I-It is the Leander Family!!"
Vexarion narrowed his eyes. Ythric, who saw his expression, knew that things wouldn’t end well for the new one.
What Vexarion hated the most was being interrupted, and to interrupt him in such a rude manner...
There was no way he would let this go.
Of course, before that, Vexarion would get all the value out of him,
"What is it?"
And just as Ythric expected, Vexarion questioned with a calm look on his face, not showing any signs of anger or frustration.
"T-The Leander Family!"
The new subordinate began with a stutter,
"Elythion, Vespera, Iridis, Eosphora, and Lumina, a-all five of them were destroyed by the Leander Family!"
"What!?"
Vexarion’s eyes widened in shock. The Halo above his head started flickering.
"Y-Yes!"
The subordinate nodded,
"We were contacted by Lumina, they sought our aide, but by the time we could even realize what happened, their Transcendent Leaders had all perished and they were then attacked by enemy worlds!
The same happened with the other four, just that the other four didn’t even get to contact us.
The only thing left behind in their land was the Leander Family Sigil!"
"...they dared to attack us?"
Vexarion couldn’t believe what he was hearing.
Ythric too, had frozen in fear. What he was dreading happened. The Leander Family... they were now working against them.
And to think they managed to crush their strongest subordinate worlds before they even had the chance to call for reinforcements.
Ythric’s body trembled.
He had met the leaders of those worlds more than once, he knew how strong they were. Honestly, every single one of them could easily crush him in a battle and yet...
To think they fell that quickly...
Just what kind of opponent did they face!?
He wondered in his head.
This was the most annoying part about facing the Leander Family. Nothing was known about them—who were they, where they came from, how strong they were, where is their current base—nothing.
They had no information about them.
It was like these people came out of nowhere and started terrorizing Factions that once ruled over the Universe.
It was horrifying how they cornered Khaemorr’s Faction and how they couldn’t do anything against them.
And now...
They were facing the same threat.
Ythric was scared.
Things were completely out of their control, and he did not like this feeling.

’Why!? Why suddenly change targets!? Did they make a deal with Khaemorr!? But how!? I have been trying to get in touch with them, but I haven’t gotten any answers yet. How did Khaemorr manage to contact them!?’
There were countless questions in his head.
And suddenly,
Knock Knock
Another knock was heard.
A knock, that for some reason, made Ythric feel uneasy. He turned towards the Gate, and from there, a slightly nervous voice was heard.
"Lord Justice, I bring news."
"Come in."
Vexarion ordered. Once again, Ythric could sense his annoyance.

This time, however, it wasn’t the man’s fault. He had followed the correct procedure—knocking and informing why he came here was indeed the standard and most nonthreatening way to address the situation,
It was just that...
In the current scenario, nothing worked.
Vexarion was already annoyed, no...
He was angry.
Of course, the subordinate did not know that. At his Lord’s command, he walked in and knelt, ready to report.
"Speak."
Vexarion ordered.
"Worlds from Khaemorr’s Faction that turned towards us no longer exist; they were devoured out of existence."
Vexarion clenched his fists.
He wanted to know who was behind it, but with the world wiped out of the Universe, there was no way to know anything.
Plus, if there was any information, he knew his subordinate would have reported it if he didn’t wish to die.
Honestly, there was no need to think about it.
Devouring the world without their leaders having the chance to call for reinforcements or even inform the allies...
There weren’t many forces who could do that.
Vexarion already had a name in his mind,
The Leander Family.
’It is them again.’
He was sure of it.
The air around him turned grimmer, his mind raced, trying to think of a way to counterattack in this situation, but then—
Knock Knock
Another knock was heard.
In an instant, the entire Hall turned dead silent. Vexarion and all his subordinates turned towards the Gate, prepared for another bad news.
And just as they expected,
"L-Lord Justice...
I bring news."
A nervous voice was heard.
Vexarion stared at Ythric, who prepared himself and ordered,
"Come in."
He had to give it all to not stutter like the rest of them. He could not show any weakness, not here, not in front of them.
Composure was important,
But...
"Khaemorr declared an all-out War on us."

The subordinate reported with a grim look on his face. Of course, this news itself wasn’t something big. They were already at war with Khaemorr—redeclaring war would normally have felt like nothing more than a desperate attempt to raise their own morale. It meant that the enemy was breaking; it was something to be celebrated.
But the very fact that the subordinate sounded this nervous while reporting the matter told Ythric that the news that the Leander Family was after them had already spread.
’To think that a mere mercenary party would have this much effect on the people of a High-Level World.’
It was absurd.
"What did they say?"
Ythric questioned.
He already had a rough idea in his head. The timing of everything was too synchronized for it to be just a coincidence, but somewhere in his head, he wanted it to be just that,
A coincidence.
But...
"They say that they do not desire pointless deaths.
They offer a direct Death Battle between Lord Justice and their Leader, Sharnoth Nocthys.
All of this would stop no matter the outcome of this battle."

"What!?"
Vexarion’s eyes widened in shock.

"Y-Yes!"
The subordinate nodded,

chapters.title: Chapter 2069: The Universe is watching
paragraphs: "They say that they do not desire pointless deaths,
They offer a direct Death Battle between Lord Justice and their Leader, Sharnoth Nocthys.
All of this would stop no matter the outcome of this battle."
The subordinate spoke as he extended his hands holding the official statement of Khaemorr.
And at his words, Ythric’s face turned solemn.
Just as he expected, it was all connected.
He looked at Vexarion, wanting his permission. Vexarion, knowing what he wanted, nodded, and with a wave of his hand, Ythric made Khaemorr’s statement float into his hands.
He quickly opened the scroll and started reading.
’We do not seek needless bloodshed.
To preserve what remains of peace, we offer a Death Duel—between Lady Sharnoth Nocthys and the so-called Herald of Justice, Vexarion Aurendor.
One battle.
One outcome.
Let this war end with dignity, rather than slaughter.
Regardless of the outcome, all hostilities shall cease.
To honor your values and traditions, we leave the structure of the accord to Aurendor’s discretion, believing you will honor it with fairness that the Herald of Justice is revered for.

Know this: should this proposal be declined, history will not look kindly upon the path that follows. The Universe is watching—and it will remember not only the victor, but those who turned away from the chance to prevent further deaths.
We shall await your reply with patience.
For two days, our blades shall rest, our forces shall hold. No blood shall fall—not by our hand. Let this interval be a testament to the sincerity of our offer, and to the choice now set before you.
Let it not be said, in days to come, that no path was offered. Nor that it was we who turned from it.’
Ythric’s face turned solemn as he read the content. He glanced at Vexarion, telling him that he should read it.
Vexarion nodded, and with a wave of his hand, the scroll appeared in his hand.
The moment he read the content, just like Ythric’s, his face turned solemn as well.
’Regardless of the outcome, all hostilities shall cease.’
These words were more than enough for Vexarion to know this: even though there was no official declaration, it was clear that Khaemorr wanted them to know the Leander Family was now on their side.
And...
’The Universe is watching—and it will remember not only the victor, but those who turned away from the chance to prevent further deaths.’
It was a direct threat.
Those bastards plan to pin all deaths after this on them.

If Aurendor did not accept this, the consequences would be on them. After all, no matter what, at the end of the day, they were part of the Light Faction. If that wasn’t the case, the deaths wouldn’t have mattered—the Darkness Faction would have actually preferred if there were more deaths.
But...
They were the ’good’ people; they cannot take the blame for all these deaths.
Of course, Aurendor could still decide to ignore the threat and continue the War as they have till now,
Or at least... that was what they could have done before.
After all, the Worlds in their Factions were strong—even if the War continued, they wouldn’t fall.

Their reputation wouldn’t fall either since the worlds from Aurendor Faction could easily release a statement saying they wished to participate in the battle for Justice’s sake and wished to fight for the cause and whatnot.
But now, things were different.
With the Leander Family in the mix,
Protecting their subordinate worlds wouldn’t be easy—even their strongest worlds fell without putting up any resistance.
The rest wouldn’t be any different either.

If what happened with Khaemorr happened with them too, controlling the worlds under them would become impossible. If the Leander Family started targeting all the worlds that released the official statements and showed the intent of participating in the War,
Making other worlds release the same statement wouldn’t be an option anymore.
It would no longer be the fight for Justice or for a cause; it would simply be a one-sided massacre.
A massacre that Aurendor allowed by not accepting Khaemorr’s offer.
They would be framed as Cowards.
The reputation they have built after millions of years of work would crumble and be smeared to dust.
It wouldn’t be surprising if they were kicked out of the Light Faction, and no other Supreme Faction would then take them in, since no one would want others’ leftovers.
Once that happened and Aurendor lost Supreme World’s support, they would become an open target for the rest of the Universe—it would truly mark the end of Aurendor and Vexarion.
Vexarion clenched his fists.
Just yesterday, everything was under his complete control. He actually thought it was a pity that he didn’t take out Khaemorr a lot sooner than this. He thought it was a done battle, and yet now...
He was being forced to play the move Khaemorr had been wanting him to play all this while.
A direct battle with Sharnoth Nocthys.
Direct battles were something Vexarion usually avoided. He was a wary being, and he knew his Faction was strong; he had always used that to his advantage.
But now...
Things have turned around,
And the only way to avoid the outcome Khaemorr wanted was to appeal to the Supreme World of Light, tell them that Sharnoth possesses the Energy of Chaos, and let them take care of it.
That, however, would not only take away his opportunity to be rewarded by the Supreme World of Light, it would also deem him useless, making it difficult for him to make any further impression.
’Tsk.’
Vexarion snorted, his frustration couldn’t be clearer. The lack of options annoyed him.
’How did they get in touch with the Leander Family!?’
He screamed inwardly.
It all happened because of those bastards!
If only they hadn’t acted!
Or better, if only they had contacted him first!
It would have been much different then; he could have given them whatever they desired and got them to his side,
If...
If only they had contacted him first—no, if only they had contacted him at all! He was sure he could get them on his side.
"Lord Justice."
Suddenly, Ythric called out.
"What is it...?"
Vexarion questioned as he glanced at Ythric, who had taken out a buzzing Call Artifact,
"I-It is the channel I gave to the Leander Family...
T-They are contacting us!"
Ythric reported, and in an instant, Vexarion’s expression changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2070: Damn, you people really are desperate, aren’t you?
paragraphs: "I-It is the channel I gave to the Leander Family...
T-They are contacting us!"
Ythric reported, and in an instant, Vexarion’s expression changed.
"What are you waiting for!? Pick it up."
He ordered, but before Ythric could do anything, Vexarion waved his hand in excitement. The Call Artifact moved towards him, and he picked it up.

With the call connected, Vexarion’s eyes fell on a being with long black hair, horns, purple eyes, and a devilishly attractive face. The being wore black robes that had the Leander Family Sigil imprinted on its chest, and as the being’s eyes fell on Vexarion, he smirked playfully.
"Vexarion Aurendor, we finally meet."
The Devil greeted.
At his words, however, Vexarion’s mouth twitched. He did not like how a mere mercenary called him by his name. For now, however, he contained his emotions and,
"Are you the Leader of the Leander Family?"
He questioned.
"Leader? Did you not hear our name? We are a Family. A Family has no Leader."
"...Do you speak on behalf of the Leander Family or not?"
Vexarion questioned directly. He clearly had no interest in his family dynamics.
"Is your sight just as bad as your hearing? Do you not see this?
Plus, I contacted you through the channel you people gave to the Leander Family, did I not?
What sort of question is that?"
The Devil questioned, pointing at the Sigil imprinted on his chest.
"How is someone like you the Leader of a High-Level World?"
He questioned.
And in Vexarion’s Hall, a heavy silence descended.
Every being who heard those words took in a deep breath as their hearts froze.
This...
Was this man... insulting their Lord?
They couldn’t believe it.
Something like this has never happened before; none of them could see it happen even in their wildest dreams.
Crack
Ythric heard a voice, and he quickly noticed that Vexarion’s Throne’s armrest was broken. He was angry—no, that was an understatement.
He was extremely angry.
And what’s worse?
Vexarion had no other choice but to continue the conversation.

After all, the Leander Family was just that important. If they could just get them on their side, all their problems would be solved. They would be able to corner Sharnoth, defeat her, and then present her to the Supreme World of Light, gaining their favor.
Vexarion could see the bigger picture as well.
He knew he needed to take it in.
Once he had the Supreme World of Light’s favor, taking care of some mere mercenaries wouldn’t be an issue.
Yes, that was it.
He needed to be patient right now. He would deal with this bastard later.
"The channel was released publicly. Even though it was meant to be for the Leander Family, anyone could use it. So I need to make sur—"
He tried to explain as calmly as possible.
"Right, that makes sense."
Nux nodded at his words, interrupting him mid-sentence.
Vexarion, once again, controlled himself and tried to nod in agreement, but then—
"So? What’s your grand solution?"
Nux questioned.
He looked into Vexarion’s eyes and,
"Let’s say I was someone impersonating the Leander Family. How are you going to find out the truth?"
Vexarion turned silent.
"Come on, Genius.
I am waiting for your answer.
You do not know the Leander Family. You do not even know the number of members we have, nor how strong our members are.
You do not know where our base is. You do not know what race we are of.
How will you prove anything?
Hmmm?"
Nux questioned, and Vexarion...
He had no way to answer his question.
What he did know, however, was that this bastard was extremely annoying. He was trying to remain patient, to not lose his calm and get what he wants, but—
"Hmm? Hmmm? Hmmmmmm?
What are you going to do, Vexarion Aurendor? You must have a way, do you not?"
Annoying.
Extremely annoying!
Vexarion’s mouth continued to twitch. Ythric, who knew his Lord was about to lose it, quickly waved his hand, and the Call Artifact floated towards him.
Vexarion glared at Ythric, who simply nodded reassuringly and—
’My Lord has no reason to lower himself and converse with a mere mercenary. Let me do it.’
He spoke using the Energy that connected him with Vexarion. Those words calmed Vexarion. Plus, he still had not forgotten how important this actually was.
It was better to let Ythric handle it than to lose his calm and affect the negotiation here.
Seeing that Vexarion had closed his eyes, Ythric saw it as a sign and sighed inwardly.
"Ythric Vaasium."
Suddenly, Ythric heard a voice.
He turned towards Nux, a little taken aback.
"You know me."
"Of course I do. Unlike your lot, we do our research."
Nux answered with a light smirk. A smirk that was enough for Ythric to realize it.
This man... he was looking down on him.
No, not just him—he was looking down on his entire World.
Just... how arrogant does one have to be to look down on an entire World?
What sort of ridiculous being were they dealing with?
Of course, unlike Vexarion, Ythric did not lose his calm. Rather, he smiled and,
"That is good. The more competent you are, the better it is for me."
He smiled.
"Damn, you people really are desperate, aren’t you?"
Nux laughed.
His mockful words tore through every Aurendorian’s hearts.
It was... humiliating.
Even Ythric was losing his patience, but—
"We would rather not use our final card to deal with the situation. It would cause too much unnecessary destruction and death, and as beings of light, we would like to avoid that."
He answered, showing that he didn’t actually need the Leander Family—they weren’t desperate.
But—
"I thought Khaemorr gave a way out?"
Nux suddenly frowned.
"Didn’t they offer a one-on-one battle to avoid any unnecessary deaths? What could be a better solution than that?
As ’beings of light’, should you not go with that option?"
He questioned with a light smile on his face, and Ythric’s face turned solemn.

You do not know what race we are of.
How will you prove anything?
Hmmm?"
Nux questioned, and Vexarion...
He had no way to answer his question.
What he did know, however, was that this bastard was extremely annoying.
He was trying to remain patient, to not lose his calm and get what he wants, but—
"Hmm?
Hmmm?
Hmmmmmm?
What are you going to do, Vexarion Aurendor?
You must have a way, do you not?"
Annoying.
Extremely annoying!
Vexarion’s mouth continued to twitch.
Ythric, who knew his Lord was about to lose it, quickly waved his hand, and the Call Artifact floated towards him.
Vexarion glared at Ythric, who simply nodded reassuringly and—
’My Lord has no reason to lower himself and converse with a mere mercenary.
Let me do it.’
He spoke using the Energy that connected him with Vexarion.
Those words calmed Vexarion.
Plus, he still had not forgotten how important this actually was.
It was better to let Ythric handle it than to lose his calm and affect the negotiation here.
Seeing that Vexarion had closed his eyes, Ythric saw it as a sign and sighed inwardly.
"Ythric Vaasium."
Suddenly, Ythric heard a voice.
He turned towards Nux, a little taken aback.
"You know me."
"Of course I do.
Unlike your lot, we do our research."
Nux answered with a light smirk.
A smirk that was enough for Ythric to realize it.
This man... he was looking down on him.
No, not just him—he was looking down on his entire World.
Just... how arrogant does one have to be to look down on an entire World?
What sort of ridiculous being were they dealing with?
Of course, unlike Vexarion, Ythric did not lose his calm.
Rather, he smiled and,
"That is good.
The more competent you are, the better it is for me."
He smiled.
"Damn, you people really are desperate, aren’t you?"
Nux laughed.
His mockful words tore through every Aurendorian’s hearts.
It was... humiliating.
Even Ythric was losing his patience, but—
"We would rather not use our final card to deal with the situation.
It would cause too much unnecessary destruction and death, and as beings of light, we would like to avoid that."
He answered, showing that he didn’t actually need the Leander Family—they weren’t desperate.
But—
"I thought Khaemorr gave a way out?"
Nux suddenly frowned.
"Didn’t they offer a one-on-one battle to avoid any unnecessary deaths?
What could be a better solution than that?
As ’beings of light’, should you not go with that option?"
He questioned with a light smile on his face, and Ythric’s face turned solemn.

chapters.title: Chapter 2071: The current you is... running towards your own end.
paragraphs: "Didn’t they offer a one-on-one battle to avoid any unnecessary deaths? What could be a better solution than that?
As ’beings of light’, should you not go with that option?"
He questioned with a light smile on his face, and Ythric’s face turned solemn.
"What’s with that face? Did you truly think I would not know about Khaemorr’s offer? That was their official statement, every single being in the Universe knows about it."
"Their statement has no value."
Ythric shook his head.
"They are from the Darkness Faction, they have no reason to care about death and destruction. For them, the more death and destruction they cause, the better it is for them.
If such beings suddenly start talking about how they worry about death and destruction, one would be a fool to blindly believe their words.
They are planning something evil, and we, as the defenders of Light, cannot fall for their trap."
It was a very political answer; at the very least, this answer was capable of protecting Aurendor’s reputation.
But...
"To me, it just sounds like your Lord is scared."
Nux shrugged, his words once again triggering Vexarion.
"There is a difference between being scared and cautious."
Ythric answered calmly.
"Cowards are cautious."
Nux answered.
"Thoughts like,
’I shouldn’t break through, my energy might deviate and I might die.’
’I shouldn’t meet him, he might betray me.’
Or...
’I shouldn’t fight, the opponent might have set up a trap.’
Sure, to someone, all this may sound cautious, but to most, this is simply cowardly. You beings of light always talk about justice, life, and everyone’s right to live,
Yet, when you are given the opportunity to actually prevent billions of deaths, you worry about all this being a trap. It honestly confuses me."

"There is nothing to be confused about. Even if our Lord takes the risks to protect all those lives, the beings of darkness have no reason to stick to their words. Who is going to stop them if our Lord falls for their trap and loses his life?"
Ythric countered, and Nux just shrugged at his words,
"If you are already thinking about losing when the battle hasn’t even started yet, then that is all I wish to know."
He then heaved a big sigh and,
"Forget it, I was at fault for expecting something. I should have known better, there was a reason your Faction’s ranked at the level it is."
"What did you say?"
Suddenly, Ythric reacted.
Ythric was much better at controlling his emotions when compared to his Lord. However, as one of the strongest Transcendents in Aurendor, even he had his pride.
Being judged by a mere mercenary in such a condescending manner— even he had reached his limit.
Nux, however, wasn’t taken aback by his reaction.
As he said, he had done his research. He knew every single thing about the people he was dealing with. He knew exactly what to say to trigger them, and knowing that it was working, he continued,

"The only significant battle you have won is against Nocthys, that too, when you took out their Sovereign in a cowardly manner. You had the support of five other Eternals, and even when you had such a big advantage, you still couldn’t complete what you started and allowed someone like Sharnoth to escape.

Someone who has now become a thorn in the eyes of Light. Her mere existence is proof that your sole victory against the Faction of Darkness was pointless. Your mistake gave birth to a new, stronger enemy.
An enemy who was once a helpless little girl, yet now stands in front of you, challenging you to a direct duel, yet you cower behind your forc—"
Bam
"I am not cowering!"
Vexarion raised his voice as he slammed his armrest, the entire thing broken into pieces because of the impact.
The Call Artifact once again hovered in the air, showing Vexarion, who now stared at Nux with unhidden anger.
Of course, Nux was unaffected. Rather, inwardly, he was smiling—this was just going exactly as he had planned.
"Vexarion Aurendor, what you say does not matter.
The entire Universe will see your actions as cowardice, and that is not even the worst part."
Nux then paused for a moment before his smile became demonic and,
"Do you know what’s the worst part?
No one will be surprised by your cowardly decision."
Vexarion’s expression changed, and Nux continued,
"Every being in the Universe, especially those who are part of the Faction of Light, are waiting for you to show your cowardly side.

The moment you cave in, allowing Khaemorr to make their move, they will come forward. They will challenge Sharnoth in your stead with the same conditions she presented to you, defeat her, and take the glory you have been saving for yourself.

Some of the Worlds I am in contact with have already started preparing. Many have approached me, wanting me to tell them everything I know about Sharnoth. This was also the reason I came to find out about the official statement they released."
"Lies! You are lying!"
Vexarion shouted.
"Huh? What reason do I have to lie?"
"You are on Sharnoth’s side! Do you think I do not know that!? Your people destroyed five of my subordinate worlds!"
The Herald of Justice snapped. His current appearance was truly... ugly.
And Nux,
He just tilted his head in confusion.
"My people destroyed five of your subordinate worlds?"
"Do not try to lie your way through it, Mercenary. Your sigil was used."
Vexarion spoke in an authoritative tone, but Nux just shook his head,
"That is just a lie.
My people did not destroy five, we destroyed a total of eighteen Aurendor subordinate worlds."
He clarified.
"But this does not mean we are on Khaemorr’s side. If you are considering this as a factor, then I destroyed hundreds of Worlds under Khaemorr’s Faction."
"That may be true,"
Suddenly, Ythric spoke up.
"Your people have been destroying ten Khaemorr Worlds every single day, but today, I have not received such reports. It could only mean—"
"It means we have stopped our attacks against Khaemorr because we got what we wanted. There is nothing more to it.
Do not forget,
I am a mercenary. I work for profit, not out of personal feelings."
Nux answered, and Ythric smiled. This was exactly what he wanted to hear,
"And because of that, we want you to work for us."
He offered.
"If it is profit you want, I am sure we can provide you whatever you want."
"I did contact you because that was what I had in mind, but seeing your current condition, I have changed my mind.
You do not have what it takes to make a deal with me.
I would rather ally myself with the young girl whom you allowed to escape.
The current you is... running towards your own end."
Nux declared, and Vexarion’s expression changed.
"...what did you say?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2072: I have a way.
paragraphs: "The current you is... running towards your own end."
Nux declared with a cold look on his face. It looked like he was looking at a living corpse, and the Herald of Justice did not like that expression one bit.
"...what did you say?"
He questioned as he narrowed his eyes threateningly.

Yes, Aurendor’s Lord Justice was losing his patience. If this continued, Vexarion knew that the fact that Nux represented the Leander Family and that Aurendor needed their help would no longer matter to him.
He would mark this bastard and get rid of him even if it was the last thing he did.
To not incur his wrath, Nux needed to be very careful with his next words.
But...
"I said that the current you is running towards your end."
Nux repeated himself without an inch of fear in his eyes, and before Vexarion could react to his words and lose his temper,
"Do not think your eyes scare me, Vexarion. I am not one of the subordinates who follow you. Your presence does not mean anything to me.
Not to mention that if you do not get your act together, you will no longer have the luxury to try and find me."
Vexarion’s face turned solemn at those words. Nux, on the other hand, raised two fingers.
"Two days."
He began.
"These two days Sharnoth gave you are all you have, Vexarion. Once these two days pass and you decide to hide behind your Faction instead of coming out and facing Sharnoth yourself,
It will be over.
Other High Level Worlds will take this chance and deliver the Heir to Chaos to the Supreme Worlds."
Vexarion’s eyes widened in surprise as he heard those words. An expression that Nux did not miss,
"What? You did not believe that this news was only known to you, did you?"
He questioned.
"Luxmire, Dawnspire, Radiance, Sunder—these so-called allies of yours have already contacted me, and all of them know about Sharnoth’s origin.

And these are the worlds that only I know about. I can confidently say there are more. Even the worlds from the Eternity or the Balance Faction are keeping an eye on this situation. It wouldn’t be surprising if even the Worlds from the Darkness Faction, Khaemorr’s so-called allies, make a move as well.
The power Sharnoth used against the Leander Family was something most of the High Level Worlds recognized, and none of them plan to let this opportunity go.

The only reason they haven’t made a move is because of Khaemorr’s ongoing war with Aurendor, but the moment you back down from the Death Battle she proposed, you will give enough reason for them to take what belonged to you, and no matter who takes this chance away from you,

You, as the one who gave it away, would become a target in the eyes of the rest. Worlds from the Faction of Darkness might even target you then and there by taking in Khaemorr after Sharnoth’s disappearance and continuing their war.
You will be surrounded, your allies will shun and isolate you, your trade contracts with other Worlds will be annulled, and it wouldn’t be long before you are swallowed."
Nux explained with a cold look on his face, and every word he said shuddered Vexarion’s very being.
Not just Vexarion—Ythric, the usually calmer one, was frozen as well. The rest of the subordinates had trembled in fear. In their minds, they had already started making plans for their own survival.
And clearly, their plans did not involve being loyal to Vexarion.
Nux, on the other hand, turned towards Ythric and,
"Do you still think I would gain profit by making a deal with you?"

Ythric’s body trembled at that question. For a moment, he stayed silent, but the very fact that Nux was still here told him that there was still a reason for it. Ythric took a while and started thinking, then,
"...what do you need?"
He questioned directly—a question that surprised not just Nux but even Vexarion.
"You say all that, yet you still remain here, talking to us. There must be something in your mind, no? A possible way out, a solution, or maybe something else, no?"

He asked, and for a moment, Vexarion shook his head. What could a mere mercenary possibly offer when even he was out of options? He believed that Ythric was trying to hold off the weak straws in desperation and fear of drowning.
But then,
"My price isn’t cheap."
Nux grinned, instantly attracting Vexarion’s attention.
"You have a way out?"
Ythric questioned. It was a long shot—even he did not think it would work.
"As I said, my price is not cheap."
"Price does not matter. What plan do you have?"
"Accept the Death Match, kill or capture Sharnoth alive, and offer her to the Supreme World of Light in return for rewards."
Nux answered confidently, and in an instant, Vexarion lost all hope. Ythric too was visibly disappointed.
"If accepting the Death Match was an option, there wouldn’t have been all this discussion. As I mentioned before, Khaemorr cannot be trusted. This is all a tra—"
Ythric tried to deny it by giving the same reason again, but,
"Cut the bullshit."
Nux interrupted, slightly annoyed.
Ythric was momentarily taken aback, and Nux continued,
"The real reason you do not wish to accept the death match is because you are afraid of facing Sharnoth."
"That is not—"

"There is no point in lying to me. As I said, unlike you people, I did my research. I know everything about you and your Lord Justice. I know how you fight, I know how strong you are, and I know how you avoid direct confrontation."
"No—"
"I am not condemning you. Your method may be cowardly, but cowards are the ones who live the longest, and in this Universe, that is all that matters.
I actually like cowards and their cautious approach, and since I am taking the risk of making a deal with you, I obviously do not want you to perish in the battle."
Nux spoke as he leaned forward, and a demonic grin appeared on his face,
"I have a way."
He spoke,
"A sure-shot way to win and put an end to the arrogant Sharnoth once and for all."
