"They are the people I fight for, people I could do anything for, people I wish to spend the rest of Eternity with.
She is..."
One by one, Nux started introducing all his wives.
The smile on his face when he talked about them was so pure that it felt like his previous frown was just an illusion.
In her mind, Sharnoth felt like every time she saw this man smile, it was merely an act, because none of his smiles ever got close to what she was seeing right now.
It stirred a... strange emotion inside her.
She felt... jealous?
Of course, as soon as that thought appeared, she suppressed it in an instant and greeted those women politely.
The women smiled at her, especially the white-haired succubus.
She... she was looking at her with a strange smile on her face.
Almost as if... she was looking at prey.
It made Sharnoth feel somewhat uncomfortable, but she didn’t say anything out loud and decided to ignore her for now.
Seeing her reaction, Allura just chuckled.
She gently patted her belly without saying anything else.
"Now, the one who said there is a way to kill Vexarion—this is Amaya.
She is my little strategist, someone I can trust with my eyes closed."
Nux introduced with a big smile, oblivious to the little exchange between Sharnoth and his Allura.
His focus was on Amaya.
The devourer, however, stared at him and spoke directly,
"As I was saying, I have a way to kill him, but you will not like it."
"What?
Why?"
Nux frowned.
"It will be painless."
Amaya shrugged.
She knew her man.
She knew what he was planning.
The last thing in Nux’s mind was giving Vexarion an easy death.
Knowing Nux, this was actually a gift to Vexarion, not a punishment.
And just as Amaya thought, the instant he heard those words, Nux scowled, even more than Sharnoth herself.
It was almost as if he wanted to torture that bastard more than Sharnoth.
"What is the way?"
Unable to control herself, Sharnoth questioned, looking at Amaya.
She had noticed the woman glaring at her before, as if she was her most hated enemy.
She did not understand why, but for now, she knew she needed to focus on what was more important.
"We can use the Universe."
Amaya answered, looking at Nux, knowing that he would understand what she was talking about.
After all, they had done this before.
"Using the Universe...?"
Of course, Sharnoth had no clue what the woman was talking about.
"Do you think it would work?"
Nux questioned.
"The Universe is angry because it was fooled, wasn’t it?
If we act quickly enough, we can use that anger and direct it towards Aurendor."
Amaya answered.
"It could work... but there is no guarantee that Vexarion will die."
Nux muttered, nodding at her words.
"Isn’t that even better?
With Aurendor gone, he would no longer have the shell to hide in.
We can then do whatever we desire."
A smile appeared on Nux’s face when he heard those words.
"But this means we would be leaving it to chance, and we stand at the lower side of the probability.
It is much more likely that he will die painlessly."
Amaya explained, and honestly, Nux wasn’t very fond of the idea.
It left things to luck, and considering everything that had been happening, Lady Luck wasn’t exactly on his side.
While the two conversed, Sharnoth stared at them in silence.
She felt... alienated.
Like she wasn’t part of the discussion.

The distance between Nux and her felt larger than usual, and for some reason, every time she stared at the woman named Amaya, she had this strange feeling that the woman knew exactly what she was feeling and was enjoying it.
Almost as if... she was making a statement.
It was quite confusing, especially considering Sharnoth had never felt like this before.
"We need something else..."
And again, while Sharnoth explored all these new, frustrating emotions, Nux muttered out loud, lowering his head.
He needed a better plan.
"What if we try and buy more time?"
Suddenly, Melia spoke up.
"Hmm?"
Nux turned towards her and the Vampire continued,
"We can destroy Nexus and the Fortune’s Call.
That should buy us some time."
"But that will only bring more focus to Mercenary Guilds present in Nexus.
It wouldn’t be long before information that the Fortune’s Call had was extracted.
This might actually hasten the entire process."
Ember shook her head.
Melia thought about it for a moment, then,
"Let’s become terrorists."
The Vampire suggested.

chapters.title: Chapter 2081: The Plan.
paragraphs: "Let’s become terrorists."
The Vampire suggested.
"What...?"
Ember blinked in surprise, unable to understand what she was talking about.
"An Anti-Supreme Group."
Melia began.

"A group whose sole purpose is to eradicate the rule of the Supreme Worlds. A group that will show resistance to every single decision made by the Supreme Worlds. A group that will commit terror attacks to oppose them."
"...how is that going to help us?"
The Dragon questioned.

"The Supreme Worlds have ordered the Mercenary Worlds to do their bidding, correct? The Anti-Supreme Group will destroy some of the most renowned Mercenary Worlds to announce to the Universe that they now stand against the Supreme Worlds and that everyone who aligns themselves with the Supreme Worlds will meet their end by our hands.
And of course, during this announcement and showmanship, it wouldn’t be very surprising if a Mercenary World like Nexus is targeted and destroyed, now would it?"
The Vampire explained and in an instant, the other eyes present here shined.
This... could be done.

Destroying Nexus alone would directly pull all attention towards it, but destroying several other groups and introducing a new organization would definitely cause enough distraction. At the very least, the investigation would be delayed by a few days, giving them the chance to get rid of Vexarion.
"But would Vexarion accept the battle after everything that’s happening?"
Suddenly, Lyriana asked another question.

"Why would he not? The Supreme Worlds’ announcement doesn’t change anything, does it? It is completely unrelated to everything happening between Khaemorr and Aurendor. If anything, their active participation might urge Vexarion to step forward and prove his worth to the Supreme Worlds when they are watching."
Riona commented.
"I agree."
Thyra nodded as well. The cat then pointed at Sharnoth and—

"Even she didn’t seem particularly bothered by their announcement until she realized it was connected to us. Vexarion won’t be an exception, he must be too busy thinking about how he is going to reap the rewards after killing her.
Not to mention he has already given seven high-level relics in exchange for this. Didn’t he only have twelve relics in total?
Someone as greedy as him would never back down when he gave up more than half of his wealth for this."
She added, getting nods from the rest.
Yes, this indeed seemed like it was going to work. They simply needed to destroy enough Mercenary Worlds to cause confusion and terror.
Yes, the Supreme Worlds will take action against them, but that was bound to happen one day anyways. It doesn’t matter if it happens a little earlier than they had planned.
"Alright then,
It is decided."
Nux nodded as well.
He glanced at Sharnoth, who looked at him with a determined look on her face. He smiled and nodded at her, the Queen nodded back.
"If there is anything I can do, please, do not hesitate to say the word. I will do whatever you want me to, even if it means I have to give away my life for it."
"Giving your life away? Don’t you first want to get your revenge?"
Nux chuckled.
A complicated look appeared on her face when he said those words,
"...you have already done so much for me. I trust that if something happens to me, you will take my revenge in my place.
I just wish that if the situation comes down to it, you make his end as agony-filled as possible."
She declared, once again finding the will to follow through with her words and laying down her life for him.
"Woman, stop raising flags when they are not necessary."
"Flags...?"
Sharnoth frowned. She had no clue what he was talking about.
Nux just stared at her and sighed,
"I would very much prefer you to be alive for my own selfish reason,
So don’t you dare die on me, or I will do unthinkable things to your dead body."
"W-What...?"
The Queen stuttered, taken aback by those words. Even the wives stared at their husband with strange looks on their faces when they heard those words.
"Dead body huh...
That sounds fun~"
Only Edda was brave enough to truly accept this, and Nux, who saw their reaction, quickly calmed them down,
"It was a joke, women."
He even specifically looked at Edda and,
"Just a joke."
He repeated, making sure the woman didn’t get any ideas.
Yes, even he was scared of his Edda.
"Anyways,"
Nux shook his head and turned towards Sharnoth,
"Don’t die."
He commanded.
The Queen nodded,
"Now let’s come up with a detailed plan and take action."
Nux announced and the rest of the women nodded,
And just then—
"Nux."
Amaya called out.
"I have a plan.
Something better than this."
The Devourer announced.
"What is it?"
Nux questioned and as he did, the Devourer stared at Sharnoth and... smirked.
As the Supreme Worlds’ announcement spread throughout the Universe, every Mercenary World panicked.

Even the strongest Mercenary Worlds were only Middle-Level Worlds, so the recent Universe’s Reaction had done a considerable amount of damage in these worlds. The World Stabilizing Artifacts that they had prepared were rendered useless. Because of this, things were already extremely chaotic as almost all the buildings had collapsed, giving headaches to the higher-ups.
However, things became even messier after the Supreme Worlds’ announcement. After all, the strongest in the Universe were directly addressing them and had given them an ultimatum.

It meant that they not only had to deal with the deaths and destruction caused by the Universe’s reaction, they also had to gather all the information the Supreme Worlds had requested and report it to them.
What’s even worse?

The required information was related to the Black Mission that had stained almost every single Mercenary Guild’s reputation. A mission that no one dared to take, and those who did—their Mercenary Guilds made sure to hide that information so as not to incur the Supreme Worlds’ wrath.
After all, failure in this mission meant that they would be raising its difficulty even further. No Mercenary Guild wanted others to know that they did it.

And of course, now that the Supreme Worlds had personally summoned the Mercenary World Leaders to give the report, it meant that these leaders had no choice but to find out information that had been hidden for tens of thousands of years.
And no, it wasn’t an easy task. After all, most mercenaries were at Sovereign Stage with lifespans of around ten thousand years. The employees working at Mercenary Halls weren’t any different.
If the information was hidden, it meant there were no written documents of it. It could only be extracted through testimonies but...
How was one supposed to get testimonies from employees who died thousands of years ago?

It was an incredibly difficult task that required extensive search. For the Mercenary Halls that were known for their disorganization and messy state, this was even more difficult. It was almost an impossible task.
What’s worse?
This task needed to be done in less than a day so that leaders could leave and submit these reports before the required time.

Every single Mercenary World was in chaos, so much that no new mercenary missions were being taken or submitted. These worlds had stopped functioning entirely without exception and every mercenary employee was busy collecting information regarding the Black Mission.

The streets of these worlds were filled with crime. With leaders all busy, no one regulated the mercenaries—murder and rape became commonplace. Within just a few hours of the Supreme Worlds’ announcement, things had deteriorated for the worse.
Of course, Nexus was no different.
The Middle-Level Mercenary World was the same. Inside one of its Mercenary Guilds known as the Fortune’s Call,
A woman barged into her superior’s office with a big file in her hand and—
"Lord Simba..."
She called out.
In front of her sat an exhausted-looking being with the giant head of a lion. Yes, he was Simba. The once strong-looking Primordial now looked weak.
Not because Primordials didn’t feel much these days, just that... he was too exhausted.
He was honestly losing his mind. However, when the man’s eyes fell on the three-eyed, orange-skinned woman who had walked in, he regained some of his composure and—
"Arshia."
He greeted lightly.
"What are we going to do?"
Arshia questioned with a worried look on her face.
"I do not know. I have been going through the Guild’s archives to find some hints regarding the missing information. I still need more time."
Simba shook his head.
"That is not what I am talking about.
I am asking what are we going to do about ’him’."
Arshia questioned, recalling the man who once turned everything around.
Simba’s face turned solemn when he heard those words.

There were no documents regarding ’that’ incident, neither official nor unofficial. ’That’ incident was slowly but completely erased from everyone’s memories because that was what they were ordered to do by ’her’.
But now...
"...what else?
We report the truth."
"Oh? Will you now?"
A/N:
*Arshia*

chapters.title: Chapter 2082: A Reunion.
paragraphs: "...what else?
We report the truth."
Simba spoke with a solemn look on his face.
"Oh? Will you now?"
Suddenly, both Simba and Arshia heard a voice. The two turned around and their eyes fell on a familiar man, a man they still had not forgotten.
"Nux! You are alive!"
Arshia’s eyes widened in surprise.
"Wow, I didn’t think I would be cursed the instant I got here."
Nux commented with a light smile on his face.
"N-No, I wasn’t cursing you...
I was just surprised..."
Arshia tried to explain herself,
"Pleasantly surprised..."
She muttered in an extremely low voice.
Nux laughed as he glanced at the three-eyed woman. He then turned towards the Lionhead and—
The man was horrified.
Simba stared at Nux, pale-faced.
Alive...
This insane monster was alive!!
B-But how was this possible!?
He took the black mission and went to Umbrasol!
Every being who went there didn’t return!
Even an Eternal from the Supreme Worlds was no exception!
If even an Eternal failed, how could someone like him succeed!?
There were too many questions in his head, however, these questions currently did not matter. Simba’s mind started racing even further...

This man did something even the Supreme Worlds failed to, yet he still acted like he was dead. There was even a woman from the Supreme World that came here, wanting them to erase his records because she wanted to ’wash away the shame’.
This... this didn’t make any sense... unless...
Unless this man did all this because he wanted to cut ties with the Supreme Worlds.
’But why?’
Simba did not understand.
Why would anyone want to cut his ties with a Supreme World?
’No, that’s not important right now.’
The Lionhead quickly shook his head, his face turning even more solemn.
The reasoning did not matter, the fact was that this man was here.
’Why?’
Simba wondered and very quickly, he got the answers.
’He wants to make sure no one finds out about him.’
Simba then stared at Arshia and—
’Me and her are the only few people who know what he wishes to hide from the Supreme Worlds...’
Nux’s intention of coming here couldn’t be clearer.

Simba felt a strong chill down his spine, he felt like his entire body had given up. Honestly, he had gotten stronger than before, even Arshia had broken through and had now become a Primordial, just like him.
But...
Even then—
Simba knew they stood no chance.
This monster... Simba could see that just like them, he had broken through as well.
He was a Primordial as well and in no Universe did Simba think that he and Arshia alone would be able to stop him.
With his strength, if this monster wanted, he could have gotten rid of them any time but...
’He hasn’t done anything yet.’
The Lionhead realized.
He then stared at Nux with a careful look on his face and—
"...why are you here?"
He questioned.
Nux stared back at him, seeing Simba’s careful face, he realized there was no need to explain anything, the Lionhead was smart enough to deduce what he wanted,
"How many people know about me?"
He questioned directly.
"...it does not matter."
Simba answered, making Nux frown.
"You are underestimating them."
The Lionhead spoke with a grim look on his face. Nux’s frown deepened even further,
"Even if you kill us, they will know what they wish to know, you won’t be able to hide from them."
He spoke.
Seeing the turn the conversation was taking, Arshia’s excited expression disappeared. She slowly stepped away from Nux, wary.
Nux did not stop her either, soon, as if he sensed something, he turned towards the three-eyed woman and,
"Don’t bother, I have sealed the space around the area. Space Artifacts won’t work here."
He informed, and Arshia’s face turned even more solemn.
Nux once again glanced at Simba and,
"If I get rid of you and every other being who knew about me and this mission, how would they know?"
He questioned with a grin befitting of a third-rate villain.
"This is a world of mercenaries, information can never be truly hidden here."

Simba answered. For some reason, seeing Nux act the way he was acting right now, a strange confidence filled him. A part of him wanted nothing more than to wipe that smug off this thankless bastard’s face, even if that cost his life.

"You defeated tens of thousands of mercenaries that day, a higher number of mercenaries watched you do that, an even higher number heard of such a surprising thing happening, and an even higher number of mercenaries started spreading what happened.
You said how would they know after you get rid of those who know about you, correct?
Then let me ask you this, how are you going to kill every being that knows about you when their numbers is in trillions spread throughout the Universe?"
"They only know about me, not the mission I took. You erased that information yourself, did you not?"
Nux countered with the same grin.
But Simba didn’t back down,
"How hard do you think connecting those two will be?"
He questioned.
"Should be quite hard."
Nux shrugged.
"After all, there is no connection between a man who defeated 20,000 mercenaries and the one who took the Black Mission and went to Umbrasol."
"As I said, you are underestimating them. They do not need any connection, they will find out it was you, one way or the other, so even if you do kill us, nothing will go like you want it to."
Simba did not back down no matter how absurd his statement sounded even to him.
This was his last resistance against the inevitable.
And honestly, even though he himself didn’t believe his words, Nux knew he was correct. The Supreme Worlds were going to find out about him.

After all, even if there was no connection between a man who defeated 20,000 mercenaries and the one who took the Black Mission and went to Umbrasol, there was a connection between this man and the Leander Family that has been popular lately.

And once the Supreme Worlds start looking into it, it wouldn’t be surprising if they order the Leander Family to present itself in front of them to prove their innocence and of course, the moment the Leander Family rejects their proposal, the ’enemy’ will be clear.
It was indeed only a matter of time before they were caught. Fortunately, Nux didn’t need to prevent it, he simply needed to elongate this ’matter of time’ in question.
The only reason he was acting like this in front of Simba was to get a rough idea as to how quickly the Supreme Worlds are going to find out about this by trying to see what ways Simba comes up with.
After all, if someone like Simba could create a link between him and Umbrasol, no matter how weak the link was, the Supreme Worlds should be able to do just fine as well.
"So? Do you have any loved ones here, the ones you wish to protect?"
Suddenly, Nux questioned.
"...what?"
Simba blinked, soon however, his eyes were filled with even more hate and,
"Do your worst, I won’t say a wor—"
"Hold your lions, Lionhead."
Nux waved his hand, making him silent using Absolute Kinesis.
He then looked into Simba’s eyes and with a solemn look on his face, he began,
"The faction behind me is going to destroy Nexus, most people here would not survive it."
The instant he said those words, Simba’s face turned pale. Even Arshia was horrified, but Nux continued,
"You two are one of the few I do not wish to harm and even though there is not much I can do, I can let you and the people you care about live."
Arshia called out, a little unsure.
But then—
"Don’t believe him, he is lying to get information ou—"
"Oh fuck it."
In the end, Nux just cursed.
He then immobilized both Simba and Arshia, grabbed Simba’s head, and started reading his memories.
The two couldn’t even resist since Nux even took their ability to speak. Within a few minutes, after reading Simba’s memories, Nux stared at this man, somewhat annoyed and impressed,
"The fuck were you acting tough for if you don’t have anyone you care about?"
Simba couldn’t say anything.
"Tsk."
Nux snorted.
He then turned towards Arshia and—
"Do you want me to read your memories, or are you going to say it yourself?"
"I-I have no one else I care about in this world either..."
"Are they in any other mercenary world?"
Nux questioned.
"I-Is your faction going to destroy m-more—"
"Just answer my question."
"N-No."
Arshia shook her head and Nux quickly waved his hand, teleported the two of them away and, with that,
"Attack."
He passed the orders and—
In an instant, Mercenary Worlds all over the Universe had their strongest leaders slaughtered without being able to show any resistance.
The terrorist attack had begun.
BOOOOOOOM

You are alive!"
Arshia’s eyes widened in surprise.
"Wow, I didn’t think I would be cursed the instant I got here."
Nux commented with a light smile on his face.
"N-No, I wasn’t cursing you...
I was just surprised..."
Arshia tried to explain herself,
"Pleasantly surprised..."
She muttered in an extremely low voice.
Nux laughed as he glanced at the three-eyed woman.
He then turned towards the Lionhead and—
The man was horrified.
Simba stared at Nux, pale-faced.
Alive...
This insane monster was alive!!
B-But how was this possible!?
He took the black mission and went to Umbrasol!
Every being who went there didn’t return!
Even an Eternal from the Supreme Worlds was no exception!
If even an Eternal failed, how could someone like him succeed!?
There were too many questions in his head, however, these questions currently did not matter.
Simba’s mind started racing even further...
This man did something even the Supreme Worlds failed to, yet he still acted like he was dead.
There was even a woman from the Supreme World that came here, wanting them to erase his records because she wanted to ’wash away the shame’.
This... this didn’t make any sense... unless...
Unless this man did all this because he wanted to cut ties with the Supreme Worlds.
’But why?’
Simba did not understand.
Why would anyone want to cut his ties with a Supreme World?
’No, that’s not important right now.’
The Lionhead quickly shook his head, his face turning even more solemn.
The reasoning did not matter, the fact was that this man was here.
’Why?’
Simba wondered and very quickly, he got the answers.
’He wants to make sure no one finds out about him.’
Simba then stared at Arshia and—
’Me and her are the only few people who know what he wishes to hide from the Supreme Worlds...’
Nux’s intention of coming here couldn’t be clearer.
Simba felt a strong chill down his spine, he felt like his entire body had given up.
Honestly, he had gotten stronger than before, even Arshia had broken through and had now become a Primordial, just like him.
But...
Even then—
Simba knew they stood no chance.
This monster...
Simba could see that just like them, he had broken through as well.
He was a Primordial as well and in no Universe did Simba think that he and Arshia alone would be able to stop him.
With his strength, if this monster wanted, he could have gotten rid of them any time but...
’He hasn’t done anything yet.’
The Lionhead realized.
He then stared at Nux with a careful look on his face and—
"...why are you here?"
He questioned.
Nux stared back at him, seeing Simba’s careful face, he realized there was no need to explain anything, the Lionhead was smart enough to deduce what he wanted,
"How many people know about me?"
He questioned directly.
"...it does not matter."
Simba answered, making Nux frown.
"You are underestimating them."
The Lionhead spoke with a grim look on his face.
Nux’s frown deepened even further,
"Even if you kill us, they will know what they wish to know, you won’t be able to hide from them."
He spoke.
Seeing the turn the conversation was taking, Arshia’s excited expression disappeared.
She slowly stepped away from Nux, wary.
Nux did not stop her either, soon, as if he sensed something, he turned towards the three-eyed woman and,
"Don’t bother, I have sealed the space around the area.
Space Artifacts won’t work here."
He informed, and Arshia’s face turned even more solemn.
Nux once again glanced at Simba and,
"If I get rid of you and every other being who knew about me and this mission, how would they know?"
He questioned with a grin befitting of a third-rate villain.
"This is a world of mercenaries, information can never be truly hidden here."
Simba answered.
For some reason, seeing Nux act the way he was acting right now, a strange confidence filled him.
A part of him wanted nothing more than to wipe that smug off this thankless bastard’s face, even if that cost his life.

"You defeated tens of thousands of mercenaries that day, a higher number of mercenaries watched you do that, an even higher number heard of such a surprising thing happening, and an even higher number of mercenaries started spreading what happened.
You said how would they know after you get rid of those who know about you, correct?
Then let me ask you this, how are you going to kill every being that knows about you when their numbers is in trillions spread throughout the Universe?"
"They only know about me, not the mission I took.
You erased that information yourself, did you not?"
Nux countered with the same grin.
But Simba didn’t back down,
"How hard do you think connecting those two will be?"
He questioned.
"Should be quite hard."
Nux shrugged.
"After all, there is no connection between a man who defeated 20,000 mercenaries and the one who took the Black Mission and went to Umbrasol."
"As I said, you are underestimating them.
They do not need any connection, they will find out it was you, one way or the other, so even if you do kill us, nothing will go like you want it to."
Simba did not back down no matter how absurd his statement sounded even to him.
This was his last resistance against the inevitable.
And honestly, even though he himself didn’t believe his words, Nux knew he was correct.
The Supreme Worlds were going to find out about him.

After all, even if there was no connection between a man who defeated 20,000 mercenaries and the one who took the Black Mission and went to Umbrasol, there was a connection between this man and the Leander Family that has been popular lately.

And once the Supreme Worlds start looking into it, it wouldn’t be surprising if they order the Leander Family to present itself in front of them to prove their innocence and of course, the moment the Leander Family rejects their proposal, the ’enemy’ will be clear.
It was indeed only a matter of time before they were caught.
Fortunately, Nux didn’t need to prevent it, he simply needed to elongate this ’matter of time’ in question.
The only reason he was acting like this in front of Simba was to get a rough idea as to how quickly the Supreme Worlds are going to find out about this by trying to see what ways Simba comes up with.
After all, if someone like Simba could create a link between him and Umbrasol, no matter how weak the link was, the Supreme Worlds should be able to do just fine as well.
"So?
Do you have any loved ones here, the ones you wish to protect?"
Suddenly, Nux questioned.
"...what?"
Simba blinked, soon however, his eyes were filled with even more hate and,
"Do your worst, I won’t say a wor—"
"Hold your lions, Lionhead."
Nux waved his hand, making him silent using Absolute Kinesis.
He then looked into Simba’s eyes and with a solemn look on his face, he began,
"The faction behind me is going to destroy Nexus, most people here would not survive it."
The instant he said those words, Simba’s face turned pale.
Even Arshia was horrified, but Nux continued,
"You two are one of the few I do not wish to harm and even though there is not much I can do, I can let you and the people you care about live."
Arshia called out, a little unsure.
But then—
"Don’t believe him, he is lying to get information ou—"
"Oh fuck it."
In the end, Nux just cursed.
He then immobilized both Simba and Arshia, grabbed Simba’s head, and started reading his memories.
The two couldn’t even resist since Nux even took their ability to speak.
Within a few minutes, after reading Simba’s memories, Nux stared at this man, somewhat annoyed and impressed,
"The fuck were you acting tough for if you don’t have anyone you care about?"
Simba couldn’t say anything.
"Tsk."
Nux snorted.
He then turned towards Arshia and—
"Do you want me to read your memories, or are you going to say it yourself?"
"I-I have no one else I care about in this world either..."
"Are they in any other mercenary world?"
Nux questioned.
"I-Is your faction going to destroy m-more—"
"Just answer my question."
"N-No."
Arshia shook her head and Nux quickly waved his hand, teleported the two of them away and, with that,
"Attack."
He passed the orders and—
In an instant, Mercenary Worlds all over the Universe had their strongest leaders slaughtered without being able to show any resistance.
The terrorist attack had begun.
BOOOOOOOM

chapters.title: Chapter 2083: Let’s do it.
paragraphs: "Attack."

Nux passed the order and in an instant, his Transcendent Level subordinates that were hiding in the selected Mercenary Worlds moved instantly, appearing right in front of the Mercenary Leaders of those worlds.
All these beings were connected to Nux’s Universe, so the respective World Wills could not sense them, making it easier for them to sneak in.

Of course, unlike Nux, his subordinates did not have Vulpiana’s Law of Timeless Veil that allowed them to hide in another timeline, so despite them doing their best in order to try and do this as silently as possible, the Mercenary Leaders were still able to sense their presence eventually and put up some resistance to try and hold them off—
Or at least... that was what should have happened.
But even when the Mercenary Leaders managed to sense their presence and react on time, it didn’t make much of a difference.

The difference in strength between the assassins and the targets was simply too high. After all, Nux didn’t just do it all without a plan—he had subordinates in almost all the Mercenary Worlds. It was one of the ways he could keep tabs on the Universe and understand what was happening and when it was happening.

These subordinates, having been completely overwritten by the Slave Seal, were active in these worlds for thousands of years. They knew exactly how strong the Mercenary Leaders of a specific world were, and Nux used this information to plan the attack.
The Mercenary Leaders of Low-Level Mercenary Worlds were all Primordials. Against Transcendent Level assassins, they never had a chance.
As for the Mercenary Leaders who were at the Transcendent Level, they were directly greeted by Nux’s wives.
Yes, Amaya, Astaria, Melia, Felberta, Aeliana, and Vyriana—all these Transcendent Level monsters were on the move.
With their Absolute Laws, the opponents—who were merely normal Transcendents—didn’t stand a chance because their Domains were crushed in an instant, rendering them powerless.
This was not a war,
It was a one-sided massacre.

Most leaders couldn’t even complete one sentence before they were beheaded, and because these were crucial times due to the Universe’s strong reaction and the Supreme Worlds’ announcement, most leaders of a specific world were gathered in one place, making it even easier for the assassins.
All targeted leaders fell within 20 seconds of Nux giving the orders and with that—
"Devour."
Nux gave the order, and his other set of subordinates—the ones that weren’t part of his Universe and had been laying low in these Mercenary Worlds all this while—started devouring these worlds.
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
A total of fifty-six Mercenary Worlds began to rumble and desperately called for help.
But these were Mercenary Worlds; mercenaries had next to no sense of loyalty in them. Instead of doing anything, they instantly rushed out of the worlds instead.
Those who did try to stay and witnessed what was happening became targets of the assassins, and very quickly, all fifty-six worlds were helplessly devoured by Nux’s slaves.
And of course, this time, since the Universe did not react to any of this, the Supreme Worlds had no clue what had just happened.
The worlds were erased out of existence, and so were the records in them.
Nux watched everything unfold in front of him in silence. Beside him stood Simba and Arshia, staring at the fifty-six screens in front of them with shocked looks on their faces.
"Y-You destroyed those worlds..."
Arshia commented with a horrified look on her face.
"T-To do this just so you could hide your identity..."
Simba muttered, staring at Nux with a pale face.
Just what sort of monster had he encountered?
He... he had this sort of power all along...?
Just what force is behind him? It definitely wasn’t a Supreme World, but he couldn’t think of any other force capable of pulling off something like this.
Of course, destroying a few Mercenary Worlds wasn’t a big deal—any force from a High-Level World could have done that.
But the problem was,
This act went against a Supreme World. No known High-Level World in their right mind would dare to act in such a way. After all, no matter how well the execution was,
It was an act done against the Supreme Worlds. In one way or another, they will find out who was behind it, and once they do...
Things will not end well.
Simba knew that, and so did every being in the Universe.
The Supremes just held that much power.
Then...
’Why would he go so far?’
Simba could not understand and frowned as he stared at Nux.
"You two will need to stay under my subordinates for a few days."
Nux instructed as he glanced at Arshia and Simba. His tone made sure that there was no room for negotiation.
The last thing he wanted was for the Supreme Worlds to capture these two and learn everything that happened here.
Both Simba and Arshia didn’t say anything either. They could tell what Nux was thinking, and they knew they had no power here.
Nux and the faction behind him were simply too strong.
But this didn’t mean they could stay silent—especially her—
"...Why are you doing this?"
Arshia questioned in a low voice.
"Hmm?"
Nux glanced at her and paused for a moment.
He knew the woman had some connections to the Supreme Worlds. He hadn’t forgotten that being from the Supreme World he had seen in the Umbrasol attack recording that Simba had showed him.

It seemed like he belonged to the same race as that of Arshia, so in one way or another, there was a connection between her and the Supreme Worlds. As for the reason why she was working in a mere Mercenary Company, Nux did not know.
Honestly, he wanted to read her memories and learn everything about her,
But he knew not many people were comfortable with it, and in the end, Arshia did help him in some ways. He would rather not have her hate him without good reason.
Not to mention...
Nux had a LOT of things to prepare right now.
After all, the plan still wasn’t over—rather, this was merely the beginning. The true game had only just begun.
’Nux.’
And just as he was thinking about it, he heard a voice.
A light smile appeared on his face and,
’Did you find him?’
He questioned.
’Mhm.’
Melia nodded. In her hands was one of the Mercenary Leaders of the worlds they hadn’t targeted—a Primordial level being—unconscious.
She stared at him, disgusted.
’He was behind the disappearance of thousands of mercenaries. He sold males as slaves, raped the females, and once he was "bored" of them, he killed them.’
’Fits the description a little too well, huh.’
Nux commented with a light smile.

Honestly, he knew he wasn’t any good. He knew he was a mass murderer; he had killed a ridiculously large number of beings for his own benefit, but in the end, his mind was still that of a hypocrite. Choosing a criminal for his sacrifice put his mind at ease much more compared to using an innocent being.
’Do I bring him?’
While Nux was thinking all this, Melia questioned.
’No, I’ll come there.’
He answered as he then turned towards his two ’guests’ and with a flick of his finger, their minds were overwhelmed, and they lost consciousness.
His shadow then trembled as suddenly, Maeve, Sharnoth’s Nocthari subordinate, materialized.
"Take care of them."
He ordered. Maeve nodded as she grabbed the two of them and, with another flick, he sent them away.

Then Nux teleported himself right next to Melia and the moment he appeared in this place, he noticed the room was covered in blood and Melia was sitting on her throne with a large, human-sized blood capsule at the very corner of the room, as if the Vampire had placed the filth as far away from her as possible while still keeping it in sight.
Seeing this sight, Nux couldn’t hold back and laughed out loud,
"Why do you have to make this dramatic?"
He questioned with a big smile and Melia, sitting on her Blood Throne,
"I need to look good in front of my husband."
She answered.
Nux could already imagine how the woman acted when he said he would be coming here. Once again, he laughed out loud as he walked towards her and fell on top of her.
Melia, still sitting on her throne, caught him, placed his head on her breasts, and started gently ruffling his hair.
Nux’s hands moved as well, his fingers crawling underneath her gown and touching her bare back.
The two stayed like this until—
’We have work to do.’
Amaya spoke in a salty tone. Clearly, the Devourer didn’t like the Vampire hogging all the attention.
Actually, in her mind, she was cursing another Vampire.
It was all her fault!

Hearing her words, Nux laughed as he finally moved. Melia too cursed the Devourer in her head, but then she waved her hand and the blood cocoon floated in front of them, revealing the Mercenary Leader she had caught.
The Vampire and her husband stared at each other and nodded,
"Let’s do it."

chapters.title: Chapter 2084: The Summons.
paragraphs: The skies above the world of Vael’Terros shimmered with different magical energies and colors. No, it wasn’t because Vael’Terros was a beautiful world with a unique atmosphere or something like that.
It was because these different energies continued to crack the space barrier around it, forcefully tearing it apart as foreign beings or ships rushed in.

This happened so often that the space barrier of Vael’Terros thinned to the limit, almost as if it no longer existed. This made it easier for the foreigners to enter its boundaries, causing the colorful change in the sky.
Yes, Vael’Terros was the Middle-Level neutral World directly under the Supreme World of Balance, and right now, it was being used as a base of the Supreme Worlds’ actions.
In the Supreme Worlds’ recent announcement, Vael’Terros was the world the Mercenary Guild Leaders were told to appear in.
And this was exactly what was happening right now.
There were only two hours left before the given time ended. Because of that, the Mercenary Guild Leaders pouring in had become more frequent. More than a few were coming at the same time now.
More and more warships of different origins came in. There were also some regularly seen ships pouring in—it seemed like more than a few Mercenary Guild Leaders were using them.
One look at them, and it was enough to know that these were the ships from the transport company who moved efficiently and made a ton of profit from this ordeal.
Yes, in this game, they were the true winners.
The Mercenary Guild Leaders who were already in Vael’Terros stared at those ships with envious looks on their faces. Clearly, they were jealous.
As more and more ships appeared from every corner of the world, the chaos rose.
"Move! MOVE! We land in one minute!"

A hulking ogre-lord roared, his arms coated in chains of molten iron. His skybarge slammed into the landing tier, scraping across crystallized marble as hundreds of his attendants scrambled behind him.
"There’s no space left!"
Barked a bird-headed commander in iridescent armor.
"Tell them to circle! The fifth convoy is still in line!"
"There IS no line anymore, fool!"
Another snarled.
"Just land wherever you can!"
The central Assembly Plateau groaned as more and more vessels descended. Many didn’t wait to dock.
Some leapt, some more capable ones teleported, while others simply crashed.
It didn’t matter if the ships were destroyed, they got here in time—and that’s the only thing that mattered.
Yes, even though there were still two hours left, these people were that desperate, simply because none of them wanted to anger the Supremes.
Of course, not all the Guild Leaders were the same. Some complained,
"We were just given twenty-four hours,"
A knight in golden runes cursed as she removed her helmet, sweat dripping down her brow.
"Only twenty-four hours to cross the Chaos Zone and three sealed borders!"

The Outer-Space wasn’t just the open space filled with Universal Energy anyone could travel randomly through. There were different areas with difficult challenges and, of course, the farther these beings came from, the more such areas they encountered.
"And you still came,"
Said a gray-robed lich beside her, not bothering with the complaining knight.
"As did I. As did they."
He gestured to the swelling crowd.
"So shut your mouth and stop complaining."
The lich growled, annoyed.
And honestly, the knight couldn’t counter his words. She just walked back and started instructing her subordinates.
Yes, the situation was chaos—World Leaders who would never share a room stood side by side, pressed shoulder to shoulder.
A wolf-headed war chief from the Ten-Star Howl Pact growled at the scenery.
"All the Mercenary Leaders in one place. If they want, they could kill us and take over all the mercenaries all over the universe without any issues."
He commented with a solemn look.
"Heh."
Another leader just laughed,
"As if they would want something like this."
The wolf-headed war chief turned toward the one who laughed at his words and narrowed his eyes,
"You talk as if you know what they are thinking."
"No, I talk as if I know where I stand—and this is because I do.
Could this be a trap to get rid of us all? Who knows? Could very well be.
But is there anything you or I can do about it?
No.
There is nothing we could do.
If this is the trap, we have no choice but to accept our fate—because if the Supremes want us dead, our death is inevitable."
The man retorted.
And the wolf-head turned silent.
Those words were harsh, demeaning even—but...
Could he say anything against them?
Of course not.

They were the truth. What the Supremes were planning did not matter because they had no way to resist them. At the end of the day, they could only lower their heads and do what they were told, even if that meant finding everything there is about buried information and giving results in a ridiculously low amount of time.
Yes, it was unfair.
The time given was too short—it was near impossible to complete this task, and yet...
Over fifty thousand leaders had gathered, and more were coming.
Some of these leaders brought small entourages, others came alone.
Every single being here was powerful enough to command armies, influence economies, and burn different worlds if they so wished.
But here?
Here, they waited like children outside a throne room.
"I had to abandon three strongholds mid-siege just to make it here,"
Grumbled a horned tyrant wrapped in bone-laced silk.
"Do they think we can just teleport through the Veins of Zhyrith?"
He complained.
"I did teleport,"
Another being muttered in a smoky voice.
"Used half my world’s remaining power reserves to do so."
"I lost contact with half my council on the way,"
Another glass-skinned monarch muttered with shaking hands.
"I don’t even know if my world still stands."
"All of that—"
A sharp voice cut in,
"—just to stand in this place and wait."
The voice belonged to a pale woman with features like an elf and silver tattoos flowing like rivers across her cheeks.
"They knew we’d drop everything,"
She smiled weakly.
And the other leaders nodded.
They knew—
The summons was not an invitation.
It was an Order.
An order where the penalty for disobedience was... erasure.
A heavy silence fell on the place.
But then—
"OUT OF THE DAMN WAY!"
A shout was heard as another massive ship descended from the skies, its jagged hull glowing red with friction as it tore through the clouds.
"Make space! Make space or I’ll land on your fucking heads!"
The man commanding the ship screamed.
"Right, more are coming..."
The other leaders laughed. Honestly, they were laughing at their own situation. In the end, they scattered. They didn’t wish to start a conflict here, not in an area commanded bythem.
As they moved away, the ship slammed down, cracking the ground beneath it. Crimson mist burst outward from its impact zone, warping the air with residual energy.
"Do you have any idea how long we waited in orbit!?"
A towering Molgarr beast-lord leapt off the deck, horns dripping magma.
"Two damn hours!"
"And whose fault is that, fire-head? You tried to cut the queue!"
Suddenly, another voice was heard.
A sharp-tongued mercenary queen, her blade-arm twitching with annoyance.
"I don’t give a voidborn damn about queues! This whole place is a madhouse!"
The Molgarr growled, nostrils flaring.
"We got the summons less than a cycle ago—we tore through three neutral sectors and five Chaos Zones just to get here in time!"
"You’re not the only one!"
The mercenary queen retorted.
"My citadel is still burning. I left mid-assault!"
"Mine is..."
Yes, the same conversation happened again—just that this time, it was another set of Guild Leaders complaining about stuff.
The other leaders just laughed, and this didn’t go unnoticed by the Molgarr.
"The fuck are you laughing at, huh!?"
"You really wish to do it here?"
The lich looked into his eyes, and after a moment, Molgarr turned silent. Again, no matter how reckless he was, he couldn’t act wild in Supreme Worlds’ lands.
In the end, he settled down with the rest of the mercenary guild leaders. For the next two hours, they stood like this.

Yes, the so-called World Leaders who were respected wherever they went weren’t even given a seat and were forced to stand on the ground like commoners with no rights. It was humiliating, and since there was no one to manage these people or address their questions, there were constant complaints as well—but the funny part was that every time after they complained,
After a short while, these leaders silenced themselves on their own.
That was simply how strong the Supreme Worlds’ influence was. Even when they weren’t present, these arrogant people still kept themselves in check.
Time passed, more and more guild leaders rushed in. As the time got close, the rush increased as well,
Until finally,
Two hours later, exactly at the time given by the Supreme Worlds,
Theyappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 2085: The Supreme Borns
paragraphs: Theyappeared.
The sky fell silent.
The wind stopped.
Time itself felt like it had paused.
There was no sound, no warning...
Just... an overwhelming presence that seemed to overpower every single being in existence. In an instant, the ’crowd’ of World Leaders realized it as well.
They were here.
They all looked up, and their eyes fell on four beings that seemed beyond mortal comprehension.
They did not walk; it didn’t look like they were floating either.
It just... felt like they simply ’appeared’ and the entire world bent to acknowledge it.
The so-called ’World Leaders’ were in awe when they saw these beings descend. The moment they sensed their overwhelming presence, they realized it.
All this while, every time the ’common people’ encountered the beings from Supreme Worlds, they weren’t exactly... the ’beings from Supreme Worlds’.
They were beings who were ’recognized’ by the Supreme Worlds and were accepted by them. Beings that indeed lived in the Supreme Worlds—and yes, beings who were ridiculously strong.
But even then, they still weren’t the Supreme Beings born in the Supreme Worlds.
Right now, however, things were different.
Even if they ignored their appearance, just these beings’ presence alone was enough to tell the Guild Leaders the truth.
The beings in front of them were not mere subordinates.
They were the Supreme Born.
The actual entities from the Supreme Worlds.
And the very fact that these people came here showed that this matter was far more serious than what any of these mercenary guild leaders were expecting.
Every being present on the ground gulped. Their eyes could not move away from the four beings hovering in the air.
The first one to attract their eyes was the being from the Supreme World of Light.

Descending slowly from the golden heavens above, this radiant being hovered in the air, bathed in warm, divine light. His long, flowing robes shimmered like woven sunlight, gently rippling with every movement. Majestic wings spread wide behind him, each feather glowing with celestial fire, casting soft golden rays across the skies.

His eyes burned like twin suns—calm yet commanding—radiating a power that stirred awe and reverence. A halo crowned his head, pulsing faintly, as if echoing the will of the heavens. In one hand, he held a sword forged of pure light, its edges humming softly, as though it existed beyond mortal realms.

His aura was overwhelming—pure, eternal, and sovereign. It was the presence of divine judgment and protection, a being who had watched over countless ages, now arriving not just to be seen, but to be obeyed.
*Picture*
And completely opposite to him stood another being—a being that seemed like the counter to him.

A dark, vile figure descending—slowly, silently—hovering in the cold void between dimensions. The very air around him warped, as if recoiling from his presence. Shadows clung to his body like smoke made solid, forming armor that resembled charred obsidian—jagged and ancient.

His eyes burned a deep, furious red—twin coals in a skeletal face twisted with endless malice. Black horns curled from his skull like the gnarled roots of a dead tree, and his claws seemed ready to tear through both matter and soul. Every movement he made left streaks of black mist behind, as though the darkness obeyed his will.

His aura was suffocating—thick with hatred, despair, and wrath. He did not simply arrive; he invaded the sky, as if his presence alone was a curse on the light—a declaration that something old and terrible had awoken.
Yes, he was from the Supreme World of Darkness.
*Picture*

These two opposing forces clashed with each other. Just the clash from their auras alone was so destructive that a world like Vael’Terros would have never survived the impact. Yet somehow, the world was still intact.
It was almost a miracle.
A miracle made possible by another being that stood right beside the two opposing energies.

This celestial figure hovered with an air of silent divinity, his presence parting the very stillness of the sky. Cloaked in deep starlight blue, his flowing robes rippled gently in an unseen wind, as if space itself bent to his arrival.

His skin glowed with a soft, ethereal luminescence—the shade of moonlight filtered through cosmic mist. His single eye like twin stars shone with piercing white brilliance—unblinking and all-seeing. A radiant halo encircled his head, pulsing faintly, echoing the orbits of far-off planets.
In one hand he held a spear tipped with a diamond-shaped sigil, glowing with ancient, calm energy. On his chest gleamed a sigil of the void white sun, radiating silent authority.
His aura was immense.
It felt weightless yet overwhelming, like the vacuum between stars—distant, unknowable, eternal.
Yes, he represented the Supreme World of Balance.
*Picture*
These were the three Supreme Worlds—showcasing their overwhelming presence and clashing, yet oddly in-sync energies.
The fourth being, however, stood at a distance, as if he had nothing to do with them.

His robes caught the starlight as he hovered above the ground. Glyphs glowed faintly across the fabric of his clothing, pulsing in rhythm with the quiet hum of unseen forces. Every movement felt measured—like the ticking of a perfect, eternal clock.

Pale eyes glowed with deep and endless knowledge. A luminous halo of shifting runes and arcane geometry formed behind his body, spinning gently. He held an ancient tome open in one hand, its pages turning without wind, while in the other, his staff shimmered with orbs of celestial energy, orbiting like distant moons.

His aura was vast—cold, calculating, and endlessly wise. It wrapped around him like the silence of space: not empty, but full of secrets. Where others brought power or terror, he brought understanding that bent the very reality itself.
Yes, he came from the Supreme World of Eternity.
*Picture*
These were the Four Beings from the Supreme Worlds, and as they stared down—like gods staring at mortals—a heavy silence descended.
It happened on its own.
The moment they all appeared—
Everything stopped.
Chatter died mid-sentence.
No one needed to speak.
No one dared.
Thousands of beings—kings of their respective worlds—all bowed as one. Some knelt, some lowered their heads, others dropped to the ground without realizing it.
Even the ships floating in the sky dimmed their lights, engines going quiet.

Mountains in the distance bent slightly inward, clouds thinned and coiled away like respectful servants. The ground beneath their feet pulsed—stone, dirt, ash, and even old bones shifting slightly, turning themselves to face the Supreme Beings.
Every living being—and even those that were not alive—seemed to acknowledge a single truth:
The rulers of the universe had arrived.
After a momentary silence, the being of Balance stepped forward, his cloak drifting like mist. He gazed down at the thousands below.
"You have arrived. As expected."
His voice rang clear, calm... and unshakably certain.
He looked over the crowd as though surveying tools, not people—and none of the mercenary guild leaders looked ’offended’.

All their spirits were already crushed the instant they realized who stood in front of them. They were expecting to meet the Supreme Worlds’ subordinates, but to directly be addressed by the Supreme Borns?
None of them would dare to say a word or show dissatisfaction even if they had millions of lives.
Balance, as if already expecting this, didn’t seem too bothered and continued,
"We will not waste time with pleasantries. You already know why you are here.
So let us begin."
He ordered.
Yes, there wasn’t even a simple sentence of welcome.
This was arrogance.
Arrogance beyond anything anyone had seen.
Balance then turned towards Eternity, and he looked down.
No one saw his eyes—if he had them at all—but all felt his gaze.
The air rippled around him.
The space twisted.
Even the energy of time seemed affected.
And then—he raised his staff.
There was no chant, no grand gesture, no declaration.
Just a smooth, weightless, simple motion and then—

The sky cracked like glass, and from it descended a structure made of flowing silver and radiant crystal, bending reality itself as it landed on the earth without sound. It pulsed with an otherworldly rhythm, every edge soft and perfect, every surface shimmering like shifting stardust.

The structure, shaped like a smooth lotus with opening layers, formed itself from light and time. Dozens of floating rings hovered around it, inscribed with glowing runes no one could read—but all instinctively feared. At its heart was a door—not one carved by hand, but formed by will.
*Picture*
Once it was created, Balance raised his hand once more, his face tilting ever so slightly toward the silver structure now rooted in reality.
"Each of you will enter—alone."
His voice rang out again—measured, absolute.
"You will read the reports you have come with."
He paused.
"And the chamber will judge."
His head tilted just a fraction further, as if amused.
"The Chamber does not ask for your opinion. It does not need your defense.
It will look into your memories and compare it with the report. Any lies, any unmentioned information, or any incomplete detail will be caught.
And if it does—
The Chamber will tear your souls apart, pulling you out of the Universal Reincarnation Cycle."

Even though they knew that the so-called Supremes didn’t give a damn about their lives, the Mercenary Guild Leaders were helpless. None of them had the gall to step forward and refuse to cooperate with them.
They... they had no choice but to step forward.

As if knowing the people were ready, the Eternity-born waved his hand, and in an instant, thousands of similar chambers appeared all over the world. Not just that—fences that placed mercenaries into a thousand different groups appeared on the ground as well.
In an instant, all the beings gathered here were divided into five thousand different groups, and the fencing made sure no members of different groups shared one chamber.
All the people needed to do was to follow the fences that would guide them to their chambers.

Yes, all this happened with a flick of a finger. It was the Power of Creation beyond what anyone could even make sense of—not to mention the calculation required to create perfect fencing to organize the disorganized group of tens of thousands of beings.
Without saying a single word, the Eternity-born had passed the instructions, and the people beneath him knew exactly what to do without ever daring to complain.
The unfortunate Mercenary Guild Leaders standing in front of the chambers gulped. They didn’t have to be told to know that they had to be the first ones to step forward.
To walk into the chambers that were very much capable of killing them—no, not ’killing them’—these chambers could ’tear their souls apart’.
And yet...
They still had no choice but to follow.
After the first one stepped forward, the rest followed. None of them wanted to be left behind and be targeted.
And just like that, it began.
One after the other, the Mercenary Guild Leaders walked in, and within a few seconds, they came out, surprising the other leaders.
Weren’t they supposed to read their reports? How did they come out so quickly? Was their report incomplete?
No, that wasn’t possible—they wouldn’t have come out if that was the case.
Soon, however, they realized it. The time flow in these chambers was different, so even when the report reading went on for hours, outside, only a few seconds would pass.
Once again, the leaders couldn’t help but feel how efficient those ultimate beings hovering above them were.
As more and more time passed, and more Mercenary Guild Leaders gave their reports and returned, a sense of ease spread over the rest of them, and the process became even smoother.
But then suddenly,
One of the five thousand chambers suddenly turned from blue to red, instantly attracting everyone’s attention.
It felt... ominous.
This was especially true for the group that was supposed to enter the chamber.
Fwoosh
Then suddenly, the chamber made a sound, and a big red screen hovered in the air in a way that every being, no matter what corner of the world he was in, could see it clearly.
In that screen, it showed what was happening inside the chamber.
The air felt unnaturally still.
Guildmaster Vharkos stood at the center of the radiant floor.

He was a massive man—clad in reinforced blackstone armor, a scarred warlord who had once conquered three worlds in a single night because of an Elite Mission given to his guild. His axe had tasted more blood than most armies.
But here...
His voice trembled slightly.
"...and that concludes my report. All movements, exchanges, and contracts have been recorded... to the best of my knowledge."
The floating symbols above him shined. The moment he spoke the final word, the silver runes pulsing through the floor disappeared, and the door before him buzzed gently—waiting to open.
Vharkos took a step forward, ready to leave.
Naturally, he heaved a big sigh of relief.
Finally—finally, he could leave and end this nightmare for good.
Or at least... that was what he thought.
But the door did not open.
Instead, the chamber pulsed.
Once.
Then again.
Suddenly, the floor beneath him lit up with a crimson glow. The rings above him spun wildly, shifting into a new, ominous shape.
"W-What...?"
Vharkos turned, stuttering, as he didn’t understand what was happening. His mind was already engulfed in fear—the entire chamber turning crimson did not help either.
Then, an ancient, emotionless voice echoed.
[The record has been reviewed.]
[Memory fragments conflict with the statement.]
[No Concealment detected.]
[Record Omission detected.]
Vharkos’s eyes widened in horror.
"Wait—I didn’t lie! I just didn’t have the details—I couldn’t find the full contracts because they were erased thirty-three thousand years ago!"
He tried to explain himself. His desperation was clear.
If this chamber indeed had the power to read his mind and know if he was stating the truth or not, he believed that it would know that he wasn’t lying.
He truly did everything he could to recover the erased contract, but it simply wasn’t possible—every single witness of that incident was dead, no records could be found.
But—
[Truth withheld is still truth unspoken.]
The emotionless voice did not care.
[You spoke knowing it was incomplete.]
[Judgment Initiated.]
And then, it began.
"AAAAAAAARGHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
Vharkos howled as he fell to his knees as pain he had never experienced once in his long life started tearing through his body.
It didn’t hit his body or his skin—
It targeted his very soul.
The floor beneath him glowed brighter. Chains clawed through his armor, piercing through it like it was nothing—and still, his physical body remained intact. After all, it was never the target.
It was just the container.
The chains quickly made their way to the real target:
The soul.
Just as Balance said, it was now time to ’tear it apart’.
"AAAAAAAARGHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
The Guildmaster screamed in agony again.
There was no blood, but it was still unbearable.
It was... worse than death.
His soul spasmed, convulsed, shattered into a dozen burning shards, then reformed—only to shatter again.
Again.
And again.
And again.
"P-PLEASE! I DIDN’T LIE! I—I SWORE I—!!"
He tried to beg for mercy—
But—
He wasn’t that fortunate.
This had only just begun.
Or at least, that was the original intention, but then—
The screen showing everything happening inside the chamber froze, surprising everyone, even the Supreme Borns standing above.
Well, everyone but one—
"That is enough."
The Supreme Being of Light declared with an emotionless look on his face.
He then turned towards Balance and—
"We have passed our message. There is no need to continue his suffering any longer."
He spoke, and with a wave of his hand, Vharkos’s damaged soul, that had frozen, suddenly began dispersing, vanishing from existence and returning to the universe as a form of energy.
It was the only form of mercy Light could have offered in this situation—a mercy that put the hearts of Mercenary Guild Leaders at ease.
’At least there was one compassionate being amongst them.’
That was their thought.
Balance and Eternity did not particularly care about Light’s actions either.
"Hypocrite."
The Supreme Being of Darkness, however, snorted in disdain—and while no one showed it on their faces, a few Guild Leaders agreed with him.
Why act after his soul was tormented again and again? Couldn’t he have done this sooner?
They could see it was all an act. They could see that Light wasn’t any better than the others—not that it mattered.
Even if they could see, acting blind was their only option.
"Continue."
Light simply ignored the comment Darkness made. He was not here to fight. Darkness, having the same opinion, did not bother as well.
After all, none of them wanted to waste more breath than they already had. Every moment wasted in this lowly place made them feel impure.
Honestly, Darkness was bored.
To think they would send a Supreme Born to deal with mere mercenaries—no matter how he thought about it, this felt too much.
Even the lowly subordinates could have done this, and the fact that everything was flowing so smoothly annoyed him even further.
Yes, a flag was raised.
This was the moment Darkness would look back in the future and curse himself for wishing what he did.
"Hm?"
Suddenly, Eternity frowned.
Every other Supreme Born turned towards him, and he commented—
"Fifty-six Mercenary Worlds didn’t come."
Eternity explained.
The Supreme Borns weren’t surprised. After all, even they knew the time given wasn’t enough, but since they still needed the reports from every world, they knew they needed to send someone to get it.
But—
"The subordinates I sent there saw these worlds no longer exist."
"That shouldn’t be possible. I checked the total number of Mercenary Worlds myself—"
"They were destroyed a few hours ago."
Eternity spoke with a grim look on his face.
The other Supreme Borns frowned, and just then—
BOOOOOOOM

chapters.title: Chapter 2087: Because out here... You will see us.
paragraphs: "Are you ready?"
Aeliana questioned as she glanced at the screen in front of her. The screen showed everything that was happening in Vael’Terros through a Mercenary Guild Leader’s eyes.
Yes, he was the one Melia had captured and, using her abilities, had gotten complete control over.
Nux, who was watching everything play out, nodded. He then turned towards his Melia, and the Vampire nodded.
The Vampire then raised her hand—
Snap
She snapped and—
BOOOOOOOM
The body of the Mercenary Guild Leader they had captured suddenly burst into pieces, gore and blood spreading all over Vael’Terros as the incident attracted every being’s attention.
What the hell...?
He just... died?
But how...?
Who killed him?
And why?
Why would anyone do something so foolish when they were in the presence of the Supreme Borns?

Thousands of questions appeared in everyone’s head, and as if to answer those questions, the Mercenary Guild Leader’s blood and gore that was spread all over the world suddenly trembled, as if an unknown force was squeezing all the leftover energy from it.

The squeezed-up energy then gathered right above and transformed into big crimson screens. Yes, wherever the blood and gore had fallen, a screen was there, effectively covering the entirety of Vael’Terros, making sure every being here could see it.
And on the screen, he appeared.
A tall man cloaked in black and silver robes that shimmered with strange energy. His face was covered in a black veil, his golden eyes, however, looked as if they were staring into one’s very soul.
"A good day to you all."

He spoke. His voice sounded so charming that for an instant, a few weaker Guild Masters lost themselves. The stronger ones, however, stared at the screen closest to them with a grim look on their faces.
They could see it—whatever that was happening, it was anything but good.
The man on the screen was insane, and honestly, none of them wanted to know what he wanted to say, especially not in the presence of the Supreme Borns.
Of course, the Supreme Borns were different. They stared at the screens, curious—especially Darkness. His crimson eyes shined brightly as his grin widened.
Clearly, this was a lot more interesting than whatever they were initially sent here to do. Darkness was actually looking forward to what the little man in the screen had to say.
Yes, he was willing to generously spend his time to see what the other party had to say—that was how generous and fair he was.
Of course, the others weren’t the same.
Without waiting any longer, Eternity waved his hand, and one of the screens hovering in the air trembled and floated towards him.

Eternity looked into the man’s eyes, but there was no change in the man’s expression. It seemed like he couldn’t see through the screen. Eternity’s hollow eyes stared at the screen as the grimoire in his hand moved on its own.
Within a second, he turned towards Balance and—
"Work of a Blood Race."
He revealed.
"Where are they?"
Balance questioned, but Eternity shook his head.
"I cannot find them."
"...what?"
Balance’s expression changed.
The Darkness, on the other hand, grinned even further. He was somewhat worried that this might end before it even began, but the little man was much more entertaining than he believed.
Darkness made up his mind—he wouldn’t make his death as painful as he initially would have.
That would be his reward for entertaining him.
"If you’re done trying,
Shall we now begin?"
Suddenly, the man on the screen spoke. His tone was condescending, as if he knew these people were trying to find him, but he was so sure that they would fail that he simply did not care.
His tone made the Guild Masters beneath tremble; they had never heard someone use such a tone in front of the Supreme Borns. The Supreme Borns, however, did not react.
They simply allowed the man to continue. He had successfully gotten their attention, so they wanted to know what he was trying to do.
"I am sure you are curious who I am."
The man began, his voice calm—too calm, in fact.
"I am just one voice... in a storm that is coming.
One voice among many."
He spread his arms dramatically.
"You may call us the Chain Breakers."
He announced. Heck, there was even a little lightning crackling behind him as he announced his name. It seemed like it was done to raise the impact even further.
The Guild Masters stared at the screen with deadpan looks on their faces.
Just... what the hell was he doing...?
They couldn’t understand.
Was he trying to joke around in front of the Supreme Borns?
Or does he not know the Supreme Borns were seeing everything he was doing?
The man, oblivious to their thoughts, just looked at them through the screen and—
"For trillions of years, you have bent your heads before the Supremes. You have served, killed, bled, and died—because someone above told you it was necessary."
He spoke, his voice growing firmer.
"Peace? Justice? Balance?"
He scoffed.
"No. These are chains.
Beautiful, golden chains."
His gaze turned cold.

"You think you are free because you get to live. But what is life when your soul can be ripped apart on command? What is order when a flick of a finger can erase fifty-six entire worlds—and they dare to act surprised?"
For a moment, the man paused. The Guild Leaders frowned. The man stepped closer to the screen; for some reason, the action made his presence seem a bit bigger.
"We destroyed those fifty-six worlds."
He announced, this time, as if he was looking at the Supreme Borns.
"We did not do it for revenge, nor was it for power.
We destroyed them because they were yours and you needed them.
That’s what a War is."
He declared, and in an instant, heavy silence fell on the place.
War.
That was quite a grand word, especially when used in front of the strongest forces in the world.
Was... was this man challenging the Supreme Worlds...?
The Guild Leaders couldn’t even comprehend this concept.
Just who in their right mind would even dare to do something so foolish?
"We are not afraid to burn what you value if it means breaking your throne. And to those watching who think we are evil... remember this—"
He raised a hand.
"We are not the ones who punish truth with soul-ripping torment.
We are not the ones who demand loyalty through fear."
His voice dropped low, almost a whisper.
"We do not believe in mercy that comes after the screams."
These words seemed to specifically target Light—saying what no one else dared to say...
The Darkness’s grin widened even further. He had now decided to make his death even less painful. This was far too entertaining.
Of course, the man didn’t know what he was thinking, neither did he care. His voice rose again and,
"We are the Chain Breakers. We are the fire that will melt the illusion of peace that you people have created.
Keep this in mind..."
His eyes glinted and—
"This is merely the beginning."
He grinned, his voice becoming more and more terrorizing.
"We destroyed 56 Mercenary Worlds that wanted nothing more than just to serve you.
And we’ll do it again—not just the Mercenary Worlds,
We will destroy every world that bows to you.
We will erase every being that serves you.
We will drag your name through blood and ash.
We will show your so-called ’followers’ what happens when they put faith in ’false gods’.
And when they look to you for help—
You. Will. Do. Nothing.
Because that is the truth you fear the most, isn’t it?
That you, the oh-so-mighty ’Supreme Worlds’—
Cannot protect what’s yours."
He announced, and heavy, terrifying silence fell over the place. The man on the screen stared right at the Supreme Borns, his golden eyes shining so clearly that it... was overwhelming them?
Before the Supreme Borns could even understand this odd feeling, the man on the screen stepped even closer. The light around him shimmered with chaotic energy, distorting the space behind his figure.
"This is what is going to happen now—
From this day,
Your rule will rot.
Your influence will burn.
And your name...
It will no longer command fear, but suspicion and doubt.
The people will begin to question.
If the mighty Supremes cannot stop a few of us...
Then how mighty are you, really?
Your word will lose its weight.
Your decrees will be challenged.
And your silence will scream louder than any threat you’ve ever made.
You will watch your power erode.
Kingdoms will laugh in private.
Worlds will hesitate to kneel.
You will be turned into a myth.
A ghost of what once ruled.
And when the questions turn to mockery...
Do you know what you will do in return?"
The man questioned. His tone was now even more mockful.
"You will retreat."
He announced.
"You will retreat into your Worlds, behind your Infinities.
You will cower.
And your Palaces of eternal light will become your Prison—Prisons with no Gates because you, the Prisoners, would never want to leave.
After all—
You will be too terrified of stepping into a Universe that no longer bows.
Because out here...
You will see us."
