Was he trying to joke around in front of the Supreme Borns?
Or does he not know the Supreme Borns were seeing everything he was doing?
The man, oblivious to their thoughts, just looked at them through the screen and—
"For trillions of years, you have bent your heads before the Supremes.
You have served, killed, bled, and died—because someone above told you it was necessary."
He spoke, his voice growing firmer.
"Peace?
Justice?
Balance?"
He scoffed.
"No.
These are chains.
Beautiful, golden chains."
His gaze turned cold.
"You think you are free because you get to live.
But what is life when your soul can be ripped apart on command?
What is order when a flick of a finger can erase fifty-six entire worlds—and they dare to act surprised?"
For a moment, the man paused.
The Guild Leaders frowned.
The man stepped closer to the screen; for some reason, the action made his presence seem a bit bigger.
"We destroyed those fifty-six worlds."
He announced, this time, as if he was looking at the Supreme Borns.
"We did not do it for revenge, nor was it for power.
We destroyed them because they were yours and you needed them.
That’s what a War is."
He declared, and in an instant, heavy silence fell on the place.
War.
That was quite a grand word, especially when used in front of the strongest forces in the world.
Was... was this man challenging the Supreme Worlds...?
The Guild Leaders couldn’t even comprehend this concept.
Just who in their right mind would even dare to do something so foolish?
"We are not afraid to burn what you value if it means breaking your throne.
And to those watching who think we are evil... remember this—"
He raised a hand.
"We are not the ones who punish truth with soul-ripping torment.
We are not the ones who demand loyalty through fear."
His voice dropped low, almost a whisper.
"We do not believe in mercy that comes after the screams."
These words seemed to specifically target Light—saying what no one else dared to say...
The Darkness’s grin widened even further.
He had now decided to make his death even less painful.
This was far too entertaining.
Of course, the man didn’t know what he was thinking, neither did he care.
His voice rose again and,
"We are the Chain Breakers.
We are the fire that will melt the illusion of peace that you people have created.
Keep this in mind..."
His eyes glinted and—
"This is merely the beginning."
He grinned, his voice becoming more and more terrorizing.
"We destroyed 56 Mercenary Worlds that wanted nothing more than just to serve you.
And we’ll do it again—not just the Mercenary Worlds,
We will destroy every world that bows to you.
We will erase every being that serves you.
We will drag your name through blood and ash.
We will show your so-called ’followers’ what happens when they put faith in ’false gods’.
And when they look to you for help—
You.
Will.
Do.
Nothing.
Because that is the truth you fear the most, isn’t it?
That you, the oh-so-mighty ’Supreme Worlds’—
Cannot protect what’s yours."
He announced, and heavy, terrifying silence fell over the place.
The man on the screen stared right at the Supreme Borns, his golden eyes shining so clearly that it... was overwhelming them?
Before the Supreme Borns could even understand this odd feeling, the man on the screen stepped even closer.
The light around him shimmered with chaotic energy, distorting the space behind his figure.
"This is what is going to happen now—
From this day,
Your rule will rot.
Your influence will burn.
And your name...
It will no longer command fear, but suspicion and doubt.
The people will begin to question.
If the mighty Supremes cannot stop a few of us...
Then how mighty are you, really?
Your word will lose its weight.
Your decrees will be challenged.
And your silence will scream louder than any threat you’ve ever made.
You will watch your power erode.
Kingdoms will laugh in private.
Worlds will hesitate to kneel.
You will be turned into a myth.
A ghost of what once ruled.
And when the questions turn to mockery...
Do you know what you will do in return?"
The man questioned.
His tone was now even more mockful.
"You will retreat."
He announced.
"You will retreat into your Worlds, behind your Infinities.
You will cower.
And your Palaces of eternal light will become your Prison—Prisons with no Gates because you, the Prisoners, would never want to leave.
After all—
You will be too terrified of stepping into a Universe that no longer bows.
Because out here...
You will see us."

chapters.title: Chapter 2088: A Hunt.
paragraphs: "Your Palaces of eternal light will become your Prison,
Prisons with no Gates because you, the Prisoners, would never want to leave.
After all—
You will be too terrified of stepping into a Universe that no longer bows.
Because out here...
You will see us."
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over the place as those words echoed throughout the boundaries of Vael’Terros. With so many screens showing the same video, every being present here heard them.
The Guild Masters stared at the Supreme Borns, terrified. This was the first time they had seen someone speak such words to the beings of the Supreme Worlds.
The Four Supreme Borns stared at the screen with solemn looks on their faces. This time, even Darkness was no exception. His amused smile was long gone, but—
This wasn’t the end.
Bzzz
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
It started with a few, but soon, almost every Guild Master present in Vael’Terros sensed their Call Artifacts ringing.
And it wasn’t just them—
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
The Supreme Worlds were the same, their Call Artifacts were reacting as well. Without any change in his expression, Balance took out his Artifact and activated it.
And then—
"M-My Lord..."
The truth was revealed.
Vael’Terros wasn’t the only place this message was being received.
Every single High-Level World saw it, even some lower-level worlds saw it as well. This message,
It was seen throughout the Universe.
The number of witnesses was so high that even if the Supreme Worlds wished to silence them, they wouldn’t be able to hide the truth—they would only be able to bury it.
Sure, if they gave the orders, no being throughout the Universe would dare to talk about this, but deep in their hearts, everyone would know.
The existence of Chain Breakers—it could no longer be unknown. Especially now, when the mercenaries had begun talking. After all, they were the ones affected by it the most.
And as if he knew exactly what was happening, the man on the screen once again extended his hands wide and—
"Welcome to the Era of No Chains."
He announced proudly. Then, as if his golden eyes stared right into the Supreme Borns’ eyes,
"This is only the first day. Fear and despair are still unknown to you.
In your arrogance, I am sure you will try to find the bug and squash it before it sucks too much of your blood.
And I welcome you to try.
I welcome you to come and find us.
After all, despair only begins with failure.
You won’t feel it unless you fail."
The man paused for a moment, then, his face behind his veil distorted as he grinned widely and—
"I welcome you—
—to Fail.
—to Fall.
—to experience your first defeat.
I welcome you to be humiliated.
I’ll be waiting."
With that, the screen disappeared and from the start till the very end, not a soul dared to speak.

And this didn’t just happen in Vael’Terros—every world or being who received this message stared at the screen without daring to utter even a single word, almost as if they were scared that something was going to happen if they did.
Of course, this did not happen because everyone was scared of these people who called themselves Chain Breakers, no, they were scared of the words they used and the ones they used them against.
They were scared of the Supreme Worlds’ retaliation, and this was even truer for the Guild Masters standing in Vael’Terros.
They stared at the Supreme Borns, their bodies trembling in fear. The last thing they wanted was to die because some fools did not know what they were doing.
Yes, that was their opinion of the Chain Breakers—
Fools who did not know what they were doing.
And the Supreme Borns...
They remained silent for a while until—
"To experience our first defeat, huh?"
Darkness grinned, his hoarse voice echoing throughout Vael’Terros, sending shivers down already scared Guild Masters.
"Now I wish to experience it."

He commented, the leisure and arrogance in his voice could not be hidden. Clearly, he did not believe he was going to lose, and he wasn’t the only one. No one—neither the beings from the Supreme Worlds nor others from the rest of the Universe—believed it.
They knew the Chain Breakers wouldn’t be seeing the next day.
What surprised them was that someone like them appeared—someone brave enough to actually challenge them.
"I guess we have been far too kind, haven’t we?"
Darkness grinned. He then turned towards Light and—
"This is what happens when you try to bring Light to this world."
Yes, he began pushing his World’s agendas.

"If we had continued to show our strength, if we had continued to wage wars, if we had continued massacres and destruction, if we had spread Darkness like it was meant to, things would have been different today."
Again the Guild Masters trembled at those words. In their minds, they once again cursed these foolish bastards who had now angered the Supremes.
The only good thing was—
"You are giving too much importance to some bugs. The Darkness you love so much is limiting your vision."
Light spoke, countering Darkness’ words.
After all, he couldn’t just let him speak whatever he wanted. He still needed to keep his side so he didn’t get overwhelmed. If he returned like this, it would be too humiliating.
"No matter how much you show yourself, such reckless fools will always appear. Following what you mention will only brand us as tyrants, but that is not who we are."
As he spoke, his words got nods of approval by the Guild Masters below. Indeed, the beings from the Supreme World of Light were different.

They saw the bigger picture and honestly, this was all working in favor of the Supreme World of Light. It was showing the Universe—especially these Guild Masters—just how important their existence was.
Seeing this, Light continued,
"We are the Keepers of Peace, and we will get to the root of this disturbance and—"
"Annihilate them."
Darkness interrupted with a grin.

He no longer cared about public opinion or the battle between Light and Darkness. After all, he already knew the truth—no matter how much they fought for a momentary victory, in the end, it was all pointless.
After all, all their small victories would amount to nothing if the Infinites above them did not make a move.
To destroy Light, the Supreme Darkness needed to move, and till then, all this was pointless—a wasteful effort that wasn’t nearly entertaining enough compared to this new toy he just found.
The Darkness only wished that his new toy didn’t break very quickly. He still needed at least some degree of resistance to make it interesting.
"That is enough."
Suddenly, Balance spoke up.
"This is merely a minor inconvenience."
He mentioned.
"But an inconvenience nonetheless."
He stared at Eternity and he nodded as well.
"We do not have the reports from the Worlds they devoured. Some of those worlds were considered quite big in the Mercenary World. We cannot exclude their input in our final report."
Balance nodded at those words—not just him, Light and even Darkness nodded as well.
They were the Supreme Borns. Because they were sent on this mission, the result shouldn’t be anything short of perfection.
That was their firm belief.
So despite having tens of thousands of Mercenary World Leaders standing beneath them, their focus was on the representatives of the Fifty-Six Worlds who were killed and didn’t appear.
In an instant, they came up with a plan—

"Find all the mercenaries that survived. Find them, read their memories, look for the ones compiling the report, and recreate their report from their memories. Also, recreate these Mercenary Worlds from the mercenary memories.

Gather every mercenary who has ever been to these worlds, read their memories, and recreate these Worlds. Recover the memory of every event, every mission, every little thing that happened in these worlds from the start to finish for these past 10,000 years."
Yes, that was the grand plan.

They would recreate the Mercenary Worlds that were destroyed from the mercenary memories. They would scan the memories of all the mercenaries who had been to these worlds even once and recreate the timeline for the past 10,000 years.
A ridiculous plan.
With how busy the Mercenary Worlds are, these people were thinking of reading complete memories of billions and billions of mercenaries, just to make sure there were no mistakes from their side.
What’s worse?
These people could actually pull it off.
To normal people, finding billions of mercenaries with no leads whatsoever might be difficult, but—
For them...
"Make an announcement. Tell all the mercenaries to come here.
They have a month."
Eternity announced.
Yes, that was how easy it was.
All they needed to do was announce, and the billions of mercenaries would have no choice but to agree to their words and leave whatever they were doing to get here.
"Not everyone will come."

Light spoke. After all, not everyone wanted to have their memories read. Plus, these were mercenaries—they were already much more reckless compared to normal people. There were bound to be a few fighters.
"It does not matter. We will read the memories of those who do. Through them, we will find the others who dared to hide."
Eternity spoke, and Darkness grinned as well.
"It will be like a hunt.
Heh.
It is much more interesting this way."

chapters.title: Chapter 2089: The hunt had indeed begun.
paragraphs: "So it will be like a hunt."
Darkness grinned.
"I accept, it is much more interesting that way."
He nodded.
Eternity nodded back.

"While we are at it, we will also look for these Chain Breakers. The only connection they have with this incident is the beings who devoured the Fifty-Six Worlds and the Guild Master whose body burst into pieces just now.
Through mercenaries’ memories, we will try to find the world devourers. If they are dead set on hiding, I doubt they have left any witnesses alive, but the memories will give us something to work on.
We will mark any oddities in any beings or any events we see. If the search is thorough enough, I refuse to believe we will not find anything."
"Does this mean we need to wait for a month before we even begin our counterattack?"
Darkness questioned, clearly not liking the situation.

He understood that the mercenaries spread throughout the world did not have the means to get to them in an instant. Most of them are Sovereigns who do not even own a spacecraft. Those who did had very slow ones, and it would take them about a month to get to them—and this is when they tried their very best.

The time limit of one month set by Eternity was actually quite well thought out considering what and who they were dealing with. And even though none of the Supreme Borns actually cared about people when they gave orders,

They also knew that if the time limit given to them was simply impossible to follow, most mercenaries would simply quit and take their own lives instead of trying to complete an impossible task and feeling the despair that came with it.
Too many deaths would cause a gap in information, making things difficult for them, so they had to be more careful—hence the month limit.
Darkness understood all that. It was just that... a month was simply too long.
He didn’t even know if he would still be interested in this little thing by the time a month had passed. He needed this to be faster.
And Eternity, knowing exactly what he was thinking, just answered calmly,

"The announcement will tell the mercenaries to come as fast as they possibly can. Their memories will be scanned, so their actions after hearing the announcement will be observed, forcing them to move instantly.
The month-long time limit is just that—a limit. In truth, the mercenaries will have to get here the fastest they can.
So we will have some information to work on. If we are fortunate, that information might reveal exactly what we wish to know."
He spoke, his hollow eyes staring at Darkness meaningfully.
Darkness’s crimson eyes gleamed at those words. Sensing his dissatisfaction, Eternity continued,
"Not to mention we also have his world."
He spoke as he pointed at the ’remains’ of the Guild Master who began all this.
"He comes from a low-level Mercenary World named Zaewver. Although I do not have any expectations,
If the so-called Chain Breakers actually hold even half of the arrogance that man displayed,
They will be waiting for us in Zaewver."
"Don’t be ridiculous."
Those words got a reaction out of Darkness.
"As I said, I do not have any expectation.
But that man did say he will be waiting for us to fail."
Suddenly, a small, light grin appeared on Eternity’s otherwise expressionless face and—
"A part of me tells me that he would like to witness our failure with his own hands."
Eternity once again stared at Darkness.
"If that part of me isn’t wrong,
Then this is an invitation."
"An invitation?"
"Indeed, an invitation to Zaewver, where he would like to watch us fail—and we will prove him wrong."
Eternity’s grin widened.
"So you are saying that he and his little group might be there?"
Darkness grinned as well.
"I do not believe they will have the guts to be there, but then again, I did not believe anyone would have the guts to openly challenge us like this.
Think of it as my wishful thinking."
Eternity answered, and Darkness’s grin widened even further.
"That is enough.
I will believe in your wishful thinking and go there."
He laughed, his crimson eyes shining in excitement.
"You cannot."
Eternity shook his head.
"Huh?"
"We still do not know how strong they are."
"...you think I will lose?"
Instantly, the air around Darkness changed. The Guild Masters underneath all froze in fear, as a suffocating energy surrounded them, ready to corrode their very souls.
But then—
"Do not be foolish."
Eternity shook his head.
"You are too strong. They might not reveal themselves if you go there.
I will go instead."
"Hah?"
Darkness tilted his head in a ridiculous manner.
"Are you saying you are weaker than me?"
He grinned.
Eternity, however, didn’t react to his taunts. Instead—
"I will have a way to find them."
Darkness couldn’t retort against those words. He knew just how resourceful these Eternity bastards were.
"I will also be needing your subordinates."
Eternity mentioned, staring at the other Supreme Borns, instantly getting a reaction out of them.
"Why is that?"
Light questioned.
"You do not expect me to do everything on my own, do you?"
Eternity questioned as if it was the most obvious thing in the world.
"Why not use your own subordinates then?"
Light questioned back.
"Then I’ll be taking all the credit."
Eternity shrugged, and in an instant—
"Do you need the direct borns or outer subordinates?"
Balance questioned.
Clearly, none of them wanted to give away their credit, especially after they came all the way here.
"I simply need a workforce, type does not matter."
Eternity shrugged. Balance nodded with the same nonchalance and took out his Call Artifact, passing orders to his subordinates.
In an instant, three beings who looked similar to him but had a much weaker presence and about ten other beings appeared in front of him, all bowing in unison.
Balance nodded, only acknowledging the existence of three beings who looked similar to him. He then turned towards Eternity and—
"Three Direct Borns and Ten Outer Subordinates. Will that be enough?"
"Yes."

Eternity nodded. He just needed to pass down the orders. How these people completed those orders, whether they called more men to do it or followed the instructions on their own, it was none of his concern.
Seeing this, Light and Darkness moved as well, both of them summoning their subordinates with a similar composition of three Direct Borns and ten Outer Subordinates.
Just like that, the party of thirty-nine was created.
"Take care of things here."
Eternity spoke as he stared at Balance.
He waved his hand as well, and five of his Direct Born subordinates appeared in front of him.
"You will not need them, but if you do, use them however you see fit."
Balance nodded, staring at the five Eternity Borns. The five of them bowed, showing their respect, and Balance simply nodded.
With that, Eternity finally left with the party that was created just now, and Balance once again turned back towards the Guild Leaders beneath and—
"Continue."
He ordered as if nothing had happened.
The Guild Leaders did not dare make him wait either—not after everything that had happened. The last thing they wanted was for the Supreme Borns to take out their anger on them.

The reporting continued, this time even more efficiently than before. The Guild Masters made sure there was not even a second-long delay between two Guild Leaders entering the chamber. Even when the chamber turned red and a soul was ripped apart, creating a spectacle for all to see, this did not change.

Only the Guild Masters who knew their reports were incomplete for whatever reason tried different ways of meeting the same fate, some even trying to take their own lives. But with Balance in charge, it simply did not work.
They were already under the Supreme Borns’ influence—they no longer had control over their own lives.
The only thing they could now do was to wait for their deaths.
’Do you think they will come?’
"I hope they do."
On the other side, near the world named Zaewver, a man cloaked in black silver robes and a veil covering his face smirked as he heard a question.
Soon, he removed his cloak, revealing his absurdly handsome face, and his grin widened even further.
"I realllyyy hope they do."
He laughed.
’I don’t understand...’
Suddenly, Lyriana frowned.
’You could have altered your appearance using your powers. Why bother wearing a veil?’
She questioned.
"For dramatic effects, of course."
Nux answered confidently.
Lyriana blinked, not knowing what it even meant.
"Come on, a veil obviously adds a more mysterious charm."
’You are not trying to charm them.’
Lyriana answered with a deadpan look on her face.
"I do not try to charm anyone, my Queen.
It happens on its own.
I can’t control it."
Nux laughed, and the women just sighed.
They just couldn’t believe that this man was about to have his first face-off against the Supreme Worlds.
"Are you ready?"
Suddenly, Nux took out a Call Artifact and questioned, and from the other side—
"I am."
Sharnoth nodded with a determined look on her face.
The hunt had indeed begun.

sentences.text: "So it will be like a hunt."
Darkness grinned.
"I accept, it is much more interesting that way."
He nodded.
Eternity nodded back.
"While we are at it, we will also look for these Chain Breakers.
The only connection they have with this incident is the beings who devoured the Fifty-Six Worlds and the Guild Master whose body burst into pieces just now.
Through mercenaries’ memories, we will try to find the world devourers.
If they are dead set on hiding, I doubt they have left any witnesses alive, but the memories will give us something to work on.
We will mark any oddities in any beings or any events we see.
If the search is thorough enough, I refuse to believe we will not find anything."
"Does this mean we need to wait for a month before we even begin our counterattack?"
Darkness questioned, clearly not liking the situation.
He understood that the mercenaries spread throughout the world did not have the means to get to them in an instant.
Most of them are Sovereigns who do not even own a spacecraft.
Those who did had very slow ones, and it would take them about a month to get to them—and this is when they tried their very best.
The time limit of one month set by Eternity was actually quite well thought out considering what and who they were dealing with.
And even though none of the Supreme Borns actually cared about people when they gave orders,

They also knew that if the time limit given to them was simply impossible to follow, most mercenaries would simply quit and take their own lives instead of trying to complete an impossible task and feeling the despair that came with it.
Too many deaths would cause a gap in information, making things difficult for them, so they had to be more careful—hence the month limit.
Darkness understood all that.
It was just that... a month was simply too long.
He didn’t even know if he would still be interested in this little thing by the time a month had passed.
He needed this to be faster.
And Eternity, knowing exactly what he was thinking, just answered calmly,
"The announcement will tell the mercenaries to come as fast as they possibly can.
Their memories will be scanned, so their actions after hearing the announcement will be observed, forcing them to move instantly.
The month-long time limit is just that—a limit.
In truth, the mercenaries will have to get here the fastest they can.
So we will have some information to work on.
If we are fortunate, that information might reveal exactly what we wish to know."
He spoke, his hollow eyes staring at Darkness meaningfully.
Darkness’s crimson eyes gleamed at those words.
Sensing his dissatisfaction, Eternity continued,
"Not to mention we also have his world."
He spoke as he pointed at the ’remains’ of the Guild Master who began all this.
"He comes from a low-level Mercenary World named Zaewver.
Although I do not have any expectations,
If the so-called Chain Breakers actually hold even half of the arrogance that man displayed,
They will be waiting for us in Zaewver."
"Don’t be ridiculous."
Those words got a reaction out of Darkness.
"As I said, I do not have any expectation.
But that man did say he will be waiting for us to fail."
Suddenly, a small, light grin appeared on Eternity’s otherwise expressionless face and—
"A part of me tells me that he would like to witness our failure with his own hands."
Eternity once again stared at Darkness.
"If that part of me isn’t wrong,
Then this is an invitation."
"An invitation?"
"Indeed, an invitation to Zaewver, where he would like to watch us fail—and we will prove him wrong."
Eternity’s grin widened.
"So you are saying that he and his little group might be there?"
Darkness grinned as well.
"I do not believe they will have the guts to be there, but then again, I did not believe anyone would have the guts to openly challenge us like this.
Think of it as my wishful thinking."
Eternity answered, and Darkness’s grin widened even further.
"That is enough.
I will believe in your wishful thinking and go there."
He laughed, his crimson eyes shining in excitement.
"You cannot."
Eternity shook his head.
"Huh?"
"We still do not know how strong they are."
"...you think I will lose?"
Instantly, the air around Darkness changed.
The Guild Masters underneath all froze in fear, as a suffocating energy surrounded them, ready to corrode their very souls.
But then—
"Do not be foolish."
Eternity shook his head.
"You are too strong.
They might not reveal themselves if you go there.
I will go instead."
"Hah?"
Darkness tilted his head in a ridiculous manner.
"Are you saying you are weaker than me?"
He grinned.
Eternity, however, didn’t react to his taunts.
Instead—
"I will have a way to find them."
Darkness couldn’t retort against those words.
He knew just how resourceful these Eternity bastards were.
"I will also be needing your subordinates."
Eternity mentioned, staring at the other Supreme Borns, instantly getting a reaction out of them.
"Why is that?"
Light questioned.
"You do not expect me to do everything on my own, do you?"
Eternity questioned as if it was the most obvious thing in the world.
"Why not use your own subordinates then?"
Light questioned back.
"Then I’ll be taking all the credit."
Eternity shrugged, and in an instant—
"Do you need the direct borns or outer subordinates?"
Balance questioned.
Clearly, none of them wanted to give away their credit, especially after they came all the way here.
"I simply need a workforce, type does not matter."
Eternity shrugged.
Balance nodded with the same nonchalance and took out his Call Artifact, passing orders to his subordinates.
In an instant, three beings who looked similar to him but had a much weaker presence and about ten other beings appeared in front of him, all bowing in unison.
Balance nodded, only acknowledging the existence of three beings who looked similar to him.
He then turned towards Eternity and—
"Three Direct Borns and Ten Outer Subordinates.
Will that be enough?"
"Yes."
Eternity nodded.
He just needed to pass down the orders.
How these people completed those orders, whether they called more men to do it or followed the instructions on their own, it was none of his concern.
Seeing this, Light and Darkness moved as well, both of them summoning their subordinates with a similar composition of three Direct Borns and ten Outer Subordinates.
Just like that, the party of thirty-nine was created.
"Take care of things here."
Eternity spoke as he stared at Balance.
He waved his hand as well, and five of his Direct Born subordinates appeared in front of him.
"You will not need them, but if you do, use them however you see fit."
Balance nodded, staring at the five Eternity Borns.
The five of them bowed, showing their respect, and Balance simply nodded.
With that, Eternity finally left with the party that was created just now, and Balance once again turned back towards the Guild Leaders beneath and—
"Continue."
He ordered as if nothing had happened.
The Guild Leaders did not dare make him wait either—not after everything that had happened.
The last thing they wanted was for the Supreme Borns to take out their anger on them.
The reporting continued, this time even more efficiently than before.
The Guild Masters made sure there was not even a second-long delay between two Guild Leaders entering the chamber.
Even when the chamber turned red and a soul was ripped apart, creating a spectacle for all to see, this did not change.
Only the Guild Masters who knew their reports were incomplete for whatever reason tried different ways of meeting the same fate, some even trying to take their own lives.
But with Balance in charge, it simply did not work.
They were already under the Supreme Borns’ influence—they no longer had control over their own lives.
The only thing they could now do was to wait for their deaths.
’Do you think they will come?’
"I hope they do."
On the other side, near the world named Zaewver, a man cloaked in black silver robes and a veil covering his face smirked as he heard a question.
Soon, he removed his cloak, revealing his absurdly handsome face, and his grin widened even further.
"I realllyyy hope they do."
He laughed.
’I don’t understand...’
Suddenly, Lyriana frowned.
’You could have altered your appearance using your powers.
Why bother wearing a veil?’
She questioned.
"For dramatic effects, of course."
Nux answered confidently.
Lyriana blinked, not knowing what it even meant.
"Come on, a veil obviously adds a more mysterious charm."
’You are not trying to charm them.’
Lyriana answered with a deadpan look on her face.
"I do not try to charm anyone, my Queen.
It happens on its own.
I can’t control it."
Nux laughed, and the women just sighed.
They just couldn’t believe that this man was about to have his first face-off against the Supreme Worlds.
"Are you ready?"
Suddenly, Nux took out a Call Artifact and questioned, and from the other side—
"I am."
Sharnoth nodded with a determined look on her face.
The hunt had indeed begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 2090: Once again, luck was not on their side.
paragraphs: ‘Do we know how many of them are coming?’
Ember questioned curiously.
“We don’t even know whether they are coming or not, my Dragon.”
Nux answered with a light chuckle.
‘What about the other Guild Master we left to keep an eye on the situation?’
Ember questioned.
Obviously, they didn’t just have one spy, that was foolish. Amaya made sure to have more than a few, making sure they got live updates on everything and possibly a head start in this situation.
‘They were found out the moment I deployed the first.’
Melia shook her head,
‘I had to forcefully erase their memories and ruin their minds to sever the link between me and them.’
The Vampire explained.
Ember turned silent, Riona, on the other hand, was worried,
‘Is it possible to recover their memories?’
‘I do not think so.’
Melia shook her head again.
‘I basically ruined their mind completely, recovering their memory would be similar to bringing back the dead.’
‘We do not know what methods they have.’
Rune muttered.

They had to be careful, after all, they were dealing with the Supreme Worlds here. Of course, Melia knew this as well and since this was the direct face-off with the Supremes, the Vampire knew she had to be careful, else her husband was going to lose his mind.
‘Even if they did somehow recover his memories, they won’t find me.
I blinded him before taking over his mind.’
‘What if they somehow make a connection and figure out it was you who took over his mind?’
Of course, this was purely just a guess, but Rune still wanted to be careful.
‘That isn’t possible. I no longer belong to the Main Universe. It is impossible to create a connection between me and him or else we would have been found out a long time ago.’
This time, the Vampire was even more confident.
‘...and what if they do?’
The Cat questioned in a grim tone and at those words...
‘If they do, we all die.’
Melia just shrugged.
Again, they had to interact with the Supremes one day or another. They needed the Primordial Energy they had the power over, or else Nux wouldn’t be able to progress any further.
Yes, the extent of the enemy’s abilities was unknown, but they were no different.
The enemy had no clue about them either.
Actually, they had a much more ridiculous advantage compared to the enemies because they were in shadows, they had a different Universe.
A literal, entirely separate Universe on their side. There was no way any enemy could guess the extent of their abilities.

Even if their abilities were unknown, they had no other choice but to trust their own abilities and methods that they had been using all this while and deal a big blow when the enemy was still looking down on them.
‘...does this mean we truly do not have a way to know if they are coming or not?’
Ember questioned again. The wait was making her somewhat anxious.
‘They will come.’
Suddenly, Amaya spoke with certainty.
‘I will look down on them if they do not.
The words you spoke were meant as a direct challenge. With how arrogant they are, they will never not accept such a challenge.
The only way that is possible is that they did not even interpret our message as a challenge, and if that is truly the case,
I will look down on them.’
The Devourer spoke. The plan she made had its flaws, but if this succeeded, what they would get in return would be far more valuable than Vexarion’s life.

Honestly, the Devourer couldn’t care less about that bastard. Rather, she actually wanted him to escape. She had seen that woman’s eyes, she saw her desperation and her neediness. Amaya could tell that the moment Nux gave her what she wanted,
Whether he wanted to or not, she would be his.
She would dedicate her everything to him.
She would be... another her.
Yes, Amaya could see it in those eyes when she first saw her.
Sharnoth Nocthys... that woman was similar to her and Aeliana.

And because she knew that, she also knew Nux knew it as well. At this point, it wasn’t even a possibility, it was certainty. Nux wouldn’t be able to resist her in any way. The charm of a crazy woman attracted him like no other.
Sharnoth will become her sister, and Amaya did not like this competition at all.
‘Tsk.’
The Devourer snorted inwardly. Soon, however, she shook her head and focused on what was important instead.
The three remaining Primordial Energies.
This was their Final Goal, everything they had put in so much effort for.

The Supreme Worlds still did not know that Nux had the power to devour his enemies’ Laws. So even if they could come up with a way to counter his ability, they wouldn’t have anything right now because of their lack of information.
Amaya planned to use that to her advantage.
She openly challenged their authority, angered them, then invited them for a direct confrontation. She wanted the angered bull to mindlessly charge at them.

Of course, she didn’t come up with all this without thinking. She had a conversation with Lord Azriel. She remembered his warning to Nux, telling him not to go near the Supreme Worlds, and she wanted to know why he said that.
‘The Supreme Worlds are ruled by Infinities. If they are even half as strong as me, their domain will be strong enough to cover the entirety of their respective worlds.

Unlike me, they have the freedom to use their powers however they wish, so I wouldn’t be surprised if the entirety of their world is under their influence—not through the World’s Will, but under their direct influence.

Nux’s quirk of not being detected by a World’s Will is useful, but in the Supreme Worlds, it wouldn’t work since he would directly be entering the enemy’s domain. There is no way they would not sense him.
And once they do, and once they realize his strange quirk,
They will capture him alive, and he will be helpless to do anything.’
The Vampire Progenitor explained.
Then, as if warning the group even further, he continued,
‘If this does happen, then even if I were as strong as I was before, saving him would be impossible.
An Infinity’s control over his Domain is absolute.
It is even above the Universe’s Will.’
‘Even the Universe’s Will?’
Amaya raised her eyebrow. Even Nux was surprised when he heard that.
‘That is correct. The Universe thinks of it as a ‘gift’ to the beings closest to it.
Even the Universe does not know what happens inside an Infinity’s Domain because it has no control over it.
As I said, inside his Domain, an Infinity is absolute, even above the very Universe.’
Azriel spoke, and recalling those words, Amaya momentarily trembled.
She finally understood why Azriel warned them the way he did. Getting inside an Infinity’s Domain was certain death—even Nux was no exception to this.
And since they did not know how much area their domain actually covers, it was better to stay far, far, far away from the Supreme Worlds, just like Azriel told them to.
Amaya obviously had no plan to go against the Vampire Progenitor’s warning.
Therefore, she had to come up with this plan.
Sneaking into the Supreme World wasn’t possible. However, since they still needed their Laws, the only way around was to bring the Supreme bastards out instead.
And the opportunity for that was right in front of her.
The Supreme Borns were out, their arrogance as high as ever. They now had the option to go for them, but the problem was, all four of these Supreme Borns were Eternals.
Even if they had Sharnoth with them, she was nowhere strong enough to take all four of them at the same time. It would honestly be surprising if she was strong enough to take on even one of them.
After all, the Supreme Borns were strong.

Even Amaya, who was confident enough to take on any Transcendent-level enemy, wasn’t sure she could actually defeat a Transcendent-level Supreme Born. Aeliana, Astaria, Vyriana, Melia, and Felberta—they were no exception to this either.

These women were strong. They had Absolute Laws. They were probably the strongest at their stage, and were strong enough to take multiple Transcendent-level enemies at the same time and win with ease if they did not have Absolute Laws, but—
The Supreme Borns were stronger.

Not only did they have Absolute Laws, their Absolute Laws came from Primordial Energies. They had a higher understanding of their Laws. They had trillions and trillions of years of piled-up knowledge they could use to get stronger more efficiently, and they had much stronger weapons.
In theory, the women were no match against them.

Therefore, Amaya had to lure them into her plan. She had to target weaker Supreme Borns. After all, it would be beneath Eternal-level Supreme Borns, who came here on a mission, to go after a lowly terrorist group just because they provoked them.
Amaya was hoping that they would send their subordinates instead.
She was hoping that they would send weaker, Transcendent-level Supreme Borns here so they could use Sharnoth to capture them, ultimately allowing Nux to devour them and complete his Universe.
But...
Once again, luck was not on their side.
“They are here.”
Nux, who sensed their arrival, spoke with a solemn look on his face.
Yes, things did not go according to the plan.
“The one leading them is an Eternal from the Supreme World of Eternity.”
Nux declared. The women, seeing the Supreme Party through Nux’s eyes, stared at the situation solemnly as well.

Amaya was even considering retreat. After all, these Eternals won’t always be everywhere, and it was very much possible for them to find Transcendents working alone in the future because of how big this incident had become.
But then—
The Devourer froze in horror when she saw Eternity looking directly at the screen.
He...
He had spotted Nux.

chapters.title: Chapter 2091: You might die.
paragraphs: ’Nux did he—’
Amaya called out, her body frozen as she saw the Eternity staring at the screen as if he had spotted Nux.
For an instant, Nux’s face turned grim as well. He was currently using Vulpiana’s Law of Timeless Veil to hide himself inside a different dimension.
It was one of his most trusted abilities, an ability he used to get an upper hand in battles against Transcendent-level enemies.
Heck, it was the same ability that also allowed him to sneak behind Vexarion, an Eternal, and take his arm despite there being the ridiculous difference of two phases between them.
It was something that had never failed him before, but...
If it failed him today...
Just as Nux was thinking about everything and was trying to come up with a countermeasure, Eternity’s gaze moved away from him as he continued to scan the surroundings.
It was less than a second, to be clear. Eternity’s gaze did not even stop at him; it seemed like he was only scanning the surroundings.
’No, he didn’t, it was a coincidence.’
Nux answered, sighing in relief.
Hearing those words, Amaya, together with the rest of the tensed-up women, sighed in relief as well. Their bodies almost gave out and they hadn’t even truly clashed with these beings.
It just showed just how ridiculously dangerous they were.
Or more accurately, just how strong of an impression these beings had on others.
Even they, who had absolute confidence in their husband’s ability, had faltered for a moment.
’Nux, let’s leave. We will get another chance in the fut—’
Before Amaya could complete her sentence, she and the other women noticed the screen shifted as Nux moved much faster than any of them could react to.
Yes, despite being a Primordial, his reaction speed was faster than Transcendent-level beings, and this reaction speed just saved his life.
"Oh?"
The women heard a voice.
A hollow, calm voice that was filled with slight amusement.
"You moved."
Eternity spoke, the amusement in his voice did not die down.
"I have never seen a Primordial react so quickly," he spoke, as he stood where Nux once did. As for Nux...
He was now standing a few hundred meters away from him, looking at Eternity with a grim look on his face.
He had already made his move.
A move that the Eternity sensed in an instant and teleported away, dodging a destructive wave that could have done severe damage.
Of course, even then, the amusement on his face did not change. Rather, it only increased as he turned towards the woman who just appeared out of nowhere.
"Energy of Chaos, huh?
Now this is surprising."
He commented.
"I did not think you people had gathered enough strength to make a move.
Or...
Is it desperation?"
He didn’t seem particularly surprised by the Chaos Energy Sharnoth was using and honestly, Nux wasn’t surprised by it either.

Zylarith was behind Umbrasol, he was also behind Sharnoth. These were all things Nux knew about. However, Zylarith had been active for billions and billions of years. There is no way he only appeared a few times all this while.
If the Supreme Worlds did not know that he was actually alive even after all these reckless things he had done, well...
They wouldn’t deserve the title of Supremes then.
They knew.
They knew about the existence of Zylarith, they just did not care enough to do anything about him.
’So they know he is in no position to do anything...’

Nux muttered inwardly, gathering every bit of information he could in this situation. Of course, his mind had already started coming up with a way out, to get something out of this disadvantageous encounter.
He could have escaped. He could have entered his own Universe, where no one could follow him, or he could have died.
All this while, Nux hadn’t just stayed still while spending time with his wives.
He had pushed himself to the limits and had learned quite a few things.
First one was to kill himself instantly.

He had learned an ability to burst his own body into pieces, that too, so quickly that if his opponent was unaware of his ability, then with Nux’s reflexes, the opponent could never stop him from dying and reforming near his wives, successfully escaping from most scenarios.
But honestly, Nux wasn’t particularly fond of any of the two ideas.

Both escaping into his Universe and killing himself would give his opponents an extremely valuable piece of information about him, putting them at an advantage and taking away the surprise factor they had, that too, without getting anything in return.
It was the first exchange between him and the Supreme Worlds; it was essential for his and his wives’ survival for them to get something out of it.
Therefore, instead of running, Nux decided to risk it.
He stared at Sharnoth, who was staring at Eternity with a determined look on her face and he recalled the conversation they had before,
"Are you truly prepared for this?"

After Amaya explained her plan of luring the Supremes out to where they could devour them without the Infinities getting involved, Nux first turned towards Sharnoth, the most important key of this place, and questioned.
"I am."
Sharnoth, who was connected with them using the Call Artifact, answered with a solemn look on her face.
Why use the Call Artifact instead of actually being there with them?

It was because they were still worried about Zylarith. Sharnoth’s Domain was still keeping him away. So even now, she was sitting with her Domain activated and no one around her. From the outside, no one in Khaemorr knew what Sharnoth was actually planning.

Nux was also worried about letting his wives close to Sharnoth. Yes, he trusted her since he saw her memories, but Zylarith still had the ability to momentarily take over Sharnoth’s body, so he had to be careful.
It was much better for Sharnoth to stay cooped up inside her Domain with no one knowing her plans before she actually made a move.
Even Zylarith wouldn’t be able to react to it out of nowhere.
"You might die."
Nux warned with a solemn look on his face.
"We are facing Supremes. Anything can happen. I have a few ways to escape, but you won’t."
"You know I do not care about my life."
Sharnoth answered. She then looked into Nux’s eyes and,
"If I die, I only want one thing:
His pain should be far greater than my mother’s before he dies."
"...if we do not follow through with it, it is highly likely that we will gain enough time to go after Vexarion.
You will be able to take your revenge on your own."
"He won’t accept."
Suddenly, Sharnoth shook her head.
"What...?"
"The Leander Family is already shrouded with mystery.
This combined with the appearance of a mysterious group that dared to stand against the Supreme Worlds will form a connection.

No matter how weak this connection is, for someone as cowardly as Vexarion, it wouldn’t be surprising if he goes back on his word and refuses to face me—at least not until this mysterious group is found."
Nux stayed silent. From the memories he had of Vexarion’s subordinates, he knew what Sharnoth was saying could be true.
"That turtle will not leave his shell, and as long as he hides inside, I cannot kill him."
Sharnoth repeated. Her crimson eyes staring into Nux’s and—
"The only one I can rely on is you."
She spoke with a determined look on her face.
"You are strong, you are resourceful, and if capturing three Supreme Borns from those three Supreme Worlds somehow makes you even stronger,
I am willing to take that risk,
Even if it costs my life."
Nux stayed silent, observing Sharnoth as he recalled everything.
But then—
"I am curious though."
Suddenly, the Eternity began.
"You have the Law of Chaos, then how did you teleport here? I do not sense any Artifact activating."
He questioned with a curious look on his face.
All his interest in Nux had faded away. After all, what could a Primordial even do in this situation?
Sharnoth didn’t answer his question.
In her mind, she was thinking of ways to fight him. The difference in the two’s attitude seemed quite overwhelming.
It looked like Eternity had absolute confidence in himself.
And he did.
"Not going to answer, eh?"
He shrugged.
Then, he slightly stretched his body, as if preparing to move and—
"Well then, I’ll get the answers once I capture you alive and read your memories."
He declared confidently as suddenly, Nux noticed the space around them being locked.
The teleportation had become difficult. Even if they used the strongest Teleportation Artifact, it would take more than a few minutes for it to work.
Yes, the Eternity had cut their escape routes,
Or... that is what he thought.
But—
Suddenly, both Nux and Sharnoth teleported again, appearing far away from Eternity and right in front of his party.
"Now!"
Nux shouted and in an instant,
BOOOOM
Sharnoth deployed her Domain, with all the Supreme Party members trapped inside it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2092: Am I now interesting enough for you?
paragraphs: "Now!"
Nux shouted and in an instant,
BOOOOM
Sharnoth deployed her domain, with all the Supreme Party members trapped inside it.
The moment Nux realized she had succeeded, he quickly diverted all his focus towards Eternity. He wasn’t a fool, he knew the distance between them and the Eternity was not huge.
Heck, the man traveled that distance in an instant, and if he hadn’t reacted, he would have been captured alive.
What’s even more scary?
This bastard wasn’t even taking this seriously.

From the start to finish, the only emotion Eternity had shown all this while was... amusement and curiosity. Nux knew that in his eyes, he was nothing more than a monkey jumping around, doing its mindless shenanigans.
Nux knew Eternity could travel this distance instantly, so even if they had the Supremes under Sharnoth’s domain, the battle wasn’t won.

He was in no position to devour them because Eternity was about to make a move. If he appeared and deployed his domain, his and Sharnoth’s domain would clash, nullifying each other’s effect, freeing the rest of the party.

And Nux, who wanted to avoid that outcome, turned towards Eternity, his mind thinking of different ways he and Sharnoth could stop him together, while also trying to predict what other things this monster might do.
But—
As Nux’s eyes finally fell on Eternity,
He realized something.
The Eternity...
He... he still hadn’t moved.

Nux didn’t understand, he had sensed the Space Laws around them were being altered, making it difficult—almost impossible to use Powers of Space for any normal person. So he understood that the fact that he still managed to teleport together with Sharnoth might have surprised Eternity, making his reaction slower than normal.
Truthfully, this was what Nux was actually hoping.
But even in the best-case scenario in his mind, he didn’t predict the Eternity to not move at all.
He was easily one of the strongest beings Nux had ever encountered, there was no way surprise alone would make him freeze mid-battle.
But...
"You moved."
Eternity commented, impressed again. Of course, his eyes didn’t look at Nux even now, he was focused on Sharnoth.
"What kind of Space Artifact do you have? I do not sense an Energy of a Relic, does this mean it is something not created by the Supreme World of Eternity?"
He questioned, his curiosity now even stronger than before.
"To think you would have someone capable enough to create an Artifact of that level, quite impressive indeed."
He complimented again, his hollow eyes staring at Sharnoth and for a moment, Nux sensed a flicker of greed in them.
Nux could feel it.
This bastard... he wanted to know...
He wanted to know everything about them.
Nux was wondering why this man froze mid-battle like an amateur, but now... he finally realized it.
This monster... he wasn’t considering this to be a battle from the very beginning.
To him... it was... a show.
A show to entertain himself and now satiate his curiosity, even if he had to sacrifice his subordinates’ lives for it.
Yes, the reason he didn’t move and protect his subordinates all this while wasn’t because he couldn’t react in time or was frozen in surprise,
It was because he wanted to see what they were going to do.
He wanted to see if they were going to surprise and entertain him again.
He wanted to know the extent of their ability.
And Nux, who realized all that—
"Heh."
He laughed.
The tension from his body began to ease up.
Being underestimated—no, underestimated was a weak word—he wasn’t being underestimated, he was being utterly ignored.
The only one the Eternity had his eyes on was Sharnoth, and her too, was only being seen as a means of entertainment.
This feeling...
It made Nux grin.
He couldn’t tell how... grateful he was.
’I love arrogant people.’
He confessed in his heart, staring at Eternity as he began walking towards his subordinates leisurely.
From his movements, it was clear that he was no longer tense, almost as if there was no opponent around him at all.
And he couldn’t be blamed for it.
After all, Nux could tell that as long as he showed something that ’surprised’ him, he wouldn’t stop him.
And when he looked at the members of the Supreme Party, whose expressions showed fear as he closed in, he knew he wasn’t wrong.
They had realized it as well.
They were being used as sacrifice.

One more thing that Nux found quite interesting was that the only members who showed fear on their faces were the subordinates, the beings the Supreme Worlds had recruited. The nine Transcendent Level Supreme Borns were different, they stood still, without any change in their expression even in face of their death.
It was almost as if they couldn’t feel this emotion known as fear.

Of course, as interesting as it sounded, for now, Nux did not act on it. He suppressed his sadistic tendencies of wanting to see their entire body reflect the emotion they were incapable of reflecting. After all, he knew what situation he was in.
It wasn’t time to play around.
Even though he was acting leisurely, his guard was still very much up and almost all his focus was on Eternity, making sure he did not make any surprise move.
And just as he got close to the frozen Supreme Party, Eternity reacted.
"Oh?"
It was just a slight tilt of his head.
It looked like he had finally noticed Nux now that he was right in front of his subordinates.
"Is this another trick of yours? Letting your subordinate move?"
He questioned, once again staring at Sharnoth.
And then—
"It is indeed."
Nux spoke up, his grin widening and in an instant, Eternity, who had been ignoring him for a while, finally glanced at him for more than a second.
He recognized him.
"You are the man on that projection."
"Took you long enough."
Nux chuckled lightly.
"I expected more from the so-called Supreme Borns."
He taunted while he prepared his next move.
But the taunt didn’t work,
"It seems that in my excitement, I overestimated your lot."
Eternity sighed.
Learning that the one who said all those words and challenged the Supreme Worlds, even threatening to ’erase their authority,’ was only a Primordial Stage insect, disappointed him.
Sure, he understood that he was just a face and the actual strength behind the Chain Breakers was obviously someone else, but—
The very fact that whoever held the most strength wasn’t even brave enough to step forward, even when they had a way to hide their presence and not get caught, disappointed him even more.
He felt like a fool for actually acting on such empty words, to think he actually came here himself instead of just sending his subordinates...
He truly was disappointed.
What about the fact that his presence saved his subordinates from dying to an enemy Eternal?
Eternity didn’t care about it either. Sure, he could tell the woman was strong. From her domain, it was clear she had an Absolute Law but...
Even then, any one of his Eternal Level subordinates could have dealt with her using the Relics. He had absolutely no need to come here on his own.
Soon however, he shook his head and cleared his mind—
"It is my mistake."
He admitted.
"I was momentarily fooled by your bold words and heightened my expectations.
Whatever, this just pr—"
"Are you sure about it?"
Suddenly, Nux interrupted, and Eternity, who was about to kill him for interrupting his words, widened his eyes in shock.
Nux’s grin widened even further as thick, dark, frighteningly cold black mist surrounded the members of the Supreme Party, and as if to add a final touch—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The very Universe reacted.
Seeing the extremely familiar reaction happen right in front of him, Eternity’s already widened eyes widened even further.
"Y-You..."
He stuttered, his reaction stroking Nux’s ego.
He was no longer a ’monkey doing his own shenanigans.’
He was—
"You are the Anomaly!"
Eternity exclaimed, his words made Nux’s face distort as he successfully devoured the entire Supreme Party right in front of the frozen Eternity.
"Am I now interesting enough for you?"
Nux laughed.
And finally—
When he could no longer sense his subordinates, Eternity came out of his reverie and—
"Hahahaha!"
He laughed out loud.
Nux also noticed how the Space around them was completely sealed, and no, this time, it wasn’t just the Space Laws being altered repeatedly, making using Power of Space impossible.
This time, the Space Laws were removed.
No Space ability, no matter how strong, could now be used here.
Not even Nux could do anything about it.
"Indeed, indeed, you are more than interesting now!
You are the Anomaly!"
Eternity exclaimed, unable to control his excitement. To think he would get his hands on the Anomaly that the Infinities were trying to find so desperately.
This trip became much more worthwhile!

Seeing the extremely familiar reaction happen right in front of him, Eternity’s already widened eyes widened even further.
"Y-You..."
He stuttered, his reaction stroking Nux’s ego.
He was no longer a ’monkey doing his own shenanigans.’
He was—
"You are the Anomaly!"
Eternity exclaimed, his words made Nux’s face distort as he successfully devoured the entire Supreme Party right in front of the frozen Eternity.
"Am I now interesting enough for you?"
Nux laughed.
And finally—
When he could no longer sense his subordinates, Eternity came out of his reverie and—
"Hahahaha!"
He laughed out loud.
Nux also noticed how the Space around them was completely sealed, and no, this time, it wasn’t just the Space Laws being altered repeatedly, making using Power of Space impossible.
This time, the Space Laws were removed.
No Space ability, no matter how strong, could now be used here.
Not even Nux could do anything about it.
"Indeed, indeed, you are more than interesting now!
You are the Anomaly!"
Eternity exclaimed, unable to control his excitement.
To think he would get his hands on the Anomaly that the Infinities were trying to find so desperately.
This trip became much more worthwhile!

chapters.title: Chapter 2093: Are you sure that you can actually win against the two of us alone?
paragraphs: "Am I now interesting enough for you?"
Nux questioned with a big wide grin on his face and—
"Hahahaha!"
The Eternity laughed out loud.
"Indeed, indeed, you are more than interesting now!
You are the Anomaly!"
He exclaimed, sealing the Space around him as he prepared to capture the Anomaly alive.

The Eternity couldn’t help but glee joyfully at this situation. To think that the being who made a mess out of the very Universe, affecting millions of worlds either directly or through the Universe’s Rage, kept even the Infinities guessing about his identity, was merely a... Primordial.
A Primordial who was standing right in front of him.
This changed everything.

Strangely, Eternity’s hollow eyes had begun to shine as different ideas popped into his head. Capturing the Anomaly alive and delivering him to the Infinities to bask in the glory for the rest of his life—yes, it sounded very enticing.
But...
This wasn’t the only enticing idea that came to his mind.
Again, he was standing in front of the being who challenged the very Universe, something even the Infinites who ruled over all couldn’t do, and yet... he was just a Primordial.
What if...
What if that changed?
What if instead of a Primordial, the one who inherited this ridiculous power was an... Eternal?
How different would that be...?
Would it be able to... change the trillions of trillions of years old Power System...?
The thought stirred something inside of him.
Yes, he understood that the thought was traitorous. If the Infinites knew what he was thinking, death would be the last thing he would be worried about—it would be a sweet release.
But...

Eternity was now billions of years old. He was one of the oldest Eternals in the Supreme World of Eternity, one of the few who had seen the Era of Five Supreme Worlds. Most of his initial peers had already ended their existence and entered the reincarnation cycle.
’End’ did not scare him.
Actually, he often found himself thinking about how his end would be—if something like that even existed.
After all, even now, even when most of his peers were gone, he still hadn’t ended himself because he simply couldn’t find an end worthy of him.
But today—
It was different.
He now stood at a fork.
A fork where one path led to certain glory, standing below Four and above the rest.

While the other led to Eternal Damnation, where he would be begging for Death at every moment, but also gave him a sliver of an uncertain, probably even impossible change. To not be standing below Four above the rest... but to stand above All.

Of course, any sane being would choose the first path. Standing below Four and above the rest sounded enticing, especially considering that the Four in question rarely bothered to deal with things. He would essentially be ruling everything.
But...
Eternity wasn’t sane.
No being who has lived for billions of years was.
Simple glory wasn’t enticing enough for him. After all, even now, he was above most beings in the entirety of the Universe.
Other than the Four Infinites, he didn’t truly have to bow in front of anyone.
This so-called ’certain glory’ was a sham.
But this ’change’...
It was different.
Yes, the Eternity had already made a decision.
This will be it.
An ’End’ worthy of him.
There was just... one problem.
"You sealed the Space."
Nux commented as he stared at Eternity with a light, confident smile on his face.
"You sensed it."
Eternity smiled back.
And soon, he realized it as well.
"So it wasn’t her but you,
The one who was using the Power of Space."
Nux just smiled, not saying anything.
He wanted to extend this conversation as long as he could because he needed time.
It was done. With him devouring the Supreme Party, he had finally gathered all Primordial Energies inside his Universe.
However, his Universe still wasn’t complete.
Even though he had ’devoured’ the Supreme Party and their Laws, he still hadn’t connected with them. Those Laws were just... floating in his Universe.
He still needed to connect, comprehend, and then streamline them, forming the true, final three Primordial Laws, before including them in his Universe, completing it for good.
And for that, he needed time.
Honestly, if this was a normal situation, he would have long split the work in his mind, with one side facing the Eternal Level opponent while the other focused on the Laws he had just devoured.
But right now,
He couldn’t divide his focus.
The Eternal he was up against was by no means normal. If he didn’t give his all, this might be the true end.
And because almost all his focus was on his enemy, the time he needed to comprehend those Laws and assimilate them was much higher than normal.
Time he did not think he could buy just by talking, but...
He had no other choice but to try.
The last thing he wanted right now was to face an unpredictable opponent.
Fortunately for him, his opponent wasn’t in a rush either.

"How did you do it? I did not see your Flow of Law, so it means you did not use your Power. Was it an Artifact? But how can a Primordial use an Artifact of that capability? You shouldn’t have enough energy."
Eternity questioned curiously.
"Aren’t you from the Supreme World of Eternity? The so-called ’Knowers of All That Is’? You should know the answer to everything, shouldn’t you?"
Nux teased.
"Actually, let’s make this much more interesting than it currently is.
I will give you three guesses.
If you guess the correct answer, I will tell you one thing about the Universe that you do not know for sure."
He spoke, coming up with the most effective way of buying time.
As for telling Eternity one thing he did not know about?
Who cared about that?
He would say some random gibberish. If he didn’t know about it, how would he know whether it’s the truth or a lie?
Not to mention, Nux wouldn’t have to say anything anyway because the Eternity would never guess it right. After all, his very initial assumption was wrong.

He wasn’t using any Artifacts. He had the Complete Law of Absolute Space. His understanding of the Space Law was greater than any being in the Universe. He understood the changes in Space faster than anyone, and with his mind that helps him analyze and calculate that change much faster than any Primordial, or even Transcendent, or most Eternals, teleporting in a field where the Space Laws were altered was child’s play for him.
As for why Eternity didn’t sense any Law Flow?
Well, that was because the Law he was using simply did not belong to the main Universe—there was no Law Flow to begin with.
This was one of the reasons he was considered an Anomaly in the first place.
Of course, the Eternity did not need to know that. He just needed to waste more time conversing with Nux.
Or at least...
That is what Nux was hoping for.
But...
"The first step to becoming one of the ’Knowers of All That Is’ is understanding how little one truly knows."
The Eternity answered.
"We Eternities know it all because we crave knowledge. Since the time we came into existence, we craved to understand the very secrets of existence itself.
This is the difference between Eternities and other beings of the Universe.
You seek strength, we seek knowledge. Our very existence wishes to know everything there is—it is our deepest, strongest desire.
This is also the reason why, unlike the other Supreme Worlds, we do not accept subordinates. After all, only a True Born can be aligned with our goals and work towards it.
We didn’t reach where we did by ’guessing’ the correct answer.
We chase knowledge—certain knowledge."
He spoke, his words much deeper than Nux was initially expecting.
Maybe... he wasn’t as arrogant as Nux initially believed.
At least, that was the case when it came to acquiring knowledge.
And... this wasn’t good news.
After all, Nux could already see where this was going.
"So instead of playing your game, I will focus on certainty.
I will capture you and learn everything you know using my own certain methods."
Eternity declared, preparing to make a move.
Nux wanted to curse his damn luck, but for now, he focused on what was important.
"Aren’t you getting a little too excited?"
He questioned, trying to stall for time.
"You might die here, you know?"
He warned, momentarily glancing at Sharnoth and—
"Are you sure that you can actually win against the two of us alone?"
He smiled as he took out his trusted sword. Eternity’s expression momentarily changed when he saw Nux’s Bloodedge, but he was more interested in Nux’s words.
"Alone?"
He tilted his head with an ominous grin.
"Who said I was alone?"
And before Nux could realize the meaning behind those words—
"Come out now.
Don’t foolishly believe you can hide from me using the Artifact I created."
Eternity spoke as he stared in a certain direction and in that moment—
"Hahaha! I was wondering when you would call me!"
A dark, menacing, soul-shaking laugh was heard as another being materialized into existence.
Darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 2094: Don’t you dare lose.
paragraphs: “Come out now.
Don’t foolishly believe you can hide from me using the Artifact I created.”
Eternity spoke as he stared in a certain direction.
As mentioned before, his ‘End’ plan was perfect—except for one ‘problem.’
This was the ‘problem.’
Nux turned around to look, his frown deepened when he didn’t see or sense any being.
Was it an empty threat? A distraction?
He wondered in his mind, but then—
“Hahaha! I was wondering when you would call me!”
A dark, menacing, soul-shaking laugh was heard as another being materialized into existence. A being that made Nux falter with his mere presence.
This wasn’t the plan.
The only reason he didn’t run away like Amaya told him to was because he thought only one Eternal came.
But...
Why was he here!?
There was no reason to!
What happened to the Supremes’ arrogance? Why would two of the strongest Eternals come for a mere terrorist group that hadn’t even done anything!?
And Nux wasn’t the only one who thought that,
“Why are you here, Neremoth?”
Eternity questioned as he glanced at the Eternal from the Supreme World of Darkness, Neremoth.

Yes, he knew that Neremoth was here from the very beginning, but this did not mean he knew why he was here. This wasn’t the plan; he specifically said he would be the only one to go. There was no need for two Eternals here.
At his question, Neremoth grinned.
“Why? Does my presence bother you, Zarveth?”
Neremoth questioned, his Grimson eyes shining even more brightly. It was clear that his excitement couldn’t be contained.
“This is not what we agreed on.”

Zarveth, the Eternal of the Supreme World of Eternity, spoke in a strict, dissatisfied tone. As the two Supremes conversed, they completely ignored Nux and Sharnoth, as if their presence simply did not matter.
And it did not. The Space Laws no longer worked here—it was impossible for them to escape. Even if they did try something, with the two of them together, the weaklings did not stand a chance.

Actually, the two Supremes were certain that even without the help of the other, they could take down the opponents. After all, Anomaly or not, with all said and done, a Primordial was still just that—a Primordial.
As for the woman, well, the Supreme Borns never considered those at a similar cultivation stage as them on the same level.
There was no way the enemy Eternal was nearly as strong as taking them.
Honestly, instead of the two opponents in front of them, the biggest concern the two Supremes had was... each other.
And this feeling was mutual; both of them wanted the other to be gone so they could get their hands on the Anomaly.
“Do you truly believe you are in the position to talk about what we agreed on or not?”
At Zarveth’s words, Neremoth questioned with a demonic grin.
“You encountered the Anomaly, and instead of following the Infinities’ direction and informing them about his existence,
You sealed the Space instead, making sure no one gets here.”
“I did it because I did not want the enemy to call reinforcements or escape.”
Zarveth tried to explain, but Neremoth was no fool.
And he did not like to be treated as one either.
“Stop this.”
He spoke, his tone stricter than before.
“We both know what you want.”
At those words, Zarveth’s tone changed as well.
Further games were pointless, so he decided to skip them.
“You knew, yet you still did not report to the Infinities.”
He blamed.
Well, it wasn’t a ‘blame’ per se, it was simply a signal—an offer to stop this pointless squabble here.
After all, just like Neremoth, Zarveth knew what the other wanted as well.
The Anomaly.
As for going against the Infinities, the very fact that Neremoth was here instead of reporting him meant that he was prepared to go against them as well.
Just like him, Neremoth wanted the Anomaly for himself.
So instead of going at each other and letting the fish escape,
Why not work together?
That was Zarveth’s underlying offer.
And understanding every part of it, Neremoth’s eyes shined even more joyfully,
“Yes, I change my statement.
We both know what we want.”
He agreed.
Zarveth stared at Neremoth in silence, and in the end, he passed a light smile as well.
There was no other option—this was indeed the best-case scenario considering the current situation.

As for how they were going to ‘divide’ the Anomaly, well, that can be discussed later. Of course, Zarveth also did not overlook the chances of Neremoth betraying and attacking him after everything was done. After all, he was considering the same thing.
However, they both knew the other would not do that.

The reason was simple—if the two fought each other, the victor wouldn’t be clear. Even if the battle continued for years and one might get a slight advantage over the other, killing each other for good was impossible.
In the end, the one who got the Anomaly would later be at a disadvantage because the other would inform the Infinities about what happened, and after that,
It was only a matter of time before the Anomaly was taken away from them without them getting anything in return.
So unless they had a certain way to kill the other in one shot, fighting each other was no different than sealing their fate for the worse.
Both of them knew this, so they knew that as long as they did not let their guard down, the other would not betray them.
And with that clear,
The two Supreme Borns decided to go against the feared Infinities and act independently—together.
Of course, while the two were having a conversation, the so-called opponents they ignored weren’t just staying still either.
They were making their own plans.

Before this began, Nux used a Slave Seal on Sharnoth. Of course, at Sharnoth’s level, she could break the seal on her own without having to do anything, so it wasn’t exactly a big deal. It was just one of Nux’s trusted methods, using which they could converse whenever needed.
‘Nux, what do we do?’
Sharnoth questioned with a solemn look on her face. She was still considering going against one Eternal, but two... even she knew it was no longer a battle they could win.
‘Can we escape?’
She asked, and Nux...
‘We can’t.’
He shook his head grimly.
‘Space Laws cannot be used here.’

From their expressions, he could tell that the two Eternals weren’t exactly allies—their greed might lead to them fighting each other. Honestly, with how things were, that would be the best-case scenario.
In the chaos, Nux believed he could figure something out. If anything, he would be able to assimilate the Laws he had just gathered and integrate them into his Universe.
But of course, this was only the best-case scenario—a scenario where he got incredibly lucky. And... considering his recent past with Lady Luck...
She wasn’t on his side.
Nux could tell there was a high probability that they would need to face the two of them together, and no matter how he thought about it,
He could not see a way to win.
This...
This might just be it.
‘Nux.’
Suddenly, Sharnoth called out with a determined look on her face.
Nux glanced at her and noticed her crimson eyes shining much more fiercely than ever.
‘You can escape, can’t you?’
She questioned.
Nux turned silent.
‘Answer me. You can escape alive, can you not?’
She questioned, her tone much fiercer than before.
‘Yes.’
Nux nodded.
His Universe’s gate did not depend on Space—he could easily escape without the two Eternals being able to do anything.
But...
If he did that, Sharnoth would be facing the two angered Eternals alone, and... there was no way they would let her have an easy death.

Honestly, Nux had thought of devouring Sharnoth together with the Supreme Party, but if he did that, Sharnoth’s Domain would have faltered, and the trapped Supremes would have moved away, ruining everything.

He could also try to devour Sharnoth again, but honestly, the only reason it worked before was because Eternity—or Zarveth—was taken aback by the fact that he was an Anomaly and was curious as to what he could do.
But now that he had already seen this move,
There was no way he would let Nux do whatever he wanted.

Even if he was arrogant, he knew better than to let someone like an Anomaly run wild. The chances of this working were low, and if it didn’t, both he and Sharnoth would be captured alive—something that cannot happen, since it might even endanger his wives.
The only other way was to...
‘Escape.’
Sharnoth spoke, her eyes shining with determination as she glared at the two Eternals, who had now teamed up with each other.
‘Shar—’
Nux tried to say something, but—
‘Escape!’
Sharnoth raised her voice, and Nux clenched his fists in frustration.
He glared at his enemies, especially at Darkness—the being who ruined it all. His anger boiled even further as he saw the dark mist moving around that bastard’s body, but then—
Nux’s expression changed as he realized something, his eyes still staring at the ‘being of Darkness’ standing in front of him.
‘Shar—’
‘I said esca—’
‘Listen to me!’
Nux countered back, raising his voice even more.
Sharnoth momentarily froze, and Nux...
‘How long do you think you can last if you just face Eternity alone?’
‘Alone...?’
‘I will take care of Darkness.’
‘Nux, don’t be foo—’
‘Answer my question.’
Nux spoke sternly, and Sharnoth...
She stared at Eternity in silence before turning towards Nux and—
‘If you face Darkness alone...
I will defeat him as soon as I can and come aid you.’
She declared, her eyes burning with intensity, preparing to kill that bastard no matter what it took.
And when Nux saw those eyes, his grin widened.
‘Remember those words.
Don’t you dare lose,
Because if you do,
I will revive you once all this is over and haunt you for the rest of your life.’
Saying those words, Nux opened his Universe’s gate through his shadow, instantly attracting the Supremes’ attention.
Zarveth, the Eternity, shouted as Nux was devoured by his own Shadows. Neremoth, on the other hand, moved before anyone could react, and using the Power of Darkness,
He barged into Nux’s shadow—
Entering his Universe.
