At his question, Neremoth grinned.
“Why?
Does my presence bother you, Zarveth?”
Neremoth questioned, his Grimson eyes shining even more brightly.
It was clear that his excitement couldn’t be contained.
“This is not what we agreed on.”
Zarveth, the Eternal of the Supreme World of Eternity, spoke in a strict, dissatisfied tone.
As the two Supremes conversed, they completely ignored Nux and Sharnoth, as if their presence simply did not matter.
And it did not.
The Space Laws no longer worked here—it was impossible for them to escape.
Even if they did try something, with the two of them together, the weaklings did not stand a chance.
Actually, the two Supremes were certain that even without the help of the other, they could take down the opponents.
After all, Anomaly or not, with all said and done, a Primordial was still just that—a Primordial.
As for the woman, well, the Supreme Borns never considered those at a similar cultivation stage as them on the same level.
There was no way the enemy Eternal was nearly as strong as taking them.
Honestly, instead of the two opponents in front of them, the biggest concern the two Supremes had was... each other.
And this feeling was mutual; both of them wanted the other to be gone so they could get their hands on the Anomaly.
“Do you truly believe you are in the position to talk about what we agreed on or not?”
At Zarveth’s words, Neremoth questioned with a demonic grin.
“You encountered the Anomaly, and instead of following the Infinities’ direction and informing them about his existence,
You sealed the Space instead, making sure no one gets here.”
“I did it because I did not want the enemy to call reinforcements or escape.”
Zarveth tried to explain, but Neremoth was no fool.
And he did not like to be treated as one either.
“Stop this.”
He spoke, his tone stricter than before.
“We both know what you want.”
At those words, Zarveth’s tone changed as well.
Further games were pointless, so he decided to skip them.
“You knew, yet you still did not report to the Infinities.”
He blamed.
Well, it wasn’t a ‘blame’ per se, it was simply a signal—an offer to stop this pointless squabble here.
After all, just like Neremoth, Zarveth knew what the other wanted as well.
The Anomaly.
As for going against the Infinities, the very fact that Neremoth was here instead of reporting him meant that he was prepared to go against them as well.
Just like him, Neremoth wanted the Anomaly for himself.
So instead of going at each other and letting the fish escape,
Why not work together?
That was Zarveth’s underlying offer.
And understanding every part of it, Neremoth’s eyes shined even more joyfully,
“Yes, I change my statement.
We both know what we want.”
He agreed.
Zarveth stared at Neremoth in silence, and in the end, he passed a light smile as well.
There was no other option—this was indeed the best-case scenario considering the current situation.
As for how they were going to ‘divide’ the Anomaly, well, that can be discussed later.
Of course, Zarveth also did not overlook the chances of Neremoth betraying and attacking him after everything was done.
After all, he was considering the same thing.
However, they both knew the other would not do that.
The reason was simple—if the two fought each other, the victor wouldn’t be clear.
Even if the battle continued for years and one might get a slight advantage over the other, killing each other for good was impossible.
In the end, the one who got the Anomaly would later be at a disadvantage because the other would inform the Infinities about what happened, and after that,
It was only a matter of time before the Anomaly was taken away from them without them getting anything in return.
So unless they had a certain way to kill the other in one shot, fighting each other was no different than sealing their fate for the worse.
Both of them knew this, so they knew that as long as they did not let their guard down, the other would not betray them.
And with that clear,
The two Supreme Borns decided to go against the feared Infinities and act independently—together.
Of course, while the two were having a conversation, the so-called opponents they ignored weren’t just staying still either.
They were making their own plans.
Before this began, Nux used a Slave Seal on Sharnoth.
Of course, at Sharnoth’s level, she could break the seal on her own without having to do anything, so it wasn’t exactly a big deal.
It was just one of Nux’s trusted methods, using which they could converse whenever needed.
‘Nux, what do we do?’
Sharnoth questioned with a solemn look on her face.
She was still considering going against one Eternal, but two... even she knew it was no longer a battle they could win.
‘Can we escape?’
She asked, and Nux...
‘We can’t.’
He shook his head grimly.
‘Space Laws cannot be used here.’
From their expressions, he could tell that the two Eternals weren’t exactly allies—their greed might lead to them fighting each other.
Honestly, with how things were, that would be the best-case scenario.
In the chaos, Nux believed he could figure something out.
If anything, he would be able to assimilate the Laws he had just gathered and integrate them into his Universe.
But of course, this was only the best-case scenario—a scenario where he got incredibly lucky.
And... considering his recent past with Lady Luck...
She wasn’t on his side.
Nux could tell there was a high probability that they would need to face the two of them together, and no matter how he thought about it,
He could not see a way to win.
This...
This might just be it.
‘Nux.’
Suddenly, Sharnoth called out with a determined look on her face.
Nux glanced at her and noticed her crimson eyes shining much more fiercely than ever.
‘You can escape, can’t you?’
She questioned.
Nux turned silent.
‘Answer me.
You can escape alive, can you not?’
She questioned, her tone much fiercer than before.
‘Yes.’
Nux nodded.
His Universe’s gate did not depend on Space—he could easily escape without the two Eternals being able to do anything.
But...
If he did that, Sharnoth would be facing the two angered Eternals alone, and... there was no way they would let her have an easy death.

Honestly, Nux had thought of devouring Sharnoth together with the Supreme Party, but if he did that, Sharnoth’s Domain would have faltered, and the trapped Supremes would have moved away, ruining everything.

He could also try to devour Sharnoth again, but honestly, the only reason it worked before was because Eternity—or Zarveth—was taken aback by the fact that he was an Anomaly and was curious as to what he could do.
But now that he had already seen this move,
There was no way he would let Nux do whatever he wanted.
Even if he was arrogant, he knew better than to let someone like an Anomaly run wild.
The chances of this working were low, and if it didn’t, both he and Sharnoth would be captured alive—something that cannot happen, since it might even endanger his wives.
The only other way was to...
‘Escape.’
Sharnoth spoke, her eyes shining with determination as she glared at the two Eternals, who had now teamed up with each other.
‘Shar—’
Nux tried to say something, but—
‘Escape!’
Sharnoth raised her voice, and Nux clenched his fists in frustration.
He glared at his enemies, especially at Darkness—the being who ruined it all.
His anger boiled even further as he saw the dark mist moving around that bastard’s body, but then—
Nux’s expression changed as he realized something, his eyes still staring at the ‘being of Darkness’ standing in front of him.
‘Shar—’
‘I said esca—’
‘Listen to me!’
Nux countered back, raising his voice even more.
Sharnoth momentarily froze, and Nux...
‘How long do you think you can last if you just face Eternity alone?’
‘Alone...?’
‘I will take care of Darkness.’
‘Nux, don’t be foo—’
‘Answer my question.’
Nux spoke sternly, and Sharnoth...
She stared at Eternity in silence before turning towards Nux and—
‘If you face Darkness alone...
I will defeat him as soon as I can and come aid you.’
She declared, her eyes burning with intensity, preparing to kill that bastard no matter what it took.
And when Nux saw those eyes, his grin widened.
‘Remember those words.
Don’t you dare lose,
Because if you do,
I will revive you once all this is over and haunt you for the rest of your life.’
Saying those words, Nux opened his Universe’s gate through his shadow, instantly attracting the Supremes’ attention.
Zarveth, the Eternity, shouted as Nux was devoured by his own Shadows.
Neremoth, on the other hand, moved before anyone could react, and using the Power of Darkness,
He barged into Nux’s shadow—
Entering his Universe.

chapters.title: Chapter 2095: Do not think your end will be dignified.
paragraphs: The moment Nux opened his Universe’s Gate through his shadow, Zarveth, the Eternity, extended his hand forward, trying to stop him, while his eyes were wide in disbelief.
This was the first time he reacted this way since he appeared—his composed face, one that made it seem like everything was under his absolute control, could no longer be seen.

It was a reaction that surprised even Neremoth, who had known Zarveth for millions of years and had never seen him react in such a manner. Neremoth, however, did not let this surprise get to him. Rather, he had a big grin on his face when he glanced at Nux’s shadow.

Neremoth was a millions-of-years-old veteran; a single gaze was all it took for him to understand that this was his moment. He could sense that whatever ability the Anomaly had used, wherever he was going, he could follow him—and Zarveth could not.
He could have the Anomaly all to himself.
And before Zarveth could stop him, Neremoth moved, dashing toward Nux’s lingering shadow.
Zarveth tried to stop him; however, with the head start Neremoth had, it was impossible for him to catch up, especially when Zarveth was faster than him only if no Relics were being used.
In Zarveth’s despair, both Neremoth and the Anomaly disappeared. The only one he could now see in front of him was the woman with Power over Chaos.
And in that instant...
Zarveth’s despair, his shock, his sense of loss... it all turned into anger.
For the first time in a long, long while, a Supreme Born—an Eternal Level Supreme Born—was angry.
And the one facing all this anger was...
Sharnoth.
“...Where are they?”
Zarveth questioned. His voice was low, but Sharnoth could feel his intense anger in those words.
And she...
“What makes you think I will tell you?”
She grinned demonically, her crimson eyes shining in disdain. It almost looked like she was the villain here.
After all, this was the same woman who had led a World of the Faction of Darkness. The number of beings she had killed probably surpassed most of the people in the Universe.
By no means was she merely a side character who would sacrifice herself just to be forgotten later.

She was planning to crush this arrogant being in front of her. Not just him, she was planning to crush his overly inflated ego. She wanted to change the look on his face. She wanted to make him know—Supreme Born or not—in front of her, he could only cower on his knees.
That was what it meant to be Sharnoth Nocthys, the Princess who rose from Chains.
Hearing her words, Zarveth’s face twitched.
“You do not cherish your life, do you?”
He questioned, his hollow eyes staring directly at her, radiating anger he had never felt before.
“Those are some bold words for someone so small.”
Sharnoth grinned again.
“Small...?”
“Is that not what you are? You used all these fancy tricks you have, yet you still failed to capture a mere Primordial.
What makes you think you can actually do something against me?
You must be an entertainer in the society of Supremes.”
“Entertainer...?”

Eternity’s face twitched even further. Nobody had ever talked to him like this in the billions of years he had been alive. Sharnoth’s mere existence was making him feel emotions he didn’t even know he was capable of feeling.

However, this did not mean he let his anger get the better of him. He was better than that. He knew such strong emotions would only cloud his decision. It was much better to direct this anger into getting what he wanted.
And what he wanted was to get to the Anomaly.

Zarveth clenched his staff. From this conversation, he could tell that this woman might know where the Anomaly was. There was still hope—as long as he captured her alive, extracting this information would not be impossible.
“Do not think your end will be dignified.”
He warned. In his mind, he was already preparing his worst. He would make it so the woman wouldn’t even be left in a state where she could beg for death.
He would rip apart whatever dignity and arrogance she had. He would... turn her very soul into something miserable.
For a moment, Sharnoth’s expression faltered—she could feel just how absurdly strong her enemy truly was—but seeing his reaction, she knew her plan had succeeded.
She knew whatever Nux was doing needed time. She had seen how he was trying to buy time the entire time.
The last thing they wanted was for Zarveth to report everything that happened here to the Infinities.
Because Zarveth wanted the Anomaly all to himself, he had made it so that nothing that happened here was leaked outside.

He even killed his own subordinates to ensure that and sealed the space so no external eyes could observe them. Because of all that, it still wasn’t known that the Chain Breakers were related to the Anomaly, and it was something Sharnoth felt could be used in the future.
Now all she needed to do was to keep Zarveth’s focus on her.
She wanted to give him a ‘hope’.
Hope that she knew where the Anomaly was, and if he managed to capture her, he could still get his hands on the Anomaly through her.
As for whether it was true or not...
Well, even though she knew Nux went to his ‘Universe’, she had absolutely no clue where it was or how to get there.
So even if she does get captured, Zarveth would get absolutely nothing out of it.
The ‘hope’ she gave him was an empty one from the very beginning.
And now what Sharnoth needed to do right now was to keep this hope alive for as long as possible and buy Nux the time he needs.
As for her?
Well, she was obviously planning on coming out alive.
She was going to crush this bastard through and through.
“See, this is the difference between us.
I do not care about your End.
I would simply end you in an instant because that is all you mean to me—
Nothing.”
Sharnoth shrugged with a disdainful laugh, and in that instant, Zarveth made a move.
The ‘Battle’ had begun.
BOOOOOOOM

While Sharnoth and Zarveth were up against each other in the Main Universe, back in Nux’s Universe, the instant Nux appeared, his connection with his wives—which he had closed off just to be sure that they did not get involved with this in any way—was restored.
“NUX!!”
They shouted in unison as they tried to rush toward him.
Nux, however, waved his hand and teleported them to a different place—and no, he did not use the Law of Space to do it. In here, he used his Will.
“Stay there.”
He spoke, and just as he willed it, his voice was only heard by his wives, who were now inside a hidden world that could only be seen by Nux.
“Nux, what happened?”
Shadow questioned, using the same authority as Nux to talk to him.
“Enemy is coming.”
Nux warned, and Shadow...
“In here...?”
She just blinked.
“What was the poor soul thinking?”
She questioned in a pitiful tone.
It wasn’t just her—the rest of the women, especially Skyla and Evane, started pitying the enemy as well.
Entering Nux’s Universe to fight him was a one-way ticket to absolute humiliation. It would simply trigger Nux’s sadistic tendencies—he would play with the enemy until the poor soul lost his mind.
However...
‘Nux, what happened...?’
Allura questioned, narrowing her eyes when she noticed his tone.
Nux had currently restricted them from sensing his emotions, and while he usually did that to keep a surprise factor and the spark in their relationship alive, this felt different.
His tone was too serious.
‘Where is Sharnoth?’
Allura questioned, and once again, Nux stayed silent. And his silence was all the answer the women needed.
Their expressions changed—they could tell that Nux was in no mood to ‘play around’ right now.
Sharnoth was still outside.
What’s worse?
Because there was no one outside to act as their eyes, they could not tell what was happening there, and this only made them worry even more.
Right now, all his focus was on assimilating the Laws he had just devoured. Yes, he had already started comprehending them and was already done with a few, but then—
He appeared.
Darkness was here.
“Huh...? Where are we...?”
He questioned with a frown on his face.
He looked around, confused. The place looked like a corner of a Universe; the surroundings resembled the Outer Space, but there were no asteroids.
Not just that, he also noticed a few other strange things—
A strange-looking colorful river flowing in the air,
A tree that seemed to be holding a large world,
A lotus hovering above it.
Hundreds of different-sized Stars all over the place.
Just...
Just what is this place...?

chapters.title: Chapter 2096: I WILL KILL YOU!!!
paragraphs: "Huh...? Where are we...?"
Neremoth questioned as he looked around with a confused look on his face.
This space seemed... strange.
Even though it did resemble the Outer Space, something felt different.
It was... dark.

And for the first time in his long life, he found this ’darkness’ creepy. Other than the strange objects, everything here—even the Worlds—were dark. It was almost as if Light did not exist in this place.
What’s worse?
He could no longer sense his connection to the Universe.
It was a discomforting feeling, and what strengthened this feeling even further was the fact that the Space Artifact that should have teleported him to his desired coordinate was not working.
According to it, the desired coordinate he set up... no longer existed.
It felt like the Artifact was brought out of its usage scope, and it wasn’t a good feeling.
Something was wrong.
Neremoth could feel it.
The signs were bad—he... he might have fallen into a trap.
His mind raced, trying to think of ways to get out of this situation, and then, his eyes fell on him.
The Anomaly.
Hovering in the air with his eyes closed, acting like he couldn’t even see him. Neremoth, of course, did not like that attitude.
"I asked a question."
He spoke, his crimson eyes narrowed.
"Where are we?"
He repeated.
And this time, Nux, who was still busy comprehending the Laws he devoured, opened his eyes, staring at Neremoth with an expressionless look on his face.
He squeezed out a few full seconds of attention from this situation—it was enough for him to comprehend a few Laws, but he could no longer ignore Neremoth any further.
No matter what, Neremoth was still an Eternal—one of the strongest Eternals at that. Even if he had absolute advantage here, he still needed to move.
And that is what Nux did.
He willed himself to appear right in front of Neremoth, and before the being of Darkness could even understand what had happened—
BOOOOOOM
Nux punched, and in an instant, the weight of hundreds of worlds fell on Neremoth’s body, and for the first time in a long while—
He felt it.
Fear.
His crimson eyes shined in surprise and horror. He tried to move away the instant his mind processed the strength behind that punch but...
It was already too late.
The punch landed, hitting his chest—the only ’materialistic’ part of his body and the only part that could truly be crushed by a physical attack. In other words, his weakness.
Yes, Nux already knew about it.
He had done his research. In the limited time he had, the Laws he chose to comprehend and the memories he chose to see belonged to the three True Borns of the Supreme World of Darkness.

In that limited time, he understood everything he could understand about the True Borns of the Supreme World of Darkness: how their body worked, the usual abilities they had, their Laws, their Bloodline powers, and their weaknesses.

In an instant, Neremoth’s body exploded into black mist, only his widened crimson eyes remained in their place. Nux could see how they were losing their shine, almost as if his life force was slipping out.

Soon, the crimson eyes lost all their shine, turning into the black mist similar to the rest of his body, and all this Mist gathered behind Nux, where a new pair of crimson eyes had already reappeared.
"W-What was that!? What did you do!?"
Neremoth, whose body was reconstructed back to how it originally was, questioned, still horrified by the punch that tore through his defenses as if they were made of paper.
"How can a mere Primordial exert this much stre—"
He tried questioning but—
BOOOOOOM
Nux punched, destroying his body yet again.
But once again, it did not make a difference.
Neremoth’s body reformed, and once again—
"How are you moving like that!? I do not sense the Space around me being affec—"
He tried asking but—
BOOOOOOM
Nux punched again.
And this did not stop.
"Why can’t I stop yo—"
BOOOOOOM
"Answer my questi—!"
BOOOOOOM
"You Bastar—"
BOOOOOOM
"Where is this place!? Who are yo—"
BOOOOOOM
"I will kill you in the most painful way I can!!!—"
Nux continued to unleash a series of deadly punches, forcing Neremoth to reconstruct his body again and again, while ignoring all his words like they did not matter.
And they truly did not.
The only thing Nux cared about right now was to get rid of him, absorb all the Laws, assimilate them in his Universe, and help Sharnoth.
Nothing else mattered right now.
Nux knew what was happening and how Neremoth was reconstructing his body again and again.
It was the Hollow Rebirth.

One of the Darkness Borns’ abilities that came with their blood—an ability that activates when they are struck fatally. It turns their body into black mist only to reform behind the attacker, and while it does chip away 10 years of life force with every use...
To an Immortal Eternal, who had endless life force, it was an ability that could be used all the time without any aftereffects whatsoever.
What’s more surprising?
This wasn’t even the Darkness Borns’ strongest ability. Their blood inherited countless similarly powerful abilities.
Unfeel—the ability to suppress all sensory inputs directed at them, essentially making it so they do not get attacked by spells and can hide their presence.
Worldless Shell—the ability to form a shield that protects them from all attacks that carry emotions.
Movement ability like Darkstep, allowing them to move through darkness at a speed that breaks the limit set by the very Universe.
Black Ripple that makes the reality distort with every step they take.

Nullfang, a Claw of Darkness that ignores all defense, shields, and magical barriers—an attack that doesn’t cut flesh, it cuts meaning. Once struck, the concept of "defense" in that area vanishes temporarily, making the victim vulnerable to anything.
And the list went on.
These monsters had other similar absurd abilities that made absolutely no sense.
Every single Darkness Born had them, and the abilities only got stronger as they grew.
Just with these alone, they held the power to destroy anyone from a non-supreme world. They didn’t even have to use their Laws in battle.
After all, just how was one supposed to destroy a being who could reconstruct his body after it was destroyed endlessly?
This was the difference between the Supreme Borns and normal beings in the rest of the Universe.
Normal enemies simply did not stand a chance. This was the reason the True Borns reigned supreme despite there only being a few thousands of them.
Not that any of it mattered right now.
After all, Nux was no ’normal’ being.

His plan was simple—he was going to punch this bastard and force him to reconstruct his body again and again and again. He was going to do it so many times that reconstructing his body became the only thing he could think about, stopping him from using the rest of his absurdly annoying abilities.
And him...
Well, he could then focus on absorbing the rest of the Laws and Memories he had left.
Yes, unlike back in the Main Universe, where the Eternals were still a threat to him, in here, they were merely an inconvenience.
If he moved correctly, he could redirect his focus to more important things.
And what’s worse?
Neremoth could tell what Nux was thinking and doing—he could tell the bastard wasn’t even taking him seriously, he was being ignored mid-battle.
He was being treated like a child being played with one hand as the adult read the newspaper with the other.
Humiliation.
Absolute humiliation.
That was what Neremoth felt during this ’battle’.
"I WILL KILL YOU!!!"
He screamed, his anger taking over every other emotion in his mind.
The fear of the overwhelmingly powerful punch, all the questions in his head, the feeling of getting the Anomaly for himself—it had all disappeared.
He now cared about one and one thing alone.
It was killing this bastard as painfully as possible. And while Nux was still ’busy’ comprehending the Laws—
BOOOOOOM
Neremoth attacked, activating his Domain.
In an instant, the air around him froze—a thick pressure spread in all directions.
Then—everything went dark.
Even Nux’s Universe, which was already devoid of light, now became even darker. If at first it looked like a night under a starry sky, now...
It was pure, pitch-black darkness.
It wasn’t a lack of light.
It was as if the very meaning of Light had ceased to exist.
There was... just darkness.
And then—his eyes opened.
Two glowing crimson slits cut through the void.
They didn’t shine, they didn’t light up the darkness.
They simply... came into existence.
This was Neremoth’s Domain, a Domain created from the Law of Absolute Eclipse. Even Nux, who was now trapped inside this domain, was now blinded and had stopped moving.
He had absolutely no idea where his enemy was.
And then—
"I deprive you of your Movement.
I deprive you of your Will to Resist.
I deprive you of your Physical Power.
I deprive you of your Law."
Neremoth commanded, taking every single thing away from Nux.

This space seemed... strange.
Even though it did resemble the Outer Space, something felt different.
It was... dark.

Other than the strange objects, everything here—even the Worlds—were dark.
It was almost as if Light did not exist in this place.
What’s worse?

Something was wrong.

The signs were bad—he... he might have fallen into a trap.

The Anomaly.
Hovering in the air with his eyes closed, acting like he couldn’t even see him.
Neremoth, of course, did not like that attitude.
"I asked a question."
He spoke, his crimson eyes narrowed.
"Where are we?"
He repeated.

He squeezed out a few full seconds of attention from this situation—it was enough for him to comprehend a few Laws, but he could no longer ignore Neremoth any further.
No matter what, Neremoth was still an Eternal—one of the strongest Eternals at that.
Even if he had absolute advantage here, he still needed to move.
And that is what Nux did.
He willed himself to appear right in front of Neremoth, and before the being of Darkness could even understand what had happened—
BOOOOOOM
Nux punched, and in an instant, the weight of hundreds of worlds fell on Neremoth’s body, and for the first time in a long while—
He felt it.
Fear.
His crimson eyes shined in surprise and horror.
He tried to move away the instant his mind processed the strength behind that punch but...
It was already too late.
The punch landed, hitting his chest—the only ’materialistic’ part of his body and the only part that could truly be crushed by a physical attack.

Nux could see how they were losing their shine, almost as if his life force was slipping out.

Neremoth, whose body was reconstructed back to how it originally was, questioned, still horrified by the punch that tore through his defenses as if they were made of paper.

BOOOOOOM
Nux punched, destroying his body yet again.

Neremoth’s body reformed, and once again—
"How are you moving like that!?
I do not sense the Space around me being affec—"
He tried asking but—
BOOOOOOM
Nux punched again.
And this did not stop.
"Why can’t I stop yo—"
BOOOOOOM
"Answer my questi—!"
BOOOOOOM
"You Bastar—"
BOOOOOOM
"Where is this place!?
Who are yo—"
BOOOOOOM

chapters.title: Chapter 2097: How did you do it?
paragraphs: “I deprive you of your Movement.
I deprive you of your Will to Resist.
I deprive you of your Physical Power.
I deprive you of your Law.”

In the region where he was the Absolute, in the region where everything was covered in Absolute Darkness, in the region where only his Crimson Eyes remained visible, Neremoth commanded, taking every single thing away from Nux.
Nux froze. Since his movements and strength were gone, he couldn’t exactly do anything but stare at Neremoth’s Crimson eyes helplessly.
Neremoth, using Darkstep, travelled through darkness and appeared right in front of Nux. Of course, in his current state, Nux couldn’t even see him. He only saw his crimson eyes coming closer.
The scene was quite haunting.
“Hmm? I do not remember taking away your voice.”
He began in a disdainful voice.
“What happened? Why the sudden silence? Where did all that bravado from before go?”
He questioned, his grin widening as Nux didn’t dare to utter a word. The situation was too disadvantageous for him, and he did not wish to anger Neremoth any further with his words.
Suddenly, Nux took a deep breath as he sensed a cold, rough hand grabbing his throat, forcing him to lift his head and stare at the crimson eyes that were staring directly into his eyes.
“Is this your limit?”
Neremoth questioned.
“You were acting so arrogantly before, almost as if you had complete control over the situation, but...
Is this it?
Was using my Domain all it took to stop you?
Just... what were you thinking...?”
His tone sounded like that of a disappointed father.
“I was expecting a stronger resistance, you know?
You went so far with your mockery, I thought you were quite confident in yourself.
Was it all an act? Were you trying to hide your weakness by putting up a brave front?
Were you... not ignoring me but desperately trying to kill me instead?”

He guessed, and when he thought about it, he couldn’t help but feel just how ‘cute’ this attempt was. He truly gave it his all. Actually, it was quite impressive, especially when one thought about how a mere Primordial was able to pull it off.
That punch of his carried an absurd amount of strength. Honestly, Neremoth had never once experienced something like this before.
He was sure that that punch had the power to take out a Transcendent—no, not just a Transcendent—even an Eternal, other than the ones from the Supreme World, wouldn’t be able to survive that punch.
It was simply that strong. If it weren’t for Hollow Rebirth, even he would have perished.
No wonder he was so confident at the beginning.

Neremoth could see how it all played out. From the very beginning, the child knew his physical strength was far stronger than anything in the Universe. He knew he had the capability to kill even Eternals with his strength.
The problem was their Domain.

After all, the Universe’s Rules were Absolute, the difference between Phases was Absolute. Even if he was this absurdly strong, in the end, the Phase difference between him and an Eternal was simply too absurdly big.
Therefore, he came up with a way around it.
He tried to surprise his enemy with his strength and take them out in one blow.
With his strength, one good blow was all he needed, and he had the speed and agility to pull it off.
Neremoth could see how this would work against any normal Eternal—heck, it even worked against him. The punch strong enough to obliterate his body did get connected.
Just that...
The child failed to calculate that obliteration was not the end.
He did not know about the Hollow Rebirth. How could he?
The Trueborns never appeared in the Universe. Every time they did, it was a one-sided destruction.
No one in the Universe actually knew about the extent of Trueborns’ abilities. They just knew that the Trueborns of Supreme Worlds were strong—much stronger than one could comprehend.
And this lack of information bit this child.
After the first punch connected, he believed the battle would end, but Neremoth’s body was reconstructed.
‘That must have made him panic.’
Neremoth realized it, glancing at Nux, who still kept a poker face despite everything happening right now.
‘His control over his emotions is exceptional. It is almost as if his body is incapable of processing emotions.’
He muttered in his head, recalling how desperately the child punched him again and again, only for his body to be reconstructed as if nothing had happened...
If before, he felt humiliation at how the enemy was ignoring his words and kept attacking him, now, when he felt how desperate of a situation this poor child was in...
Neremoth felt... pity.
At the same time, he had no choice but to admit it.
The child was exceptional—far more exceptional than anyone he had ever met.
Even in despair, he continued hitting without stop until he no longer could. He continued to do whatever he could to try and defeat an enemy he could not.
The child was brave. Exceptionally brave.
‘An Anomaly, huh...’
Neremoth muttered in his head. It was the first time in his life that he appreciated another being’s exception.
And of course, at the same time, he also wanted to see it.
He wanted to see this brave child break.
He wanted to see him cower in fear and flinch in agony.
He wanted to see him beg for mercy.
The moment he thought of that, Neremoth’s grin widened. He had to use all his willpower to not act right now.
After all, the child still had his use.
“How did you do it?”
Neremoth questioned.
Now that the Anomaly was finally his, it was time to extract the useful information and use it for his sake.
It was time to ‘take’ this power from the hands of a Primordial and use it in a way that actually made a difference.
It was time... to plunge the Entire Universe into Absolute Eclipse.
At least that was the plan but...
The child did not say anything. Even now, he kept staring back at Neremoth with the same, expressionless look on his face, almost as if instead of his movements, Neremoth froze him in place instead.

chapters.title: Chapter 2098: Ah, shit.
paragraphs: "How did you do it?"
Neremoth questioned but...

The child did not say anything. Even now, he kept staring back at Neremoth with the same expressionless look on his face, almost as if instead of his movements, Neremoth froze him in one place instead.
Of course, Neremoth expected it.
The child had continued fighting all this while. It made no sense he would simply answer his question just because he asked.
Actually, Neremoth wanted this to happen.
After all, now he officially had a new goal in their little game.
He would make him speak.
He would break his will, he would break his bravery, he would break his very existence, and in the end, when he was merely a shell of his previous self,
He would make the child talk and answer all the questions on his own.

Of course, there were far more efficient ways to do it. The child was trapped in Neremoth’s Domain. He could simply ’order’ him to answer all his questions and he would have no other choice but to do it. He could even use Artifacts to directly read his mind, making sure nothing was left out.
There were hundreds of different ways but...
Neremoth chose the most fun one.
From his Claw—that was holding Nux’s neck—tendrils of Darkness formed and crawled their way towards Nux’s mouth and nose.
Through these two orifices, these tendrils made their way into Nux’s brain, making his entire body twitch.
Then, Neremoth began.
He was the being of darkness, a being who thrived on negative emotions. Because of that, he had a certain level of authority on one’s emotions and senses.
Slowly, Neremoth began altering Nux’s senses—
He raised his pain perception, making it so that even a slight poke would feel like being pierced through by a spear.
He slowed down his time perception so that the pain he felt stayed for a much longer duration than normal.
Then, he amplified his fear of pain.

A Cycle. A torturous, endless cycle where he planned to continue making Nux wither in agony, raise the pain he was feeling, elongate the time he was feeling the pain for, and... later inject the fear of future pain into his mind.
What’s worse?
This fear would continue to rise as he was subjected to more and more pain.
And it did not end here. Neremoth even strengthened Nux’s Willpower, wanting him to resist and fear the agony a bit longer before breaking.
This was his masterpiece—a plan to thoroughly enjoy this.
And after he made the preparation in front of the immobile enemy, he grabbed the tip of his nail and—
Rip
He ripped it apart.
"AAAAAGGGGGGGGHHHHHHH!!!"
And for the first time in a long, long while, Nux screamed in agony. His horrifying screams made Neremoth’s grin wider than ever.
"Are you going to answer my questions now?"
Neremoth questioned with a playful look on his face.
And before Nux could answer,
Crack
The finger was broken.
"AAAAAGGGGGHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
Nux screamed again, with Neremoth enjoying every moment of his soul-shrieking screams.
And only when Nux stopped screaming and the pain started fading...
Rip
He repeated it again.
"AAAAAAGGGGGGGHHHHHHHH!!!"

The torture continued for a long time. Neremoth continued to rip his nails out using different manners. He broke his fingers, crushed his hands, tore his limbs apart. He even crushed his eyes, peeled his skin.
He did every possible thing he could, playing with Nux to his heart’s content—so much that a drop of tear fell out of Nux’s crushed right eye.
And when Neremoth saw that...
"Recover."
He ordered, and suddenly, Nux’s body returned to how it was before, making him widen his eyes in horror.
"W-Wha..."
He spoke. His emotionless expression was long gone. Now, only the fear of pain remained.
Neremoth laughed when he saw that—
"You didn’t think this was it, did you?"
He questioned, his grin becoming more and more demonic as the sadistic pleasure of breaking him was simply too relishing.
He had long stopped asking questions. That wasn’t necessary right now.
He had other plans.
"Let me show you something interesting."
He spoke as he suddenly took out an Artifact—a dark, beetle-shaped thing that was barely the size of a thumb.

"It was something my subordinate gave in order to impress me. He said that this little thing is supposed to enter one’s body and contaminate their very blood, making one feel unbearable pain as the contaminated blood moves throughout their body.
According to him, this is far more painful than just breaking limbs.
What did he say again...?
Ah, right.
He said the pain is comparable to tearing one’s soul piece by piece. Quite interesting, isn’t it?"
Neremoth grinned, and Nux’s eyes widened in even more horror.
He stuttered.
"P-Please stop this...
I-I will t-tell you e-everything!!"
He begged.
Of course, Neremoth did not listen. He slowly brought the beetle close to Nux, and in his fear, Nux moved back.
"N-NO! I-I will tell you everything! Please!! Spare me!!! I BEG YOU!!!"

He screamed, his entire body trembling in endless, primordial fear that seemed like it was now etched into his very soul. His golden eyes stared at the thumb-sized beetle as if it was the scariest thing in the world. Even the thought of it getting close to him shook him to his very core.
Yes, Neremoth had succeeded.
He had broken the Anomaly.
Or at least...
That was what the Anomaly wanted him to believe.
But...
Suddenly, Neremoth noticed something.
"...I deprived you of your movement.
How did you move...?"
He questioned in a doubtful voice, his eyes narrowing ever so slightly.
Nux froze.
Neremoth’s questions, however, did not end here.
"You shouldn’t be able to see anything but my eyes in my Domain...
How are you staring right at the beetle?
How do you know where it is...?"
He asked another question and—
"Ah, shit."
Nux cursed out loud, his trembling body returning to normal as if everything before was just an act.

After all, now he officially had a new goal in their little game.
He would make him speak.
He would break his will, he would break his bravery, he would break his very existence, and in the end, when he was merely a shell of his previous self,
He would make the child talk and answer all the questions on his own.
Of course, there were far more efficient ways to do it.
The child was trapped in Neremoth’s Domain.
He could simply ’order’ him to answer all his questions and he would have no other choice but to do it.
He could even use Artifacts to directly read his mind, making sure nothing was left out.
There were hundreds of different ways but...
Neremoth chose the most fun one.
From his Claw—that was holding Nux’s neck—tendrils of Darkness formed and crawled their way towards Nux’s mouth and nose.
Through these two orifices, these tendrils made their way into Nux’s brain, making his entire body twitch.
Then, Neremoth began.
He was the being of darkness, a being who thrived on negative emotions.
Because of that, he had a certain level of authority on one’s emotions and senses.
Slowly, Neremoth began altering Nux’s senses—
He raised his pain perception, making it so that even a slight poke would feel like being pierced through by a spear.
He slowed down his time perception so that the pain he felt stayed for a much longer duration than normal.
Then, he amplified his fear of pain.
A Cycle.

A torturous, endless cycle where he planned to continue making Nux wither in agony, raise the pain he was feeling, elongate the time he was feeling the pain for, and... later inject the fear of future pain into his mind.
What’s worse?
This fear would continue to rise as he was subjected to more and more pain.
And it did not end here.
Neremoth even strengthened Nux’s Willpower, wanting him to resist and fear the agony a bit longer before breaking.
This was his masterpiece—a plan to thoroughly enjoy this.
And after he made the preparation in front of the immobile enemy, he grabbed the tip of his nail and—
Rip
He ripped it apart.
"AAAAAGGGGGGGGHHHHHHH!!!"
And for the first time in a long, long while, Nux screamed in agony.
His horrifying screams made Neremoth’s grin wider than ever.
"Are you going to answer my questions now?"
Neremoth questioned with a playful look on his face.
And before Nux could answer,
Crack
The finger was broken.
"AAAAAGGGGGHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
Nux screamed again, with Neremoth enjoying every moment of his soul-shrieking screams.
And only when Nux stopped screaming and the pain started fading...
Rip
He repeated it again.
"AAAAAAGGGGGGGHHHHHHHH!!!"
The torture continued for a long time.
Neremoth continued to rip his nails out using different manners.
He broke his fingers, crushed his hands, tore his limbs apart.
He even crushed his eyes, peeled his skin.
He did every possible thing he could, playing with Nux to his heart’s content—so much that a drop of tear fell out of Nux’s crushed right eye.
And when Neremoth saw that...
"Recover."
He ordered, and suddenly, Nux’s body returned to how it was before, making him widen his eyes in horror.
"W-Wha..."
He spoke.
His emotionless expression was long gone.
Now, only the fear of pain remained.
Neremoth laughed when he saw that—
"You didn’t think this was it, did you?"
He questioned, his grin becoming more and more demonic as the sadistic pleasure of breaking him was simply too relishing.
He had long stopped asking questions.
That wasn’t necessary right now.
He had other plans.
"Let me show you something interesting."
He spoke as he suddenly took out an Artifact—a dark, beetle-shaped thing that was barely the size of a thumb.
"It was something my subordinate gave in order to impress me.
He said that this little thing is supposed to enter one’s body and contaminate their very blood, making one feel unbearable pain as the contaminated blood moves throughout their body.
According to him, this is far more painful than just breaking limbs.
What did he say again...?
Ah, right.
He said the pain is comparable to tearing one’s soul piece by piece.
Quite interesting, isn’t it?"
Neremoth grinned, and Nux’s eyes widened in even more horror.
He stuttered.
"P-Please stop this...
I-I will t-tell you e-everything!!"
He begged.
Of course, Neremoth did not listen.
He slowly brought the beetle close to Nux, and in his fear, Nux moved back.
"N-NO!
I-I will tell you everything!
Please!!
Spare me!!!
I BEG YOU!!!"
He screamed, his entire body trembling in endless, primordial fear that seemed like it was now etched into his very soul.
His golden eyes stared at the thumb-sized beetle as if it was the scariest thing in the world.
Even the thought of it getting close to him shook him to his very core.
Yes, Neremoth had succeeded.
He had broken the Anomaly.
Or at least...
That was what the Anomaly wanted him to believe.
But...
Suddenly, Neremoth noticed something.
"...I deprived you of your movement.
How did you move...?"
He questioned in a doubtful voice, his eyes narrowing ever so slightly.
Nux froze.
Neremoth’s questions, however, did not end here.
"You shouldn’t be able to see anything but my eyes in my Domain...
How are you staring right at the beetle?
How do you know where it is...?"
He asked another question and—
"Ah, shit."
Nux cursed out loud, his trembling body returning to normal as if everything before was just an act.

chapters.title: Chapter 2099: A-An Infinity!!
paragraphs: "You shouldn’t be able to see anything but my eyes in my domain...
How are you staring right at the beetle?
How do you know where it is...?"
Neremoth questioned as he narrowed his eyes and Nux...
He froze.
Then—
"Ah shit."
He cursed out loud, his trembling body returning to normal as if everything before was just an act.
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over the place.
"...It was all an act."
Neremoth muttered, his tone much, much heavier than before.
Nux looked into his eyes. He remained silent for a while, then—
"Ahhhh. I beg you. Please leave me?"
He spoke in an almost dead tone.
As if he was trying to take one chance, but since he knew it wasn’t going to work, he was no longer putting in the effort.
And just as he expected, Neremoth’s body twitched in annoyance.
Clearly, he was not buying his act, and as if to prove that, his claws extended.
Nullfang, an ability to cut the very concept of defense, an attack that would tear Nux’s body into two pieces.
Neremoth pounced on Nux, but...
Nux had already moved away.
"Tsk."
Of course, this didn’t mean Nux was satisfied with the outcome.
He looked behind, his eyes easily piercing through the curtain of darkness and stared at the new Balance of Energy he had created—or more accurately, was in the middle of creating.
One more minute...
That was all he needed to assimilate the Laws he absorbed into his Universe and form a new balance, completing his Universe.
Yes, that was what he was doing all this while. Because he was ’trapped’ inside Neremoth’s Domain, giving him all the ’control,’ it allowed Nux to focus on everything he absorbed.

He was invincible in his Universe anyways. Even if he actually died, he could easily be reborn without any conditions. It was an ability similar but far better than Neremoth’s Hollow Rebirth. After all, unlike a mere racial ability, this came from a complete Law.
Anyways, the plan was to keep Neremoth occupied. Because of the Darkness Born’s memories, Nux knew of Neremoth’s sadistic personality. If he gave him ’control,’ Nux knew he would try to play around.
All Nux needed to do was scream every now and then while he moved all his focus into assimilating the Laws and completing the Universe.
And the plan was working well...
But...
Because most of Nux’s focus was on his Universe, he acted a little too much and moved when he shouldn’t have.
"Tsk, this is what happens when you aim for perfection.
My acting was so good that I even forgot that I shouldn’t be moving."
He sighed as he shook his head in disappointment.
Soon, however, a question popped up in his mind.
"Wait, if I forgot the restrictions I had, does this make me a bad actor?"
He wondered, but once again, he shook his head.
"Nah, that makes no sense.
The restrictions were just too dumb to make sense.
How could I be wrong?"
Since it was a convincing argument, Nux nodded to himself, easing all the doubts he had in his mind.
Of course, while he was doing all this, he was constantly dodging Neremoth’s ’Claws of Nothingness’ like they truly were nothing.
And Neremoth...
"How...
HOW!?"
He was losing his mind.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
He moved his claw again and again, using all his speed and might to try and catch Nux.
But nothing worked.
Nux’s reflexes were simply out of Neremoth’s league. In a place where he could move with his Will alone, just a thought was more than enough for him to avoid all of Neremoth’s attacks.
And Neremoth...
"HOW ARE YOU MOVING!?
YOU SHOULDN’T BE ABLE TO MOVE!!
I TOOK YOUR MOVEMENT!!
I TOOK YOUR POWERS!!
IT IS THE LAW OF THE UNIVERSE THAT YOU SHOULD HAVE BEEN DEFEATED BY ME!!"
He couldn’t believe what was happening.
Nux shouldn’t even be able to see him, let alone dodge his attacks—nothing made sense!
Neremoth could feel it.
He was losing.
What’s worse?
He was losing to a Primordial!
"AAAAGGGGGHHHHHH!!!"
He screamed in rage.
WHOOOSH
Oblivion Ray, a beam of condensed despair that consumes energy, hope, and willpower—those struck with it feel their bodies crumbling before the ray physically reaches them.
BOOOOM
Dreadwake Pulse, a black shockwave released from Neremoth’s chest, slows down time for enemies caught inside while making their thoughts echo endlessly, leading to emotional paralysis.
The Eternal from the Supreme World of Darkness used every single attacking ability he had to hurt, but...
It was already too late.

Nux now knew everything there was to know about the Trueborns of Darkness. He knew how their abilities worked, he knew how to avoid them, he even knew the tactics these Trueborns normally use and are taught.
He knew it all.
What’s worse was that Neremoth’s Law wasn’t helping him either.
Usually, Trueborns of Darkness use their Laws to differentiate themselves from each other. Their Laws give them powers different from that of their racial abilities.
But...
Neremoth’s Law of Absolute Eclipse simply strengthened his racial abilities, making them much more efficient than normal.

It was an efficient method. Instead of coming up with something new, he decided to improve what was already considered perfect. When he first formed and displayed his Law, it caused so much stir that his Law was actually studied by other Trueborns.
The knowledge of his Law was added to their basic education that has constantly been improving for trillions of years.
It was said even Lord Infinity looked into it.
It was Neremoth’s greatest honor, something he flaunts to this day, but...
Today, his prided Law became a weakness.

After all, because of the power of his Law being such common knowledge in the Supreme World of Darkness, the Darkness Trueborns Nux had devoured knew about it as well, giving Nux all the information he needed to come up with a perfect way to counter Neremoth.
Every ability he used, no matter how enhanced, was still the same racial ability at its core, making it possible for Nux to dodge them without many difficulties.
"Haaahh..."
Nux sighed.
Since he once again had to focus on the fight, the time he needed to complete his Universe rose up again.
It was something Nux couldn’t afford. After all, Sharnoth was still outside—he needed to help her, and he needed to do it as fast as possible.
He needed to do something that would allow him to spend more of his focus on his Universe and less on the mad dog in front of him.
And the best way to do it?
Well, for now, Nux decided on the talk no jutsu.
Of course, this was his own version of talk no jutsu. Instead of trying to emotionally connect with the enemy, he insulted them.
"You are a fool."
He began, and in an instant, it worked.
Neremoth paused, dumbfounded.
"Law of the Universe? Did you forget who you were up against?"
He questioned, and Neremoth’s expression changed.
He slowly realized it.
The Anomaly...
He was up against the very existence that enraged the Universe so many times that it had become a common occurrence now.
"I am the being who breaks the so-called Law of the Universe as easily as breathing.
What made you think it would be different this time? Especially when you followed me here?"
Nux questioned as suddenly, he waved his hand and...
CRACK
Neremoth’s domain of Darkness cracked.
His eyes widened in surprise, unable to believe what just happened.
CRACK
The crack began to widen, giving birth to more and more cracks as time progressed, and soon—
BOOOM
Neremoth’s domain was crushed out of existence.
"W-Wha..."
He stood frozen, unable to even speak.
Nux, however, just grinned, as if mocking his opponent.
"W-Where is this place...?"
Neremoth questioned.
It was the same question he had been asking all this while, but this time, Nux decided to answer.
"It is my Domain."
"Y-Your Domain...?"
"A place where I am absolute.
A place where all Laws belong to me.
A place where no other domain is effective.
A place where I am at my strongest."
Nux’s voice echoed throughout the universe, coming from all sides.
"H-How can a Primordial have a Domain...?"
Neremoth questioned, and at those words, a small smile appeared on Nux’s face,
"Do you... still believe I am a Primordial?"
"W-What...?"
Neremoth’s eyes widened, and soon, he realized it.
It all made sense now...
This being...
H-He...
He was never a Primordial...
He...
"T-Then what are you...?"
Neremoth questioned carefully.
"A being who has a Domain that is an entirely different world on its own.
What do you think I am?"
Nux questioned with a laugh, and Neremoth’s eyes widened in disbelief and horror.
"A-A d-different w-world...?"
He stuttered.

Nux then pointed at Umbrasol, the very center of his Universe, and when Neremoth turned towards it, he saw hundreds of thousands of dark entities living inside that world, and he froze in absolute horror.
A-A Domain that is a Separate World...
A-An Infinity!!
The Eternal from the Supreme World of Darkness felt his entire world falling apart—a complete mental breakdown,
And while he stood frozen, looking back at the foolishness of trying to go against an Infinity...
Nux focused on his Universe, and finally—
BOOOOOOOM
An explosion of light was heard. Nux’s dark, colorless Universe finally gained color.
The new, complete Balance was set—all Ten Primordial Energies forming a perfect, balanced environment, an environment where ’Life’ can be born, live, die, and reincarnate.
Yes, after an absurdly long journey,
Nux’s Universe was now complete.

chapters.title: Chapter 2100: A Law that should not exist.
paragraphs: BOOOOOOOM
A powerful shockwave rippled through the empty space—the explosion did not have any sound, there was no fire, no blast, nothing, yet...
It was louder and brighter than anything any being had ever witnessed before.
The dark, lifeless, and still Universe began to change.
With the Assimilation, the Light and Darkness finally formed the perfect Balance. The dark Universe began to see ’color’ for the first time.
The soft, gentle light came like sunlight, but soon, it grew stronger, brighter, deeper. Soon, the color expanded.
Blues, golds, greens, and reds flowed into the space. What saw the biggest change was Umbrasol, the center of Nux’s Universe.
A wave of color spread across the land.
The mountains turned deep stone gray, then shifted to warm brown and silver, with green moss blooming along their peaks.
Rivers lit up with shining blues, flowing clear as crystal, as if they had always been moving but only now remembered how to shine.
Forests turned from ash-colored shadows to bright hues of green and gold, their leaves fluttering for the first time.
The skies gained a gradient of deep purples and soft oranges, stars glowing with warmth instead of cold light.
Umbrasol no longer looked like the dark world it was—it looked brighter than ever, even more than when Nux devoured it. The once-called World of Dead felt more alive than anything in the Universe.
Even the space between things changed—shifting from cold emptiness to something that felt alive, something balanced.
The Ten Primordial Energies had settled.

Light and Darkness flowed side by side. Creation and Destruction pulsed together. Life and Death circled each other in quiet agreement. Time and Space held everything in place, even Chaos and Balance formed a perfect harmony.
Nux’s Universe was no longer just a structure.
It was now a complete Universe—ready to grow.
Ready tobegin.
Then...
In the calm of a quiet lake, on a small, floating island,
A tiny spark formed.
It was small.
Simple.
And barely visible.
Yes, the first speck of life.
The first cell.
It pulsed once... then twice...
And then it moved.
The first lifeform of Nux’s Universe had been born.
The beginning of everything had finally arrived.
And during all this change...
BOOOOOOM
Nux, who was still smirking at Neremoth, keeping up the act, suddenly felt a deep pulse ringing out—not from the Universe, but from himself.
From within.
His body shook, even his enhanced mind trembled as a pure, raw Power surged through every corner of his being.
"What is this...?"
He muttered as he sensed all this power.

Nux wasn’t a fool. He had finally gathered all Ten Primordial Energies, so obviously he was expecting big changes after this. He knew even breaking through to the Transcendent Stage wouldn’t be surprising.
But...
This wasn’t it.
He could feel it—something inside him was breaking open, he was breaking through.
But... it was something different.
It was something he had never felt or experienced before.

Nux had devoured worlds. He had set up a cultivation bridge up to the Eternal Level, so he knew everything there was to know about the Transcendent Stage. He had devoured hundreds of Transcendents, so he even knew what it felt like. He knew how the body shifted, he knew how one’s soul expanded, how the Law changed,
But this...
This was different.
It was greater, far, far greater.
A storm of golden-black energy surrounded him as his form began hovering in the air without him doing anything.
It... felt like an Evolution.
A Step beyond what was known.
Nux clenched his fists. A simple action such as this made the sky shimmer. His Universe pulsed with an extremely pure energy.
"Transcendent Stage huh..."
He muttered as he closed his eyes and sensed the changes inside him.
The cultivation bridge that everyone followed—Beginner to Divine, Divine to Primordial, the Transcendent and then Eternal—it was created by the Main Universe.
A stable, linear, and predictable path.
But
But his own path was now diverging.
Of course, as a Universe, his Path had always been different, but they were still in line, even similar in some cases, but now...
It was no longer similar.
It was something else entirely.
The gap between his way and the common path had widened so far... they no longer looked like the same road at all.
As if the moment his Universe was completed, the final thread tying him to the old cultivation system had been cut forever.
Then it happened.
His body, that was releasing this pure, gentle yet threatening energy, suddenly stopped. In an instant, the changing Universe came to a halt as well.

Neremoth, who came out of his reverie, felt like this was a chance. He pounced toward Nux, but Nux simply waved his hand and willed his existence far from him. The Space around Neremoth formed a loop, making it impossible for him to leave that region.
Yes, just like that, one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe was jailed with no way of getting out.
Could Nux have done it sooner?

Of course, he had complete control over this place. He could have done it sooner, but for it to be possible, he needed to constantly alter the Space Laws to make sure he didn’t escape. It was far more taxing than talking to him, punching him, or being tortured and shouting whenever needed.
After dealing with the momentary distraction, Nux focused back on his own body again and the changes happening inside it.
It felt as if his very being was changing, and of course, all this change was being reflected inside Nux’s Universe.
Far above Umbrasol and all other entities, something was born.
A Star.

A Star different from the worlds Nux had assigned to act as a star. It was a Star with a far more powerful Aura than anything present in his Universe, and as the Star grew bigger and more overwhelming,
Nux sensed his connection to it.
A Law.
A new, entirely different Law—something outside of the known system.
A Law that belonged to Nux and Nux alone.

Yes, Nux had finally formed his own, original Law. A Law he couldn’t put into words. A Law that made no sense. A Law that was the amalgamation of all of his experiences thus far. A Law that would continue to grow with him till Eternity.
A Law that truly represented him.
A Law that should not exist.
A Law that goes against everything that was, is, and will be.
It was the rejection of everything that was ’known.’
Order, Structure, Framework—it went against all. It went against even the newest concepts and the concepts that had existed for eons.
Where other Laws follow fixed patterns—bound by balance, cycles, and principles—this Law existed outside the rules entirely, just like Nux.
It cannot be predicted.
It cannot be replicated.
It cannot be suppressed.
This Law destabilizes reality itself. It corrodes everything there is—weakening Domains, bending Space, warping Time, and breaking cause-and-effect—all of it happens merely because of its existence.
It was not a Law of destruction or creation.
It was the Law ofException.
A Paradox.
An Exception made manifest.
A Law that grew stronger the more "impossible" Nux became—feeding on contradiction, thriving on imbalance, and evolving each time the very Universe failed to define him.
It was... the antithesis of control.
A threat not just to enemies...
But to reality itself.
And Nux, whose mind was loaded with all the information about his new Law and everything it could do, came up with a suitable name for it.
"The Law of Anomaly."
He spoke with a confident smirk.
He believed that his Law no longer needed the nametag of being ’Absolute.’ His Law was already above that.
Flicker
The Star that represented his newly formed Law hummed, as if accepting its name.
Nux called it theStar of Anomaly.
As the Star of Anomaly stabilized, the energies roaming wildly inside Nux’s body and the entirety of the Universe came to a still, calm halt as well.
Nux’s cultivation had stabilized.
Finally, he was now a Transcendent—if he could even be called that.
With a smile, his gaze passed through what was hidden and fell on his wives. His body moved, appearing out of thin air without even altering the Space around him.

His wives were already surprised by what happened around them, staring at a certain woman with shocked looks on their faces. When Nux appeared, they glanced at him and sensed the changes inside his body.
"It is good to see you all in color."
Nux chuckled lightly.
The wives laughed.
"We finally did it, huh..."
Amaya muttered.
"Indeed."
Nux nodded.

Of course, there was still a lot he wanted to do, this wasn’t yet over. Therefore, he glanced at another woman. The woman who had attracted his wives’ attention before him—the woman who... had turned into an entirely different entity.
"Shadow."
He called out, and an incredibly beautiful woman stepped forward.
"So this is my new body, eh?
Acceptable."
The woman chuckled.

sentences.text: BOOOOOOOM
A powerful shockwave rippled through the empty space—the explosion did not have any sound, there was no fire, no blast, nothing, yet...
It was louder and brighter than anything any being had ever witnessed before.
The dark, lifeless, and still Universe began to change.
With the Assimilation, the Light and Darkness finally formed the perfect Balance.
The dark Universe began to see ’color’ for the first time.
The soft, gentle light came like sunlight, but soon, it grew stronger, brighter, deeper.
Soon, the color expanded.
Blues, golds, greens, and reds flowed into the space.
What saw the biggest change was Umbrasol, the center of Nux’s Universe.
A wave of color spread across the land.
The mountains turned deep stone gray, then shifted to warm brown and silver, with green moss blooming along their peaks.
Rivers lit up with shining blues, flowing clear as crystal, as if they had always been moving but only now remembered how to shine.
Forests turned from ash-colored shadows to bright hues of green and gold, their leaves fluttering for the first time.
The skies gained a gradient of deep purples and soft oranges, stars glowing with warmth instead of cold light.
Umbrasol no longer looked like the dark world it was—it looked brighter than ever, even more than when Nux devoured it.
The once-called World of Dead felt more alive than anything in the Universe.
Even the space between things changed—shifting from cold emptiness to something that felt alive, something balanced.
The Ten Primordial Energies had settled.
Light and Darkness flowed side by side.
Creation and Destruction pulsed together.
Life and Death circled each other in quiet agreement.
Time and Space held everything in place, even Chaos and Balance formed a perfect harmony.
Nux’s Universe was no longer just a structure.
It was now a complete Universe—ready to grow.
Ready tobegin.
Then...
In the calm of a quiet lake, on a small, floating island,
A tiny spark formed.
It was small.
Simple.
And barely visible.
Yes, the first speck of life.
The first cell.
It pulsed once... then twice...
And then it moved.
The first lifeform of Nux’s Universe had been born.
The beginning of everything had finally arrived.
And during all this change...
BOOOOOOM
Nux, who was still smirking at Neremoth, keeping up the act, suddenly felt a deep pulse ringing out—not from the Universe, but from himself.
From within.
His body shook, even his enhanced mind trembled as a pure, raw Power surged through every corner of his being.
"What is this...?"
He muttered as he sensed all this power.
Nux wasn’t a fool.
He had finally gathered all Ten Primordial Energies, so obviously he was expecting big changes after this.
He knew even breaking through to the Transcendent Stage wouldn’t be surprising.
But...
This wasn’t it.
He could feel it—something inside him was breaking open, he was breaking through.
But... it was something different.
It was something he had never felt or experienced before.
Nux had devoured worlds.
He had set up a cultivation bridge up to the Eternal Level, so he knew everything there was to know about the Transcendent Stage.
He had devoured hundreds of Transcendents, so he even knew what it felt like.
He knew how the body shifted, he knew how one’s soul expanded, how the Law changed,
But this...
This was different.
It was greater, far, far greater.
A storm of golden-black energy surrounded him as his form began hovering in the air without him doing anything.
It... felt like an Evolution.
A Step beyond what was known.
Nux clenched his fists.
A simple action such as this made the sky shimmer.
His Universe pulsed with an extremely pure energy.
"Transcendent Stage huh..."
He muttered as he closed his eyes and sensed the changes inside him.
The cultivation bridge that everyone followed—Beginner to Divine, Divine to Primordial, the Transcendent and then Eternal—it was created by the Main Universe.
A stable, linear, and predictable path.
But
But his own path was now diverging.
Of course, as a Universe, his Path had always been different, but they were still in line, even similar in some cases, but now...
It was no longer similar.
It was something else entirely.
The gap between his way and the common path had widened so far... they no longer looked like the same road at all.
As if the moment his Universe was completed, the final thread tying him to the old cultivation system had been cut forever.
Then it happened.
His body, that was releasing this pure, gentle yet threatening energy, suddenly stopped.
In an instant, the changing Universe came to a halt as well.
Neremoth, who came out of his reverie, felt like this was a chance.
He pounced toward Nux, but Nux simply waved his hand and willed his existence far from him.
The Space around Neremoth formed a loop, making it impossible for him to leave that region.
Yes, just like that, one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe was jailed with no way of getting out.
Could Nux have done it sooner?
Of course, he had complete control over this place.
He could have done it sooner, but for it to be possible, he needed to constantly alter the Space Laws to make sure he didn’t escape.
It was far more taxing than talking to him, punching him, or being tortured and shouting whenever needed.
After dealing with the momentary distraction, Nux focused back on his own body again and the changes happening inside it.
It felt as if his very being was changing, and of course, all this change was being reflected inside Nux’s Universe.
